reviews.text: Had a suite a the palms place for 4 nights. When we got there the room and bathroom were not clean. We checked in well after check in hours. Took them two møre hours to clean iT and iT still wasnt done very well. The room iT self is Nice But you can tell iT is used as a party hotel. There were shoe prints on the ceiling and most of the handels and Doors were damaged. The bed was very Nice and big and so was the view. During the nights iT was very noisy in the halls from people running around and slamming Doors. Check out was terrible. Very unfriendly woman at the counter.

reviews.title: Not a care for the patrons
reviews.text: We were upgraded to the suites in Palm Place. While nice and modern five years ago they were dated and showing wear. The reason for the upgrade was due to us paying a resort fee but with no access to the large pool. They moved us so we could be close to the only other pool on property. Resort fee aside, One of our friends staying in another room had to call front desk about the safe being ripped out of the wall and another about a used condom in a drawer. Imagine that.Back to the suites, our group had 4 of them and we all made a game of finding imprints on the glass of other patrons fruitful endeavors. Cheek marks, face and hand imprints painted a sordid picture. We expect this in Vegas so we can let this go. On our second day, at the pool my wife stepped on glass. Upon telling the bar tender there was a flurry of commotion to get the issue to the manager and security. However, No one checked on my wife, including life guards. It took about 30 minutes to get a bandage from the manager. Whom told us he would have security follow up. To no avail. We did not hear from anyone about the incident.When we returned on the 3rd day, I carefully checked for glass and guess what....I found another piece. This was after their thorough scoping and pool closure from the day before. These pieces were curved and about 3 inches long, fortunately my wife reacted quickly when she felt it. This could have been a quick trip to the hospital. Our bartender was also less than a peach with gratuity included on the pool side service. Maybe they were disappointed about the pool closure the day prior.I’m not sure what the life guards do here. They definitely do not check the pool with any sort of diligence. Maybe place that attitude on the responsible party for the previous days closure and not paying patrons. Personally, while the place was nice and suites were still above average I’m not planning on another visit. They did not really seem to care about us or the experience and certainly did not offer to make any amends.

reviews.title: SMOKING WEED ALLOWED
reviews.text: WARNING! WARNING! WARNING! WARNING! WARNING! WARNING! WARNING!If we have known we would not have stayed at the Palms Place.  Worst night ever, our adjacent room neighbor was smoking marijuana, and the smell was entering our room.The smell of marijuana was making my wife and myself sick.  We made a phone called and informed the front desk and nothing was done.  After waiting for 15 minutes for a response and putting a towel underneath the doorway.  This did not help with the smell of marijuana entering our room.  We had to quickly pack and go to the lobby.  While we were in the lobby, there was no security at the entrance to the elevator.  My wife was so upset, when she saw the front desk manager Sharee Hall, my wife approached Sharee. My wife explained to Sharee of the smell of marijuana.  Sharee said that smoking weed was allowed.  When we heard that smoking marijuana was allowed, we demanded a full refund, and we left the hotel.  WE WILL NEVER STAY HERE AGAIN.

reviews.title: Excellent and Professional Staff
reviews.text: From valet parking to check-in to waiters and waitresses in the numerous restaurants and the staff at the Pearl showroom, all were as courteous and professional as possible. Even the housekeepers were professional and gracious. The room was large, comfortable and an excellent sized bathroom as well.

reviews.title: 33rd Floor
reviews.text: We stayed in a private owner suite and it needed some work and attention.  Biggest negative was that we could hear the party at KAOS (Palms pool) both day and all three nights.  I would not choose a strip view in the future.We enjoyed being off the strip and loved the pool and restaurants.  Everyone working there was kind and friendly!

reviews.title: Not a fan.
reviews.text: Booked two rooms for myself and an employee who was traveling with me for the MAGIC trade show. My husband arrived before us and got us checked in to both rooms. There is a $22 charge a night if you request a high floor, however guests aren't permitted to access the balconies so it was kind of a bust. The t.v. in our room did not work when my husband got there nor did the t.v. in my employee's room work. The comforter on our bed was dirty.. housekeeping never replenished toilet paper... and check out was the worst. One person working the front desk at 11am which is the check out time. Overall, I would say it was just an o.k. experience at an o.k place.

reviews.title: Dirty, dusty, Nasty
reviews.text: Housekeeping is awful. After checking in we walked into our suite with someone still in it, claiming to be doing final housekeeping inspection. She left once we walked in. The suite was filthy. The furniture was torn. The room smelled disgusting from an old, dirty shower drain. Housekeeping came back when we called to owner to complain. This was booked through Air Bnb for full disclosure. Don’t go through owners Tony & Beth. They showed no care. They definitely have the Palms personnel care for their property and use their housekeeping services. We showed them how nasty everything was. The floor had not been mopped or vacuumed. The cleaning lady literally took a rag and wet it with just water to “clean” the floor. Needless to say, we couldn’t stay. It was beyond gross. We checked out and went to the strip. Awful experience.

reviews.title: unwind here after a long flight before going to the strip
reviews.text: we got one bed suite witch was stunning .so relaxing room had everything like washer dryier massive fridge freezer look up videos of this place like I did and that's what you get I will be back.......

reviews.title: Palms Place - A great venue!
reviews.text: I stayed at the Palms Place Hotel on August 3rd and 4th.  The room was upgraded to the 38th floor.  The view was incredible and the customer experience was excellent.  The Palms Place Pool was also a relaxing and comfortable experience.  This is one of the better hotels in Las Vegas. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: I really enjoy staying at Palms Place
reviews.text: I stayed here on a Wednesday - Friday.  It was not very busy, service was alright, the bell service was outstanding and very helpful.  The rooms all have TWO large TVs on the wall which is great for sports.  The pool is small but, very nice.  Great bar and you have to check out Drift Spa.  The do charge for EVERYTHING here so, becareful what you touch in the mini bar.  I will do a review on drift spa as well.

reviews.title: No from me.
reviews.text: Stayed here for 4 nights in july 20-25.  Almost 1k for a balcony suite.   The balcony was LOCKED, and i was informed by staff it wouldnt be opened for me. Downstairs, at the bar, the bartenders were extremely rude & un-wecoming. Made me feel like i was a hassle to them. I asked for a cup of water and they said "$6", i said id just like some sink tap 2ater in a cup and she said NO. I couldnt believe it.   1 vodka tonic cost me $14 + tip. There was a hidden resort fee of almost $50/day, even tho i didnt use ANY amenities.  They say it covers access to the pool,  wifi, free shuttle service (never saw that one),  a newspaper daily. I didnt get or use 1 of those things. Total rip off imo. Theres nothing to do too,  and its way off the strip, need to taxi everywhere! Not staying here aggain, the room was nice tho, big turkish baths. Front desk during check in was nice too.

reviews.title: Terrible inside and out
reviews.text: My husband and I booked room 319 from Expedia not knowing it was through a private owner. The only reason I gave it a one star is because the view was ok.. 10th floor. Upon arrival the front desk was rude and looked as if we were bothering them. Once inside the room was so dirty, chocolate chips left on the floor, windows were not cleaned , why have a balcony if there is no seating and filthy , gum on the floor just bad housekeeping. Broken furniture and lamps. Stained bedding.. Bathroom tub had mold didn’t even try to take a bath . We left and no one cleaned for 2 days. We booked 3 nights only stayed for 2.  Never again !!! Staff rude, room dirty, and expensive for what you get. Not worth your money look elsewhere

reviews.title: Not a "condo" Experience
reviews.text: After a tireless search for my housing during a summer work trip I settled on Palms Place.  KITCHEN:I did this primarily for the Kitchen space.  However I was extremely disappointed when I arrived and there was nothing in the kitchen.  NOTHING.  I called room service that brought me a setup which was -1plate-1cup-1 silverware set-1pot-1pan-1 large plastic spoonI had ordered grocery delivery the next day, and of course I Needed to make a 2nd order to get some knives, a cutting board, a can opener, a coffee maker, etc.  Well I had just accepted this but when my first grocery delivery arrived and I asked the bell man if I could use a cart to take my things up he informed me it would cost -$10 fee to use the cart because they were groceries. HUH? So not only did I have to pay the fee for the grocery delivery, I also had to pay a fee once they got delivered and I still tipped the bell man.  I figured it wasn't his fault Palms had a weird policy.  The worst was because I had to do this twice.  THE ROOM: -Blowdryer didn't work -Only 1/3 Televisions worked -Only one Phone worked ***The patio door is locked!  I called to get it opened and they said it is locked for safety?  When my friend had an AirBNB last year they said they were able to have theirs opened but if you book through the hotel you can not?  But that is just speculation.  It was definitely a waste of space.  -The room itself was nice and had a cool view. -Although I was really worried about noise due to the party atmosphere I was only awakened twice on my stay to drunk people screaming and talkingHOTEL: -LOTS of WASTED people, the elevators are a total show-Gym is great-Pool is small and had Super loud music.  I was definitely hoping it would be more low key and all the party people would go to the actual Palms, but it wasn't the worst.  I went once. SERVICE: -when two girlfriends came over for breakfast I called room service and they brought over 2 more set ups right away. -Housekeeping was hit or miss.  I started calling down every day when I left of there were several days when no one came even though I turned my "please service" light on.  Then there were other days I pushed nothing and someone did come and clean.  SO, just to be safe I started calling.  When I did this the service was usually good. Will I stay here again next year, No.  Found an Airbnb for the last part of my stay that was way cheaper and overall felt like much better value.

reviews.title: Meh
reviews.text: The good: The studio we rented through Airbnb was clean and comfortable. It was on the 20th floor. We had rented a car and there is free valet in self parking. It’s not on the strip but close enough to not be a big deal. The strip is not exactly walkable anyway.The bad: I came to Vegas to sit by a pool.  I realize I need to change my expectations of the pools in Las Vegas and accept that they are simply another moneymaking opportunity, and not an amenity provided for hotel guests. the music at this was horrible. And seems to be targeted to 18-year-olds people who were not at this pool... wtf.  And because it was incredibly windy, they took down many of the umbrellas. The only shade available were in all of the empty cabanas. Available to rent for $150...Lobby very crowded :(

reviews.title: Noisey and poor value
reviews.text: During the period 12 June to 06 July 2019 (23 nights), we visited several west USA National Parks and stayed in 17 different hotels/motels. This provided a unique opportunity to compare and review these establishments.We stayed for 2 nights, 04 & 05 July 2019, room 10318 (10th floor), and paid GBP98.99 plus USD44.22 resort fee, per night.The room was a suite with 1 king size bed, see photos.The main complaint was that loud music originating from the poolside, 4 floors below, could be heard in the room from 0900 to 1900 everyday. Despite requests to customer services, nothing was done to minimise the sound levels.Whilst most facilities and amenities were provided, the basic room layout/design was poor because:•	Glass partition wall between bathroom and bedroom means light in bathroom can be seen at night.•	Common glass door to shower and bath•	No towel rail near to washbasin (one could have been easily added under the washbasin counter)•	Poor location of towel storage rack over WC.In addition, the following were found to be missing:•	No shower gel provided•	No ice machines on each floor although in-room directory states otherwise. Front desk claim that as they provided refrigerators, ice machines were not. Ridiculous excuse!•	No USB charging points•	iPod/radio clock not working•	Damaged furniture (see photo)

reviews.title: Missed opportunity
reviews.text: After I had the privilege of aiding save the life of a fellow guest at the Laguna restaurant, I was promptly presented with my bill. I guess they were kind enough to comp my coffee, since it got cold while I was on the floor helping to revive the young man during his massive seizure. My breakfast got cold too, but who really cares. It took a long while for paramedics to arrive on the scene, I was glad to be there. Anyway, not even a proper thank you from management. I guess this is the sign of times in this new era. I was happy to check out earlier, and  comped them my room for the second night. Beds are comfortable, very pleasant suite with sound proof sliding doors to help block the blasting music by the pool.

reviews.title: FALSE ADVERTISING
reviews.text:
I booked a 2 bedroom suite through VRBO.com for the Palms Hotel and Spa for a 3-night stay. Through a private owner. I paid $1,000.00 to be notified 24hrs before my arrival that they were double booked and canceled my reservation. I had to re-rent another suite through VRBO for the same hotel for $1400.00 for the same 3 night. This time the owner of the suite was the hotel. What hasn't what upset me the was that I now had to pay an additional $400.00. Why would that upset me :/ why would that upset anyone? :? What made it worse was that they weren't giving me the 2 bedroom suite. But they advertise a 2 bedroom suite by pictures and description. Not only am I paying more I'm getting less. But wait you don't know that until they send you an email of your purchase and send you the right picture of your room, The picture on VRBO shows a 2 bedroom suite. IT"S FALSE ADVERTISING!!!! PERIOD!!! VRBO has the nerve to tell me that it wasn't them that its the hotel "the hotel can put any pictures of the room" that they want. NO, THEY CANNOT!!!! The description clearly states a separate bedrooms separate seating area.!!! How can they get away with this?The hotel states they can not make any changes to the reservation without VRBO know. That VRBO is the one that has to make the changes to make sure I get the room I'm paying for. And VRBO WON'T. They keep telling to call the Palms the Palms tells me to call VRBO this went on for a while I called the hotel 3 times on this matter and no one would help. I called VRBO 3 times and no one would help. Well, I made one more final call to the hotel to reservations I tired book a new reservation for the room I wanted to my surprise they didn't have anymore 1 bedroom suite available. There's the scam they charge you 1 bedroom suite prices and give you a regular room cause they overbooked!! SO PLEASE PLEASE DO NOT BOOK THROUGH VRBO!!!!!1 King Bed and 1 Queen Sofa Bed581-sq-foot (54-sq-meter) room with valley views
Layout - Separate sitting area

reviews.title: Great value near the strip
reviews.text: I had a great experience at Palms Place during my recent three night stay. I think it's important to set your expectations that this isn't an ultra luxe hotel such as the Wynn. However, it's an excellent choice for travelers on a budget who are seeking a better than average room with all the frills of an on strip casino but without the price tag.Pros: 1. Free parking 2. Free WiFi 3. Very large rooms with kitchenette. One bedrooms have washer dryer and balconies.4. Beautiful views from all rooms.5. Amazing pool on casino side, but it's a long walk. The palms place pool is mediocre.Cons:1. Cleanliness. Both the lobby and my room needed attention. There were food spills on the fridge, counters needed wiping and the windows were very dirty. That said, housekeeping was amazing when I raised the issue about my room. They came immediately to clean, apologized and offered me a new room. 2. The pool is pretty lame. It's smallish, music is obnoxiously loud and generally uninviting. Walk to the casino pool for a much nicer experience. It's included in your stay.3. Lack of kitchenware. I ordered Uber Eats on two evenings. The kitchen doesn't have anything at all except two glasses and two mugs. No plates, silverware, nada.Again, my three night stay ran me just over $300 including the daily resort fee. I feel I got far more a value! It's not the Mandarin Oriental but it was definitely worth the price. I booked through priceline so not through an independent owner.

reviews.title: Terrible customer service from front desk
reviews.text: The hotel is just okay, the staff is not.  They are so rude at the front desk and not accommodating.   I have stayed at many hotels in Las Vegas of all different star levels and have never been treated so rudely.

reviews.title: Elevated Escape
reviews.text: Palms Place is where you go to spoil yourself with a spacious suite. The marble bathrooms and decor are beautiful. However, I noticed the bath tub had a few chips in it, so it's not perfect. I enjoyed the elegance here and all the amenities. As a hotel guest, you can enjoy the fitness center and spa for $25 a day. Super relaxing in there! This is also the perfect place to be if you want to go to Kaos- it's about a 5-10 minute walk to Palms. I also love that they have their own food court so you don't need to go too far to get anything- it's all right there!

reviews.title: Mini Bar/ Rude customer service
reviews.text: I booked a room for my birthday, mini bar fridge wasn’t working. I not once got told upon check in or anytime after that that there would be a cost for the mini bar if anything was taken out of it because I was like well if the fridge doesn’t work & im paying all this money, might as well take advantage. Repair guy came to “fix” the minifridge, said he couldn’t do anything about it because the compressor wasn’t working. Mind you, I had put a whole cake in there earlier which ended up spoiled btw. Checked out next day.. fast forward a few days I check my bank statement and there is a charge of a little over $500 plus the booking of the room. I call the hotel so i can get an explanation as to why there’s two separate charges on there, staff is extremely rude, saying that if im making it up just because its a financial issue that I couldn’t afford it then I shouldn’t have stayed there, so so rude & unprofessional btw! I asked for her name & she hung up on me. Later that day another person reaches out to me, once again very rude & yet no response whatsoever and also i stated that I wanted to talk to a manager/supervisor to which im still waiting for a callback. I’ve been to many hotels & have traveled & I’ve never gotten a charge like this to my account or gotten treated so poorly. I don’t think I’m ever coming back here. Im still waiting for management to reach out because I truly felt like it’s unfair & all they’re doing is ripping people off!

reviews.title: Just Ok!!
reviews.text: Stayed here for 4 nights, you’d do good to read trip advisors warning! Check in was ok BUT beware there is a $40-00 per night extra resort fee on top of your accommodation WHICH was not clear at time of booking and on hind sight if I had known this I would have booked elsewhere as it worked out the same in the end.  I still don’t know what I actually paid for to be honest. One can hardly charges $40-00 resort fee per day just for the use of the pool and WiFi?? Check in staff at the Casino side is pleasant, staff at the Palm Suite side on the contrary is unhelpful and unfriendly. Our room had a balcony, it was locked and when I inquire about a key to open it I was told it’s against rules and we can’t have a key to open it, however, I saw many rooms with their balcony doors open and occupants standing outside. It’s supposedly non smoking rooms, I could not sleep at night as the smell of marijuana was unpleasant and most nights unbearable! Even during the day the smell in the corridors were overwhelming and nauseating!! Rooms are starting to look dated but they are cleaned daily so no concerns there. Use of the pool casino side was limited, they have live entertainment over weekends and it gets so busy you cannot get in - unless you are there when they open. The pool at the Palm Suite building was super crowded and quite small compared to Kaos at the casino. Drinks were super expensive (but to be fair, that’s to be expected). Food is OK, although we hardly dined in the hotel. I can highly recommend the bagel cafe (Einstein Bros) across the road, they open early (06:00) and closes at 16:00 so be sure to get there in time. It’s quite a walk from the strip, there is a lift share (and date I say, might be included in the resort fee??) BUT it doesn’t run in the week so we couldn’t make use of it. You cal UBER, it costs about $13-00. The casino it self is on the quiet side, certainly not as busy as the ones on the Las Vegas Strip. If you fancy catching a movie, book early to ensure you get a good seat (and you beat the rush). I am not sure I’d recommend Palms place to friends and family - i could consider it if they are more open and upfront about the resort fees and if they have better control over the “non smoking” policy - which appears to be non existent at the moment.

reviews.title: New owners still garbage service
reviews.text: I used to stay here back in the day when the maloofs owned the property and it was nice. The condos are well done and very easy access. Understandably the maloofs met some hard times in 2008-09 as well the condo owners. Rooms and service upkeep was not not tenable during the recession. Finally came back after 8-9 years as the Fertitas took over the property. It was clean this time as it was not the last few times but you still get nickel and dimed for something so simple as a cork screw. It is supposed to be a condo but no plates or silverware. I called over to room service for a corkscrew and the women told me I had to pay $5 for it. I justed wanted to use it but ok. Then it shows up and it’s $10 as they added a $5 delivery fee for an item that should have been in the room. Bad business.

reviews.title: April 23-26  2019
reviews.text: This is a condo hotel. (CONDO AT PALMS PLACE )  Don't expect to received a good service like a hotel .They don't have a professional cleaner to clean the room.  .The aircon grill  are dirty, ( I got an allergy ) Lots of molds,dust and rust  in the bathrooms and roomsDark lighting at night, Hotel and room is not accessible. DESPITE MY COMPLAIN , MANAGER RHEA  DID" NOTHING."

reviews.title: Great room ....
reviews.text: Stayed here for a week on honeymoon....room was amazing on 36th floor perfectly cleaned everyday and extremely friendly front desk However so expensive to drink 2 beers were most expensive we found in Vegas $26 for two as they add $4 gratuity on no matter what ! For opening a bottle ! I prefer to pay a tip when I have received a service meant we didn’t spend much time at pool

reviews.title: Great Room
reviews.text: Great room and room service. I really never left the room except to eat at the buffet. I had a suite which was very roomy. Room service prices were comparable to surrounding hotels. Overall, I would definitely stay again!

reviews.title: Awesome place for New Years!
reviews.text: We stayed here for New Years to see the fire works on the strip.  The room was very nicely appointed. Marble was used all over the bathroom with large walk in shower with kind of a weird tub.  There is a single basin in the bathroom but it has plenty of counter space for two people.  The no smoking / no casino feature means no smokey smell on you and your clothes.  That is a real plus.  There are Gaggenau fixtures in the kitchen whcih makes the place feel rally luxe.  Pay extra for high floor strip view.  It is worth it if you can afford it / are going to be in the room.  The rooms have great strip views from a distance.  Make sure you get a room with a balcony that opens.  Not all do.

reviews.title: Best hotel off the strip
reviews.text: Tired to grab a room week ahead and was receiving offers of $199 and up. I finally called Palms after hearing the pool was newly renovated. After speaking with hotel reservations, I received a room for $50 Thursday, Friday, and Saturday. The hotel has been newly renovated and so was their old buffet. Only down side was the resort fees were as much as the cost of the room, but small price to pay for nice hotel (close to the strip). I would recommend this palace anytime.

reviews.title: Very Disappointing
reviews.text: We were really excited for our first trip to Vegas to stay at the Palms Place. Upon arrival we were greeted with a very friendly staff and they quickly checked us in. Upon getting to the room we were very disappointed to find the room very old and dated. Scratch marks all over the walls, dirty floors, dirt between the walls and the bed,Dirty under the sink and inside where they expect you to use ice from. For the price we paid to stay here I feel we could have stayed in a much newer nicer hotel that would have not looked so worn out. The rooms really need a facelift. Also keep in mind that the balcony doors are locked and they won’t give you a key to them, which I find ridiculous! Why did we come to Vegas and book a room on the 50th floor only not to have access to the balcony. Another thing to note, we waited over 2Hours for a wine opener to be brought to our room which cost $10. The garbage disposal stopped working after the first day. Be prepared to bring your own cups and silverware, they onlyProvide you with 2 glasses and no forks or spoons. Overall if you are not used to staying in nicer places then these things might not bother you, but honestly I have stayed in nicer Holiday Inn’s which were cleaner. Be cautious when booking this place and ask lots of questions about the condition of your room. Take a look at my pictures.

reviews.title: Great deals with nice rooms, some details could use more attention though.
reviews.text: This property has amazing rates for what you get. We were in a 1 bedroom, 1 1/2 bath strip view suite, managed by a outside property company - but you check in through the front desk like any other room. We had a kitchen with a four burner glasstop stove, a microwave, a fridge & freezer, and a dishwasher. Our room also included a washer & dryer, fireplace, TWO balconies, a big fold out couch, tons of seating, and wrap around windows. Having a small kitchen and two bathrooms are a lifesaver for a family, but we don't always want to stay at a non-resort/extended stay property, so having these available at a location like Palms Place is fantastic. Our room here was definitely larger, with more upgraded features and finishes, than our room at The Signature (which also offers multi-room suites with kitchens). I'll be exhaustively nitpicky here, for honesty's sake. You should know what you're getting for your money. The sheer size and amenities within the room make it a great value. I couldn't, however, give it a full 5 stars, because there were some details that could use a little attention. The two balconies were great to have, but they had ZERO furniture on them, not even those cheesy white plastic chairs, so it made them a lot less usable. The finishes were upgraded, but some look dated, while others have just suffered their fair share of wear and tear and need replacing or refurbishing. The giant tub was great to have, but a few times the jets randomly turned on by themselves, and it was a bit startling since in an empty tub that's loud, and it was sudden. All three bathroom sinks dripped from the cold water handle when they were on, even if only using the hot water. One of the toilets ran (quietly, but still wasteful) unless you jiggled the handle, the icemaker in the freezer was pretty noisy at times (opening and shutting the freezer door made the sound stop), a few lightbulbs were out, and the bedroom was lacking bedside outlets for charging your devices near you overnight. The two TV's are pretty small by today's standards, especially for this size room, and don't accommodate guests hooking up computers/gaming systems/ etc. very easily, while most hotels and have entered the modern age and make this a simple task with media centers and easily accessible hdmi inputs. The super limited amount of channels and no PPV options also greatly limited their use, as it was hard to find anything anybody wanted to actually watch while we were in the room. The TV system's guide also only showed the networks, not what was playing on them at the time, so by the time you made it through the channels looking to see what was actually on right then and chose something, you had missed at least the first few minutes of it. A guide that showed what was playing and not just what channel was what number would have been nice. Also, the bedroom tv would randomly glitch and black out for a few seconds here and there, and once entirely lost sound for nearly 10 minutes, throughout all channels, before we turned it off, waited a minute or two and turned it back on, which fixed it, but it was annoying when you're in the middle of watching something. On a positive note, the free wifi was plenty to accommodate a family of four, including streaming. I was confused at first because it was made to sound like the basic (free) wifi limited the number of devices that could connect, and offered very low-speed connections. I even upgraded ($9.99/day premium package) to start off with, but once that expired and we tried the basic there was no discernable difference and we were not limited on the amount of devices that could connect (we had 8 connected). It streamed just fine too. I recommend trying the basic first to see if it meets your needs before assuming you need to upgrade. The pool (next door at the Palms, but included for Palms Place guests) left much to be desired, but Mabel's BBQ (also, next door at the Palms) was the best BBQ I've ever eaten. The staff was friendly, the hotel is nicely quiet, no rowdy crowds anywhere, and it doesn't reek of cigarette smoke. Free parking, including free valet (gratuity is obviously up to you, but you SHOULD tip if you use it) is a nice change from the MGM properties that have found yet another way to squeeze an additional $15 a day out of their guests.  Overall I would definitely stay here again, in the same room, and I would also recommend it to others. Just have realistic expectations. It's not perfect, and it's not the best suite on the strip, but hotel rooms are NEVER as shiny and immaculate as they seem in pictures, and it's a hell of a deal for what you get.

reviews.title: Mini bar
reviews.text: Like i said I didn’t take anything inside the mini bar. I bring my own stuff like soda, water, etc. and when I checked out they charged me $59 to my card they claiming i take on their mini bar... when i check out probably the housekeeping thought all the thing on the trash like soda etc are came from the mini bar, like i said im not stupid. I bring my own stuff like that... they are steeling my money...

reviews.title: Multi-Million dollar Penthouse ABSOLUTELY DISGUSTING!!! I have tones of videos and photos!!!
reviews.text: I went to the Palms Place for my Bachelorette party April 30th- May 4th 2019. I rented the penthouse on the 56th floor Room 304 Taking the elevator up to our suite -waking out to the 56th floor, there is significant water damage, and the smell of mold slaps you in the face, my sinus and eyes were bothered pretty bad everything I walked through the hallway.Opening the suite, the chairs were scattered, the set up just didn’t make any sense. The glass table is broken we were too afraid to eat on the table and it collapse! Not to mention the glass itself was cracked, didn’t want to cut our hands and legs up. The furniture is ripped, holes in the pillows, holes in the chairs, there is food on the wall where a BIG picture should be hung up. Cigarette burns in the floor and master bed night stand. The bedroom furniture in both the master bedroom and spare bedroom has banged up bad also in the guest room bathroom the light bulbs on one side were burnt out and there is water damage behind the mirror (pretty sure wall will need replaced- made a video you have to watch it),The wood trimming around the penthouse is either scuffed really bad or there’s entire wooden pieces missing, I stubbed the front of my toes on a loose wood piece with the nail JUST missing my foot. Master bedroom has a broken chair and wooden planks stuffed in the closet, master bathroom- railing on the one side where you hand the towels was broken off! Looking at the ceilings there’s water damage I’m pretty sure the owner is going to have to gut the place out. There was NO hairdryer, actually was a hassle to even get one! 4 girls in this room and no hairdryer??? We tried calling the front desk and they couldn’t be bothered it took us over half hour to get a dryer.The owner threw the hairdryer at my girl friend and gave her a nasty look... awesome. Kitchen doesn’t have any knives so we couldn’t cook anything while we stayed there. The deck- the couch, someone broke it as you’ll see in the picture I post, the condition of the upholstery was stained by white residue, the pool itself the jets didn’t work.EVERYTHING the ceiling, the furniture must go! I am absolutely appalled in the condition of the penthouse of all things?? We asked for a different suite and we were told we couldn’t... I booked this unit months in advance and the service we all got it’s pathetic and quite embarrassing to be totally honest. Shame on the owner of this building!!!** Strip View Suites manages this penthouse, I don’t know how the condition of this place slipped through the cracks??? My bachelorette trip was ruined this penthouse DOES NOT look like what it does in pictures!!!

reviews.title: A quiet oasis
reviews.text: This is my new favorite place to stay in Las Vegas. The pool is relaxing with good people to hang out with. The rooms are huge and we had a view of the mountains in the distance off our balcony which was a pleasant surprise. I can't say many bad things about palms place. Well there's a thick aroma of perfume in the lobby which was a bit aggressive. Self park was close to the door. Kaos night club is a must to check out if you're in to that nightlife vibe. I will definitely be staying at Palms Place on my next visit. Oh dogs are allowed too which is nice.

reviews.title: Great Location and Rooms
reviews.text: We stayed one night at the beginning of our trip then 2 nights at the end of our trip.  Both stays were great.  Our rooms were fantastic.  Our one-night room did have a pungent odor of cigarettes, which was a challenge because all our stuff smelled like smoke after check out.  We stayed in different rooms on each stay and both had wonderful views of the strip.  One complaint, which I do not know if the hotel can control, is the overwhelming smell of marijuana in the hall ways leading to the rooms and the elevator areas.  That, along with the cigarette stench on our 1st night, are the only things that kept me from giving 5 stars.  We will absolutely return to this hotel in the future.

reviews.title: They refused to allow us to check in after we drove 4 hours to get there
reviews.text: I book 5 nights at the Palms Place.  When we got there, the receptionist refused to take my credit card for a security deposit.  He said they do not take Greendot bank cards.  I told him that was the only credit card I had on me.  I have never had a problem using this card before and used it at the Wynn last year with no issues.  He said it had to be a card from a bank other than Greendot or Paypal.  I told him nowhere on the webpage does it say that and there was no mention of that in my booking confirmation email.  The website only says a $100/day security deposit is required, with no specific exclusions on certain credit cards.  I asked if I could pay the $500 in cash instead.  He said no, they don't take cash.  I offered to pay for the entire stay in cash and put down $1000 in cash for the security deposit.  He refused.  A manager was called.  She also refused to allow us to check in.  Another manager was called and he told me the same thing, that he could actually swipe my card and it would go through, but it was against their policy so he couldn't do it.  At this point our vacation was pretty much ruined and I was ready to drive back home.  My wife asked if they could recommend us a hotel that would take our card.  It turns out 90% of hotels in Las Vegas do take my card OR cash, including the Wynn which is now our go-to hotel.

reviews.title: Money scamming
reviews.text: This hotel is a joke. The staff are useless, do not bother booking. Or add an extra 500 dollars onto the price. They charge you for everything including a bottle opener. A hotel of this price shouldn't be charging for a bottle opener I've traveled the world and I've never experienced that. Also, they don't tell you that they charge you for every drink you MOVE AROUND in the fridge. We made room for our items and got charged for items we didn't consume. AMEX is still investigating the situation so hopefully I get my money back but if you paid cash or debit you'd be screwed. We were there with 15 people for a wedding and no one had any idea about the fridge charging their cards. YOU MUST INFORM YOUR CUSTOMERS. money scammers.

reviews.title: Not the best experience
reviews.text: Easy check in for 1 of our rooms but a mess for the other 2 rooms. As British on holiday we book a room and turn up and expect to get a room at reception right? This did not happen. We were not aware the rooms booked had nothing to do with the hotel and had to call the owner of the room!!! He had to meet us at the hotel to take us to the room. A lot of stress but room 2 sorted. Room 3 on the other had was cancelled without notice and it was another private owner room. Our group was stressed at this point. No contact prior to say so. We got told that we would have been contacted via email and phone. We were on holiday and did not have access to email and phones. Now back in the uk emails were checked and answer phone checked and no such emails or calls. Our only option by hotels.com was to stay in a different hotel ( splitting up our family) or pay over $1000 for an available room in the Palms. Welcome to the Palms. We stayed in Palms Place. The rooms we had were clean and spacious and great views of the strip. The staff were great from reception, valet, casino waitresses, bar staff and security. The casino was a good size and a mix of old and new machines. Pleanty of eating spots in the hotel and the A.Y.C.E buffet was great value and good selection. The hotel is a long walk from the strip so a taxi is recommended or the bus to Ceasers Palace. We learned the hard way!!!. We could not use the pool the first day as staff told us  it had broken glass in from a party and needed drained. It was to windy the rest of the stay. The bad start of our stay always played on our minds and our group could not relax properly. We stayed here on the launch weekend of kaos nightclub and saw how badly it was handled. People there will know what i mean. Thank you Hotels.com for ruining our stay.Thank you Palms we will visit again.

reviews.title: Palms Place Penthouse Floor57 Heated Infinity Pool
reviews.text: We booked the Penthouse on the 57th floor w/infinity pool at the Palms Place. On the second night, we phoned the front desk to report a noise disturbance next door and they did nothing.  By 3 am we physically went downstairs to the front desk and reported the disturbance again, since the initial request was ignored.  The rental had no drinking glasses. So, we went to the bar for glasses and provided 8 plastic cups.  We reached out to the property manager twice, who advised they were in the movies and would get some drinking glasses to the unit in 30 minutes. The experience and description was misleading.  For the price, the only thing you are paying for at this property is the view.

reviews.title: STAY AWAY- CAMERAS in Room
reviews.text: Worst place ever, stay suck, 21/2 hour wait to get in room. Girls weekend reserved in 2 bd with pool strip view end up being a one bedroom no pool not facing strip penthouse on 11 floor.. dirty room,staff rude unprofessional and to say a wireless camera facing the sitting tub in room.. no help to solve why it was there or who’s it was and what it recorded.my friend way too nice I wanted to file a police report end result it was booked thru home away from home.. regardless the hotel treats you like outcast that don’t belong.. worst hotel stay ever.STAY AWAY ROOM 11301..I have video but it I can’t load sorry..

reviews.title: Amazing room!
reviews.text: Clean & a great view! Had a blast, and was very impressed with room. Only complaints would be the pool area (pool bar not open yet, this time of year & pool would have been better heated. Wish the ice maker worked, but we made due with convenient store across the street.

reviews.title: Great hotel awesone views
reviews.text: Fantastic staff, front desk through bell and valet service. Free parking and fast bellman service. Good restaurant on premices and short skyway power sidewalks to Palms Casino. Ez uber Lyft pick up location just outside of valet loop. Views of mountains for sunsets just as good as city skyline side. Corner 1 br. Suites are super large but if you rent through hotel directly no balcony access. Try Air BNB for best value and patio access...

reviews.title: Book through Airbnb!
reviews.text: Booked through Airbnb and felt I got a good deal. No extra resort fees. The room was large and had all the amenities needed. The pool is nice, as is the fitness room. I left my book in the fitness room and when I called the front desk that evening, they confirmed they had it in the lost and found. Enjoyed the free parking for our rental car as well. If course staying on the strip in a nicer hotel would be great, but also much more expensive. This place was fine and a short Uber to the strip when needed.

reviews.title: 3 nights @ palms place - overcharged
reviews.text: This resort was clean but some parts under construction . Our check in took a long time and our keys didn’t work at first , then back to the front counter for new keys again they didn’t work so we had to again go down and we were put into a different room . The room was clean with a nice view of the strip . Biggest complaint is the hotel charging me for mini bar consumption  when we never took anything from  the mini bar . They put a few extra charges to my credit card 1 week after my stay including a higher resort fee than was stated and the mini bar charge that we didn’t use . After contacting the hotel they are saying nothing can be done because something was consumed for mini bar . 100% we did not use our mini bar . Unless the maid were thirsty ?? Also our room was only cleaned 2 out of three days , hair dyer didn’t work and we needed to request more towels . Resort fee was high 44$ per night and obviously the service we received was subpar . Over all I would not recommend the palms due to they overcharging , high resort fee and poor cleaning service . Be advised to watch your credit card bill for overcharges  for this hotel .

reviews.title: Honeymoon suite
reviews.text: Booked the suite for our wedding Night. The staff was kind and helpful. Could do an early checkin (had to pay extra for this Ofcourse). The suite was nice and the view was mindblowing. Unfortunately some things was missing. The bathtub didn’t work properly. No robes or glasses. The lighting system was tricky to use. But overall, happy with the place. The valet guys were Very kind and helpful at this hotel.

reviews.title: Worth checking out
reviews.text: Keep in mind that you can book directly with Palms Place but that many rooms are managed by their owners thru Airbnb.  You'll want to explore both options for best rate.My sister and I have stayed here twice now and each time she's snagged a great deal for SUITES.  Two entire walls of windows with patio, large bathrooms, full gourmet kitchen and the last suite had a huge tub!Palms place has proven to be a quiet property yet you can easily walk to the Palms for dining, gaming & entertainment.Worth the time to shop for great deals.  The rooms are slightly dated but the value of space is definitely worth the trip.

reviews.title: Disappointed!!
reviews.text: My husband and I booked this hotel Sunday night to celebrate our one-year anniversary being married. We were in town early and wanted to see if we can check-in and we were told no so we waited until 3:45 to check-in. We were told our room was not ready. Okay, we waited until 4pm. Our room should be ready by 4pm to check in, BUT...we were told to wait AGAIN! We waited until 4:30pm to check-in. Terribly disappointed with this hotel. Would not stay here again.We were too disappointed and upset. Wasted our time waiting.

reviews.title: Never Again
reviews.text: I should have followed my first mind not to stay here after reading so many other bad reviews. But my brother lives in Vegas and gifted me this reservation and paid all the ridiculous “resort fees” so I decided to stay. And still hated it, for all the reasons outlined in the other bad reviews. At first glance everything is lovely. It’s set back from the Strip, the lobby is lovely, at first glance the rooms are spacious and modern...but then. My sheets hadn’t been changed—visible dirt on the pillowcases & they smelled. Either staff took a nap in that room before I got there or the sheets just hadn’t been changed from the previous guest. There was hair (that wasn’t mine) everywhere. The floor had a huge stain that looked & smelled like something that had come out of both ends. The jacuzzi tub was dirty and the jets didn’t work. Everything was dusty and dirty. When I approached Cassandra at the front desk and asked “can you help me with a problem with my room?” she had the nerve to say “Depends...” *Eye Roll* When the room was cleaned they used so much bleach it gave me a headache. Just poor management and housekeeping all the way around. The final dealbreaker for me was that despite this room having a full kitchen with appliances and utensils, they don’t include a wine opener. Why? So they can charge customers $6.49 for one. It’s really ridiculous how counterintuitive their “customer service” is. Won’t be back.

reviews.title: Beware of hidden prices
reviews.text: The room was nice, and a great tub and shower. We didn’t utilize the kitchen, other than the refrigerator. We did request the kitchen set-up (pots, pans etc.) in case we decided to purchase food.  Walkable distance to the strip - providing no health issues. They do have a walkway to the casino, but some of the area is under construction, so not a pleasant walk or feeling of security. They do have a free parking lot if you rent a car, which is nice. HOWEVER, upon checking out, they informed us of a resort fee of $42 per night, and an internet access fee of $9.99. We had NO recourse to debate or decline payment.  Therefore, we will NEVER stay here again!!!

reviews.title: WOULD NOT RECOMMEND
reviews.text: We stayed for 3 nights in early February in a studio suite in Palms Place (adjacent to the hotel/casino).  Pros: The room was large and included some kitchen facilities (2 burner stove, microwave).  Bathroom featured amenities, but no bathrobes.  Walkable distance from the strip.  Lovely spa and gym.Cons:  The Palms Place tower seems to have been built as condos, the rooms are rented out as hotel rooms but are actually for sale - this was not disclosed when we booked the room.Service, attention to detail and follow up were non existent. Part of Palms Place is under renovation, we had to walk through the garage to get to the main hotel/casino.  Most serious:  when the reservation was made, we were immediately billed on our credit card.  Consequently, we were charged for an additional night, the Palms billing department refused to refund the $.  Also, there is an almost $50 resort fee per night which is fine if you are using the spa/gym but makes the room not that much of a bargain.   Check out is 11am- we asked for 12n and were refused.

reviews.title: Very comfortable
reviews.text: This hotel room was very comfortable. It had a ton of space and is very modern. I really liked the kitchen area and the bathrooms have ample storage space. The only drawback is that the casino was under construction, so some areas were closed. Overall, I would return here

reviews.title: Great hotel for the price
reviews.text: Great price and just a little off the strip. Nice giant suite. Nice view of the mountains from our room. We asked for hypo-allergenic pillows and they came and traded out all bedding to meet the need. Super customer service and attention to detail. Only draw back to the suite was there no refrigerator other than the one stocked to purchase from. Only draw back to the casino was the perfumey smell spray they use to cover the smoke smell.

reviews.title: In desperate need of a renovation
reviews.text: We booked two "studio" suites for a 1-night stay.  Upon check-in around 2:30-3pm, there was only a single person working the entire front desk.  The check-in wait was 15 minutes, and then the check-in process was anything but quick and smooth.  Our request for a high floor was accommodated, but when we asked for adjacent rooms, they could only give us rooms on opposite sides of the corridor...and on the extreme opposite ends of our floor.  That was not a good start.  Then one set of the card keys that we were provided during check-in did not open 1 of the 2 rooms we were assigned.  When I went back to the front desk 10 minutes later...still the sole employee working the front desk with a line of people waiting to check in.  When I tried to motion to him that the keys he gave me would not allow us in our room, he shrugged his shoulders and said we would have to wait back in the long line.  Twenty additional minutes later, he finally gave us a new set of card keys.  Oh by the way, it wouldn't hurt if their front desk employees would smile for a change versus the stern no-nonsense look we were greeted with both times.  Our rooms (both on the 36th floor) 303 and 316 were not very clean.  I have attached photos I took of a non-working lock of the bathroom sliding door.  Apparently, Las Vegas is a hard water area, and from the amount of visible calcium deposits that were built up and clogging our hand held shower head, apparently the housekeeping department has not considered cleaning or dunking these shower heads in a glass of the cleaning solution "CLR" to remove the lime and hard water deposits.  My white end table to the left of the bed had burn marks from what looked like maybe a past cigarette smoker.  The dark brown colored fake woodgrain  front credenza at the foot of the bed had all these visible scratches.  Before going to bed, I was stepping into bed.  My barefeet was touching the dark stained wood laminate flooring that covers the bed and mattress floor area...when my foot felt a very sticky material on the floor.  I don't know what "it" was, but it apparently had been thete for awhile, and somehow never noticed or cleaned up my housekeeping.  When I bent down to see what it was, I found what was half way exposed from underneath the bed, a used paper towel or tissue.  As I pulled it out to dispose of it, to my utter surprise and disgust, was a used condom!  Is the housekeeping staff at this place that lazy and not actually spending time to "clean" these rooms??  The studio suites come equipped with microwave, refrigerator, stove top, and dishwasher.  Although I didn't have a reason to use these appliances, when I pulled out the drawer of the dishwasher, i found it all wirh lots of lime and calcium deposits.  Once again, does the housekeeping ever drop one of those dishwasher "self cleaning" tablets to clense and disinfect their dishwashers once or twice a year??  When we arrived back at the hotel around 11:30pm from a show we attended earlier that evening, we were greeted at the front door entrance with a very loud exchange of some people that arrived from a ride sharing car service, with a heated exchange of non-stop screaming profanities and vulagarities for all to hear regarding the driver being horrible...and supposedly had run into or damaged a parking pole while dropping off his customers at this hotel.  Where was the hotel's onsite  security to break this up before fists were about to fly?  My family felt very uncomfortable, and thought we were staying at a hotel of thugs and overly drunken patrons.  It ended our evening on a very scary note.  Our room's so-called air conditioning never pumped cold air into our room, just room temperature air.  Versus, the other room in our party (36-316), way down on the other end of the floor's hallway, had cool air piped into their floor constantly.  Although the price for the 1-night's stay was less expensive than anything comparable on the strip, I can't recommend this property.  I took the photos to validate my concerns, and hope that the property's management will take my review serious enough to warrant some long overdue changes in their current policies.

reviews.title: Over Priced Resort
reviews.text: I called the hotel for an early check in the night prior to my stay and they said if a room was available at the time it would be a $25+ tax fee. No problem. I get to the hotel, check in at 9am and go to the room. It was FILTHY! There was a hand print on the mirror above the bed, the floors had dried stuff on it, the couch had stains on it and the wood paneling behind the couch had visible stuff splattered on it. After calling the front desk and behind on hold for 10min, I went down and asked for another room, which was frustrating that the 2 agents at the desk were not busy but I was on hold without answer. They did not have one and said they would send housekeeping up. I asked if there was anything they could do - reduce the $44 resort fee, waive the early check in and the gal said no just housekeeping. Not the customer service I am experienced to receiving from any Las Vegas property, being a local at a now locals casino I would have thought they'd have treated me better. Housekeeping did come up and changed my bed linens and did a throughout job as I sat there and made sure of it.

reviews.title: Do not stay here!
reviews.text: It is rare that I write a review that is negative but this place is a rip off! I flew in and arrived at the hotel to be treated by 2 nice ladies at the front desk who were very nice and helpful (they are the only good thing about the experience). When we got to our rooms they smelled of smoke pretty badly. We decided to try and tough it out since we were so tired from traveling all day. After tossing and turning for hours we decided early in the am to just check out and find another hotel. Now the real issues begin, When we explained that we wanted to leave the hotel they told us they wouldn’t refund any money and that we had to pay for the stay since we didn’t make the cancellation deadlines... I’m not sure I saw smelly, smoky rooms as the room type we reserved... hmmmm I should look closer next time I guess🤷🏽‍♂️. Needless to say we asked for a manager. When he arrived and heard our story we got the same reply, you’ll have to pay for the room. We told him that this is ridiculous but we were willing to pay for the one night we stayed. When the cc bill arrived we were charged for 3 of the 4 nights of the rooms and I was also charged hotel fees, room surcharges and etc for the entire stay! I have been disputing these charges ever since and. The hotel is fighting giving me a refund. If you want horrible customer service, smelly and smoky rooms, your time wasted if you decide to speak to management, well then you have found the perfect place to stay!!!!!!! I am open to discuss this issue with senior management if they choose to reach out.

reviews.title: Entire staff needs lessons in hospitality, property is disappointing
reviews.text: I am just sitting down after a 45 minute journey from check in to my room. This disaster started with the Front Desk at the Palms. If there are separate lobbies for Palms versus Palms Place, wouldn't it be smart to email guests that information in advance so they know where to tell taxis to drop them? I have 4 heavy bags for a week's stay and am nearly 7 MONTHS PREGNANT. I check in and, upon inquiring about how far the walk is to my room, Karmel tells me it's 5 minutes. It is not. No offer to get a belman, nothing so I figure I'll just step up and do it myself since it's super late. It's about 10-15 minutes for me to drag my heavy bags along the carpeted floor (much harder to wheel luggage) through a desolate and potentially unsafe parking garage with hardly any signage to the far away Palms Place. I finally get there and have to search for that lobby. I explain how unhappy I am about this treatment (or lack thereof) to the front desk manager and she barely bats an eye. My back is now full of shooting pain and my neck stiff from dragging everything, doesn't seem to care. I ask nicely if they can offer some kind of massage for my awful journey on property... denied! All they do is get me a bellman who doesn't even offer to lift up my suitcase and set it up on the rack!To top it all off, the furniture is tattered and the room is tired and rudiementary.A complete disappointment and I feel that I received grossly negligent services.

reviews.title: Surprise? Yes! Nice? No!!
reviews.text: I had not stayed at Palms Place for more than four years. My memories were good ones in general. New ownership, Station Casinos,  have cut corners and belt-tightened to the point of failing the customer badly.  I cannot recommend staying here. When I visit Las Vegas, I always try to have a kitchen to avoid going out for breakfast and snacks. So I gravitate towards places like Palms Place and Hilton Grand Vacations Club. Problems started with check-in. 4:00 PM check-in time and there are only two agents on duty. Far too long of a wait. The beautiful kitchen was in a great state of disrepair. The ice maker on the Sub Zero refrigerator had been removed and ice was nowhere to be found. No kitchen utensils were provided. When I requested full kitchen materials, I was provided two plates, two glasses, two forks, two knives and two spoons. So I would not be entertaining in my room. The faucet in the kitchen sink was loose as was the handle on the refrigerator that was stocked with items to buy.  Many other things in the room showed great wear. This room had not been updated since before my last visit in 2014. Housekeeping was horrendous. I was completely ignored and had to call two of my four days to get someone to come. I did without the other two days. Room service had a habit of not picking up their phone either. Add to this the inconvenient location (unless you want to purchase some marijuana - there are two dispensaries directly across the street), you are better off spending a few dollars more and staying at one of the Hilton grand Vacations Clubs, like the Elara. And finally, I have now been home for 36 hours and am STILL waiting for them to E-mail me my final bill, which they could not provide me with at checkout. I had this hotel booked for another trip in June but I cancelled today and booked elsewhere.

reviews.title: Nice Surprise
reviews.text: I had not been to The Palms in years. I had a business trip coming up and they had a pretty good rate so I thought I would try them even though the last time I was there I did not think much of the place. I arrived and much has changed. For the better. Totally redone since I’ve been there. The place is great. Nice casino. Great sports book. A movie theatre. Concert Venue. Great night club. Great spa and workout facilities. Many restaurants. Great bar. Rooms are great. I had a long week and wanted to see about a room upgrade. The great girl at the counter and gave me very reasonable price to upgrade to s suite. Needless to say my upgraded room was incredible. Everything was five star. Highly recommend staying here. Just off the strip so you get a much better deal on a similar type room on the strip.

reviews.title: Average hotel, too far off the strip, dated rooms
reviews.text: We stayed here one night because we were in town for a show and the show was at The Palms Casino Resort.  The Palms Place hotel is part of the resort but is a separate tower on the same grounds.  The great thing about the Palms Place is that you do not have to walk through a seedy casino to get places in the tower.   It does feel more like a boutique hotel - small lobby area and no casino however it has kind of a "miami vice" feel - dated and definitely too dark.  There was only 2 agents checking in guests so it took about 20 minutes plus it was 5 PM and we were told the housekeepers were still vacuuming so we had to take a room on a much lower floor (10) than we had originally booked (53). Our room was a 1 bedroom suite but there was just a half wall separating the bedroom from the living room which was not disclosed to us at booking.  There was a kitchen but it looked like it had taken a beating and needed some help.  The room was very dark and in the bedroom the lamps which were the only light source were entirely encased in big pink transparent bubbles so our room was pink.  Not a good look.  The worst part was the street noise - it was horrendously loud.  Seriously, felt like we were next to the interstate - cars at all house, 3 police cars blasting sirens, 1 fire engine, 1 car alarm for about 15 minutes, etc - all between midnight and 7.  VERY LOUD - must get a room at least above the 20th floor.We didn't like the dining options at the resort and wanted to try Trevi at Caesar's (a great choice).  It was very busy in town so we decided to walk as we could see Caesar's  from The Palms - took 30 minutes each way.  Most areas off the strip are pretty seedy and this area was no exception - passed over the 15 on a covered bridge and had to dodge a few people in sleeping bags.....So in all, OK hotel, too far off the strip, too loud at low rooms, dated rooms, and average dining options.

reviews.title: No full disclosure
reviews.text: Standard rooms were OK.  We didn't expect to get a sun tan in December but wanted to sit the pool and there wasn't one.   You had to walk about ten minutes to the sister resort past construction/construction workers  and temporary walls, into a garage and up and down elevators and through the spa.  All that being said the pool at the other resort was beautiful, but its hours were erratic and some days not open at all with no prior notice.  The Palms also sent us on this same walk to the use the Gym.   All of this should have been explained at booking, nothing was said.  Nothing was said at check in either, so it was a nasty surprise to find this out on your own.   Also there was a big construction site outside so there will not be any pool there anytime soon.   There were also other restaurants that were not open.

reviews.title: Away from the STRIP
reviews.text: If your are a regular LAS VEGAS visitor like myself, The Palms Place HI-Rise Suites is the place to STAY.  Go to AIRBNB and look for TYLER and rent his condo. It's quite..bed is comfortable, clean, and you will love the bathroom. This place has it's own kitchen area with refrigerator, stove, microwave etc.  He's a great host and communicates timely. It's very modern, and the images shown on AIRBNB is exactly how it looks in person. Price is affordable and fees are decent. Unlike these other hotels on the strip, they charge for resort fee, parking, etc.  This location does not charge for parking and it's very convenient. Even if you don't have a vehicle, there's taxi, lyft, uber...  The major plus for me, is that once you park your car,, you go into the hotel.. walk in the elevator ... not like the other places you go through the stress of having to find what tower your elevator is on.. etc.. LIKE I said.. I recommend this place, but most return VEGAS visitors.. understands why it's best to say away from the strip from time to time..

reviews.title: Quiet Off Strip Place To Stay
reviews.text: If you are looking for a Vegas hotel that has more of a boutique feel this a great spot.  Hotel is off strip so you will have to walk or drive over to the strip.  This is the residential wing of the Palms Hotel so it's a lot quieter and calmer then some of the other hotel casinos.  The room was spacious with a kitchenette and an amazing bathroom.  Limited amenities, no mini bar.  Only one lobby bar that closes early but your attached to the Palm Hotel and Casino so you can just walk over there for the action.  Definitely would stay again.

reviews.title: Wsop 18
reviews.text: I highly recommended this place for long poker stays in Vegas.. try booking a place here well in advance through Air BnB or contact them directly.. ordering room service everyday can be a bit unhealthy for us for I recommend getting your own groceries or ordering in , eating out basically mixing it up.. there’s a food court in the hotel as well... can always watch a movie in the In-Hotel Theatre next to the food court on the casino floor... this is just a u turn away from rio... I walked it once when there was no sun otherwise too hot to walk it , I recommend Uber over renting a car as you can waste a lot of time finding parking!! Perfect place to stay if you’re on the grind for poker or any other sport which  requires you to spend a long time in Vegas! oh and that view <3 I wish I could stay here forever! #Fingerscrossed

reviews.title: Tired Hotel with Exorbitant Resort Fee
reviews.text: We stayed for one night in a studio suite. Room was reasonable but pretty tired, the toilet roll was half pulled out of the wall and the thermostat for the heater/cooler was broken so the room was either too cold or ridiculously hot. Pool is nice but not heated enough during winter to make it swimmable. My main gripe with the property is the $45 resort fee, the highest resort fee I've ever seen in my life. I was initially okay with paying it because I thought it included a shuttle to/from The Strip, but The Palms canceled the free shuttle a few months before our stay so for the resort fee you basically get...nothing. Will never go back, the resort fee is pure extortion.

reviews.title: Beautiful View of City
reviews.text: I really enjoyed my stay here at Palms Place Hotel & Spa. The room & accommodations were spectacular. The hotel staff were very pleasant and welcoming. Everything we asked of them they made sure was done. We stayed December 12/4-12/7. The suite was immaculate. very nice. I Loved it! The only two things I had issues with were that we couldn't open the balconies (due to some Air B&B policy or something), and the dryer DID NOT work.

reviews.title: Great Place To Stay
reviews.text: spent 2 days we hired a suite which was amazing up to date decor fully fitted kitchen with oven, fridge, dishwasher, washing machine. Very plush apartment we were on 52nd floor amazing views. Separate toilet, large bathroom with walk in shower, toilet and sink. Large flatscreen tv in lounge. Bed very comfortable further large flatscreen tv in bedroom and also free standing bathHighly recommended

reviews.title: Dirty rooms and the most terrible service
reviews.text: I don't even know where to begin with our terrible experience at this hotel. We had to switch room over and over again because how dirty they are. The first one had a dirty mop hanging on the ceiling, and fridge smelt. We moved to the second room and there was a coffee and sugar all over the floor. Kitchen sink was very dirty. Okay at that point we were so tired we just asked them to clean the room. The manager that night was nice (and the only nice one) who waived the resort fee for us. Then in the middle of night, the AC unit is not working and my husband could barely breath. We called the service in the morning, no one came to fix in the entire day while we were out. We had to call again and they sent someone at 10Pm and started to make noise. We had a young baby in the room and he started to spray toxic gas without even asking us if it's okay for the baby. Then the AC broke again in the middle of the room, and released toxic gas. The next day after much back and forth with manager, they move us to a bigger room. but instead of making it convenient for us, they forced us to move everything before we head out to start our day. We have a baby with lots of stuff. The move took more than an hour and pretty much ruined our last day there at vegas. Then we moved to the new room, there was an used soap in the shower. We spoke with manager the next day. They said there is nothing they can do.  The place is so dirty and disgusting. The windows are full of dust. the services are terrible. We spoke with four managers. other than very first one, I forgot his name but he was the tall and skinny one - very polite and the best one. everyone else was unhelpful. The  female manager Sharee was the worst. lots of attitude. rude and unprofessional. One of the worst of service individuals i have met (and I have traveled to 54 countries and stayed at thousands of hotels). She was upset because we were telling her the issues we encounter. She was upset because she had to do her job to make her customers happy.

reviews.title: A nice place to stay
reviews.text: At the end of a grand tour of California I decided to stop and relax at one final location. I have stayed in many places in Las Vegas over the years but this was the first time at The PALMS.I was wanting to have the ability to stay somewhere that provided a variety of food outlets but also allow me the opportunity to look after myself, food wise if i wished. Although the suite seemed to offer this, upon inspection I found that the galley was not fully equipped. The top fridge was full of hotel goodies and worked on, a take it from the unit and you are charged basis, even if you put it back!The room temperature control was difficult to fathom.However, overall a great place to stay, even though there was a lot of construction taking place. Once complete I'm sure it'll be even better.Scotch restaurant was excellent.

reviews.title: 36th floor stunning views
reviews.text: 3 nights stay here as part of a road trip across USA.Easy check in and polite staff.Room on 36th floor with glass balcony and fantastic view over the strip.Lovely apartment room with kitchen, sofa , comfortable bed and bathroom.Good location to visit strip. Good facilities nearby with shops/ restaurants.Parking onsite was free.Loved our stay here.highly recommend

reviews.title: Dark and dreary
reviews.text: The staff here are all very friendly, Our room was extremely dark and dreary. Makes it almost impossible to get any work done, or even to put on makeup. The tile floor was grimmy in the kitchen area and the red bed stand lamp was really dusty. We have stayed here before and deal with the darkness of the room, however the cleanliness is a deal breaker for me in the room.  Way way overpriced for what you get

reviews.title: Stayed for my Birthday !
reviews.text: Stayed in room 18102Although they are still doing construction, (they were on our last visit as well) we had no complaints.  Sad the pool is not available but anxious to see the new pool when It is all complete.  Staff from the Valet, Baggage men and front desk staff all were very pleasant.  Are room was clean and comfortable. Large and spacious bathroom. We have not checked out the spa but hope to on a future visit.  Nice newly decorated front desk and bar called Unknown in Lobby area.  We will stay again in the future and really looking forward to see everything when the construction is done.

reviews.title: Great space!
reviews.text: We really enjoyed our stay at Palms Place. The location is as awesome as the condo. The host was very responsive when we had a problem connecting to the internet. We were there for a concert at the Palms which is next door.....very convenient.

reviews.title: Odd stay and not in a good way
reviews.text: An unusual set up in that these "studio apartments" may or may not be privately owned.Pro: quiet entrance and lobby with no need to trek far and through a casino.Room is a good size with small kitchen, large jetted tub and separate shower.Cons: $44 per night "resort fee". Resort fee charges continue to outage me, especially in a season where there is no possibility of pool or other resort type use.  Also room is pretty shabby, which is really obvious given the contemporary decor.  Couch cushions are very faded and bed cushions are stained with what is clearly hair oils.Finally, rooms were advertised as with balcony, but doors are permanently locked so balcony is not accessible.To sum up: not worth the close to $300 a night total. For that money (we stayed sat and sun) you can find a much nicer room without the stains.

reviews.title: Looks Good But Only On The Surface
reviews.text: Our tub we leaking sewer gas into the room. The shower backed up into the bathroom when draining the tub. It absolutely reeked the whole time. The refrigerator in our room was broken so they put a tiny mini fridge in there. No apologies from the staff and they treat you like dirt. I spent my time and my gambling money at the Rio instead. This place left a horrible taste in my mouth that won't soon be forgotten.

reviews.title: 2 nights visit to Las Vagas
reviews.text: The room is very large and complete in every sense of it.Very comfortable bed.  The facilities provided in the hotel room are nice. The hotel staff were courteous and friendly. The hotel was undergoing renovation and yet the inconvenience was minimal.

reviews.title: Out Standing
reviews.text: We have friends who stay here all the time so it was a no brainer not to visit, the staff cant do enough for you and the rooms are spotless, even the cleaners were nice to talk too.The place was undergoing a major re fit while we were there but apart from areas being boarded up for work it was fine, look for to a re visit

reviews.title: Excellent Hotel
reviews.text: We recommend this place, we celebrate marriage anniversary, excellent buffet, nice room with strip view, very nice staff, excellent pool, excellent spa , we recommend this place to couple , we enjoyed it, romantic place. Thank you.

reviews.title: Weekend treat to see the rock band Blink 182
reviews.text: What a perfect location to stay at whilst watching Blink 182 at the Pearl theatre at the next door Palms hotel resort.Check in at 2pm on a Friday afternoon was easy and quick, I asked for a high floor and strip facing. Got room 50310 on the 50th floor.Perfect and a fabulous view of the strip.The room was immaculate , large and everything is good order. I could not have asked for more.Pool area is small but for the amount of people around it on a Friday afternoon it was fine.I would recommend this hotel if you don’t mind been of the strip a little and is perfect for when all the renovations to the Palms resort next doo are complete, I believe it is to have the biggest pool area in Vegas when finished by the middle of next year.Now that’s worth a visit.Well done the Palms Place Hotel and Spa.

reviews.title: Good off strip option Shuttlebus discontinued
reviews.text: 2nd time we have stayed here and value for money is amazing.We had a corner room, room 26102 which had amazing views.best bit is the cleanliness of the rooms, they are immaculate.Building works are still ongoing so only 1 pool which suited us.Only issue is that they have stopped their free shuttle bus from palms to Caesar’s forum shops.Not really a dealbreaker Feel like they are going to go more upmarket a fed think maybe their prices will change too

reviews.title: Don’t waste your money
reviews.text: We booked a three night stay with the Palms, which has turned out to be a huge disappointment.  Our room, unknown to us, was privately owned.  So when I called down to the front desk to get a couple extra pillows and a coffee cup for in the morning, I was informed that they couldn’t help with a cup and that it was going to cost me $5.00 a day per pillow.  To make things worse the towels were so hard and dingy in color that I wouldn’t even wash my dogs with them.  So unless you want to pay $250.00 a day for a room without room service, only one coffee cup, and ugly hard towels, don’t book a night at the Palms

reviews.title: Awesome room
reviews.text: I found this room on Airbnb looking for a space close to the Strip, but with a balcony. It was more than I could have imagine. The balcony was very spacious and had an amazing view of the entire Strip. The mini-apartment was extremely modern and well maintained. Parking was free and easy and the staff in the lobby were polite and helpful, even though they don’t offer all hotel amenities like daily room cleaning. The price was great for all you get. The bathroom was our favorite!

reviews.title: Amazing place
reviews.text: I have stayed at Palms Place with my husband for over a week at the end of July/beginning of August 2018. We had a 1 bedroom suite on the 26th floor with two massive balconies and a view of the whole Strip. It was close enough to go by Uber (about 6 usd one way trip) but far enough to be away from all the noise. The suite was very modern, with plenty of room, huge bathroom with double shower and a bath in the bedroom! Kitchen lacked few utensils- no knives or other silverware, few pans/pots etc. and the fireplace did not work but we did not mind. Very comfortable bed, great water pressure and a touch of luxury by the furnishings. During the weekend we had to present the room key to enter the premises. Very nice gym and pool- a little quieter than the ones on the Strip but we still had lots of fun (like everywhere no food/drinks allowed to the pool site) and never had a problem finding the sun bed. SPA was on a rather expensive side so we decided not to use it. There is a little shop in the lobby should you need any essentials.
