Three weeks later I get a £143 charge again. You have not responded my emails despite me sending it three times! What great customer service after us spending so much as your hotel.Room was 26309

reviews.title: Let's give this a second try
reviews.text: I will heading to the Palms Place in a few weeks for 4 days and hope to have a better experience than before. Already my booking experience has been a little concerning. I love the views and hope to have better experience. Gail J.

reviews.title: Fabulous Room.
reviews.text: Stayed here for 3 nights in July. Amazing room. Huge, with lounge area tv, locked patio area. Great views looking East.Amazing bathroom, jet tub, tv in bathroom. Spotlessly clean, well maintained.Very nice. The rooms are privately owned studios and apartments and are rented out when owners not in residence.Super fast elevators.Covered Walkway to main Palms Hotel and Casino.Very nice staff on front desk.would stay here again.

reviews.title: A good experience in the hotel but not enjoyable experience in their casino
reviews.text: This hotel is clean and comfortable. I and my wife visited Palm place resort during the labor day weekend. We really enjoyed and relaxed when living there. In addition, the view from our room is incredible fantastic! We can see the skyline of the Strip during the night. The jacuzzi hot tubs is awesome, too. However, we had an unhappy experience when we played the table game "roulette". Usually each table has screen and show latest numbers in recent games. When we played in one of their table, I found the screen was broken just right after exchanging chips and started to bet. I think at least the dealer and staff in casino should inform all of the guests before they want to join the game, even consider close that table. Because I still saw other empty table (might be still functional) when I was there.

reviews.title: Most horrible hotel experience I have ever had
reviews.text: This review is the subjective opinion of an individual traveller and not of Tripadvisor LLC nor of its partners. Tripadvisor performs checks on reviews as part of our industry-leading trust & safety standards. Read our transparency report to learn more.

reviews.title: Enjoyed our stay & the beutiful view over the strip
reviews.text: The room was very nice and spacious and would like to thank reception in providing us with a room to have the most beautiful view over looking the strip. The bed was so comfy and the bathroom was divine.  We were very happy to be just outside of the strip and a courtesy bus is available if needed. Due to having a car the undercover parking was very beneficial due to the hot weather. Overall I would be very happy to stay again.

reviews.title: Started Out Poorly but Ended Well
reviews.text: This was my first time to The Palm Place to stay. I'm typically a Signature Suites and Encore Suites person. We arrived around 2 AM and check in was flawless.We stopped to eat at the only cafe open before going to the room and was a bit taken back by poor attitudes of the staff. The food there was really good however. Once in the room on the 39th floor we experienced setback #2. I believe Cheetch & Chong just had just checked out as the room reeked of Marijuana which was terrible. A call to the front desk went unanswered therefore we just suffered because we were too tired. The next morning a trip to the counter resulted in a room change without issues but no apology or attempt to compensate us for the inconvenience. The next three nights were great. The 600 ft Suites had wonderful beds, bathrooms with shower/ Jucczi and wood floor. At check out I asked to speak with the manager who I've seen respond to negative responses on Trip Advisor. I looked at Trip Advisor before booking this hotel and noticed they read the critics. The manager was apparently at another building, therefore Nathan spoke with me at my request. I personally believe the first  night should have been taken off totally but at least he waved the resort fee and some room charges. They at least listen and made an attempt to make it right. Hopefully there housekeeping will do a better job as a result of this. I would return to this hotel to try it again.

reviews.title: The best!
reviews.text: This was our second consecutive stay at Palms Place. The room was exactly as we expected and hoped. We really enjoy the full kitchen and open studio. The huge jetted tub is amazing! Housekeeping kept the coffee and towels stocked and even brought a shaving kit with razor and shave cream when requested. The white bedding was spotless and so comfortable! The bellhop had my boyfriend's tux pressed and were always super helpful. A special shout out to Paige, the best concierge ever! She was so friendly and helpful, we looked forward to chatting with her as we headed out to our daily activities. Another great thing about Palms Place is that the lobby is quiet and the taxi/valet area is small. You can step out of your ride and the elevators up to your room are right there in the lobby! It has its own pool, bar, sundry shop, and restaurant. This way, you aren't forced to withstand the loud smokey casino if you don't want to. Easily enough, you can take the sky tube over to the Palms casino side for the imax theater, more restaurants, the casino, and another pool.For us, vacation in Vegas isn't just the casinos and other attractions, it's also about feeling pampered and having a luxurious room!

reviews.title: Nice Stay
reviews.text: I had a studio suite. It was modern in decor and spacious. The bathroom had a walk-in shower and a jacuzzi tub. I was in walking distance of other hotels and a decent trek to the strip. I car ride probably would have been more comfortable but if you want a little exercise you can walk it. My only complaints are having to pay for internet access and one day my room was not cleaned. I had to call and ask to have it done. However, I would consider staying here again. Safe location.

reviews.title: I really did not enjoy this hotel
reviews.text: I would not recommend this property. The suites very large and the building itself is attractive. The staff is extremely unprofessional. The front desk personnel was very unprofessional. Same goes for the staff at the bars. There was one woman that worked at the pool bar that was so rude that I finally just walked away from her. I would recommend the entire staff including Managment be retrained in hospitality. I will not ever come back to this hotel. 30 trips to Las Vegas this was the worst hotel experience I have ever had.

reviews.title: Beautiful Hotel, Suites Need Some Work
reviews.text: The hotel itself is beautiful, especially when you first walk in.  The food court downstairs is definitely a plus.  Even though its not on the strip, theres so much to do at the hotel you wouldn't necessarily always need to go on the strip.  The shuttle service to the strip could be a lot better in regards to them having more buses to accommodate all the guests or at least make more trips.  There is usually a big crowd waiting but only one 15 passenger bus every 1/2 hr.  The rooms, in particular, the suites were beautiful but can use some TLC. The first suite we went in was really dusty, smelled really musky, and the furniture was beat up. We requested a new room and we got it with no problem.  This room wasn't much better which made me realize that they were probably all just outdated.  Other than this we really enjoyed our stay here.

reviews.title: Less than average
reviews.text: My husband and I visited for our honeymoon and we were less than impressed. After ordering room service my husband and I asked for a couple of wine glasses to be sent up to the room with our order only to be told that they was a $2 dollar charge per glass. We booked a room with a kitchenette in so kinda expected there to be at the very least wine glasses. My husband also emailed the hotel prior to the visit regarding a surprise for me to which he is still awaiting a response. We will not be returning and certainly will not be recommending the palms!!!

reviews.title: Fun in the sun
reviews.text: In college and before my two beautiful kids, Vegas was Loud clubs, flashing lights and fast cars . If you're looking for a quiet, peaceful luxury resort on a budget, the palms place is your best bet.Ive been to alot of vegas resorts but nothing compares to the 1 bedroom 950 square foot suite with fireplace, full kitchen, living area and bathtub in bedroom.If youre lucky they will only charge you maybe 80.00 a day for the upgrade. You will also get a view of the pool as well amazing.If youre with your family, i suggest going  swimming at the palms place pool. If youre with the guys or girls walk 5 minutes next door to the palms pool where the dj is bumping and they serve HOOTERS POOLSIDE. AWESOMENESS

reviews.title: World Class Concierge Service @ The PalmsPlace Hotel And Spa..
reviews.text: The Palms Place Hotel And Spa is a great place to stay while in Las Vegas it has everything you'd need if you didn't want to leave the property during your stay...Now lets say you want to leave the property and go explore Vegas maybe a Hover Dam Tour or how about getting a rental car or just about anything else you can dream up while in Vegas . Then here is what you do go down to the Concierge Desk @ The PalmsPlace side and Ask for "Stacey.G". Not only did Stacey know the hotel property but her recommendations about what to do and see in Vegas was over the top and spot on...And if that wasn't already good enough the setup of the Tours and rental car was fast and super efficiently handled. All done with a smile."Stacy.G" your a world class concierge...   Thank you for making this the best Vegas trip ever. A+++++

reviews.title: Great rooms but a little removed from the action
reviews.text: We really enjoyed our room and most of the amenities of the resort.  It was a little odd that we had to request the dishes for full kitchen that was included with the room.  The shower and bath were excellent for a getaway to be able to relax.  We enjoyed the pool and outdoor area a few times.  The only challenge is that the hotel is a solid 20-25 minute walk just to get to the strip.

reviews.title: Palms Place: neither overwhelming or underwhelming.  Just a solid "Good."
reviews.text: This review is the subjective opinion of an individual traveller and not of Tripadvisor LLC nor of its partners. Tripadvisor performs checks on reviews as part of our industry-leading trust & safety standards. Read our transparency report to learn more.

reviews.title: Comfortable place to stay
reviews.text: We enjoyed the rooftop pool, the studios with very modern furnishings.  We would definitely stay there again. I feel it was a good value for the money and even though not on the strip it was close enough to the strip.

reviews.title: Best hotel ever!!!
reviews.text: Rooms are very spacious and very modern.bathroom area is beautiful, great jacuzzi inside...excellent rate!!!!Spa in this hotel extremely good, very clean and full of accessories.All around this hotel is definitely my favorite in Vegas.

reviews.title: Love the full-service options at this live-in hotel
reviews.text: Stayed here on a staycation for my birthday with my husband and we absolutely loved the amenities. We were able to use the spa for a couples massage (amazing and very luxurious, considering we have stayed at many 5-star resorts), as well as the gym area, which was very well maintained and immaculate. While Palms Place has a setting in which many of the levels are time shares or are privately owned, it has built in kitchenettes and is fully functional for the well-made cook. However, it is walkable to the Palms, where if you do not want to cook, you have world-class restaurants and entertainment. We dined at N9ne Steakhouse and it did not disappoint. Have also dined at the local restaurants within Palms Place with other locals and the fare is fresh and well-put together. Entertainment is within walking distance at the Palms or a $10 taxi or Uber ride away at other resorts. Palms Place is fantastic for couples or small families looking to be in Vegas for a short stay.

reviews.title: Home from Home
reviews.text: This is the 3rd time we have stayed at Palms Place and each time we have been upgraded to a one bed suite courtesy of our Expedia+ status. This is basically a 1200 sq ft apartment, modernly fitted out with floor to ceiling windows and everything you could possibly need. If you are staying more than a few days it is certainly an environment where you don't mind spending time in your room, in fact my wife spent more time in the room than in the casino!The distance to the casino itself is a slight pain but if you stay in one of the bigger casino properties chances are you will have even further to walk to get to your tower.Couldn't afford most of the restaurants so just used the buffet and Hooters this time round. The buffet is cheap but not so cheerful. It was better when we used it previously. The Hooters was great - especially if you sat overlooking the pool people-watching. And Kenya, our waitress on a number of occasions, was awesome. $15 for a bucket of 5 beer could not be beat.The blackjack tables didn't take too much money from me and had a good vibe. Managed to play on the $5 minimum table which is a rarity these days in Vegas.The slots were not too harsh either. For the first time ever we came home with some money!Oh, and as a final tip - use Lyft and Uber to get around Vegas. Awesome price and service, especially as Palms Place is off strip.

reviews.title: Our stay at the Fabulous Palms Place!
reviews.text: Where do I start!?!  Too hard to say...  So this review may jump around from area to area.  But trust me...  You want to read what I have to say about this hotel!!!     OK, first of all... These aren't your typical hotel suites. These are more like Palms Living Quarters.  First thing I noticed upon walking into studio suite was the 3 flat screen Tvs in the room. Very nice touch IMO. Then the kitchen area with included a stove top... cabinetry with dishes... Range/microwave... And a dishwasher!  Then there's this area off to the right side of the bedding area.  This was like a carpeted lounging area with a TV... sofa... Chaise lounger... Coffee Table... Sitting chairs, and another smaller table.  All of this is in front of a beautiful floor to ceiling windows.  Then the bedding area...   Hard wood flooring here...  Another TV faces the super comfortable king sized bed. Oh yeah, throughout the room... There's plenty of modernized lighting and lamps(not in the bathroom though. Lots of direct lighting that creates shadows)  OK. Now to MY FAVORITE FEATURE OF THIS HOTEL ROOM!  On the left side of the bedding area is a wall...  A wall made entirely of freakin' Frosted Glass!!!   OK... Let me calm down!(This is the bathroom area behind the glass) On the other side of this glass is the jetted/jacuzzi tub...  Then the separate very spacious glass enclosed shower!  Now let's go into the bathroom area. You'll see to the left separated by a partial glass wall is the business part of the bathroom(toilet.)  immediately in front of you is the sink area with the 3rd TV... Which is also facing the shower/jacuzzi tub.  And to your right, is the shower, and tub area with the wall of Frosted Glass!  OK...  THE MAGIC OF THIS FROSTED GLASS WALL!  On either side of the Frosted Glass...  The closer you get to the glass the better you can be seen on the other side of it.  From not being seen at all... To a silhouette... All the way to being seen perfectly when touching the glass!(No u can't peep through the glass by pressing ur eyes against it)OK... Picture this... You're partner is in the shower.  Now just standing in the shower...  You can't be seen. You'll have to get closer to the Frosted Glass in order to be seen on the other side.  And vice versa if your on the other side(bedding area)This is where the fun begins!   Ur partner could go against the glass and motion for u to join them etc etc.  I'll let you image the possibilities the Frosted Glass pose! ;)   The hotel also houses a nice Swimming pool area...  Spa...  Fitness center too.   Very courteous staff... Easy parking! All the other amenities of most of the Strip hotels as well. There are restaurants... Plus there is a sky walk that connects you to the Palms hotel and Casino(see my Palms Casino Review)As you can tell...  I love this hotel and definitely will be staying here again on my next visit to Las Vegas!

reviews.title: Palms out
reviews.text: Not the service one would expect and certainly overpriced. Basic accommodations are good but I must say they are understaffed at the front desk and overstaffed in other areas. If you use Airbnb you will be paying a la carte for everything. If you don't want to spend $200 per meal then you can go close by for your dinners and lunches. The reservation system is not manned on Sundays? I guess nobody should travel there on Sundays then because they won't find your reservation and you won't be able to check in. Not the best experience we've had.

reviews.title: Don't believe the negative hype
reviews.text: After pouring over reviews here, I prepared for an outdated and dilapidated facility. Was pleasantly surprised to discover a clean and modern hotel with a contemporary, spacious room and master bath in addition to a 5-minute trip to get there via the valet parking and hotel elevator convenience. This is truly a boutique hotel with a moving walkway that gets you to the Palms casino and food court in minutes. Avoiding the long trek through the casino to get to your room is so worth it staying here! FYI, it is tougher to get into Palms pool area than through airport security LOL, seriously.

reviews.title: needs some improvement
reviews.text: We stayed here to attend the Culture Club concert in August.   We paid for a one-bedroom suite.   It was spacious, but needed some improvements.  Some cabinets not closing, chairs needed repairs, sofa pretty warn, lights needed to be adjusted.  The most irritating was the pool.   The Palms pool was pretty small and no loungers available, not much shade.   There were 20 cabanas, with maybe 3 rented, for $100 a day.   The pool bar was sad.   We went over to Palms Casino pool.  They charged an additional $10, which is a rip off since we are already paying a $40 resort fee..

reviews.title: Wow!!!!
reviews.text: A five stars suite just few minutes driving from the strip! The suite was huge, on 38 floor, restroom with shower and jacuzzi, there were 3 TV! The staff of the hotel was super kind. The swimming pool at the 6th floor was amazing, I had really a great stay!

reviews.title: Awesome accommodation for couple's anniversary!
reviews.text: My wife and I stayed at the Palms Place last weekend as part of the celebration of our 5 year anniversary and after informing the assistant hotel manager, Shelby, of the reason for our visit she and the staff there upgraded, free of additional charge, our room to a large suite! It was a very nice room and we were very happy with the view of the strip and all the features of the room. The hotel was not loud or crowded (no long lines) and early check-in was available and easy. The pool was nice at the Palms Place - we hung out there for most of the afternoon.  We went to the main Palms hotel and casino for dinner and entertainment later and it was an easy walk from the Palms Place.  We definitely recommend the Palms Place to others!

reviews.title: Decent Hotel, Horrible Management
reviews.text: After staying at the Palm Place, I would say this is a decent hotel but I would look elsewhere due to the current management. We stayed in the one bedroom suites with a advertised balcony. Upon arrival, we were not helped with our luggage to the room. Actually, another guest helped after the staff stated they were to busy to assist.  When arriving in the room, we realized the balcony was locked. After calling downstairs, we were told that only the penthouse suite had a functioning balcony. So while already disappointed, we inspected the room and saw dirty stained furnature and pillows. We decided that in the future, maybe we would stay at the penthouse suite for a better experience, as we enjoy this location.  When calling downstairs to inquire about a tour, we were told that the current manager on duty would not allow us to do a tour of the penthouse. I asked if that was the hotel policy and was told it was not. It was simply her decision.  Upon conclusion, due to the lack of service upon arrival, dirty stained room and lazy service by manager Shelby, we would say, do yourself a favor and stay elsewhere.

reviews.title: poor maintenance of property
reviews.text: we checked into the palms place resort on Tuesday AUGUST 8.for 3 days,after checking in we discover that the hot water faucet leaked when it was turn on,the chairs were torn like it was a dog or cat paws had ripped the chairs, the chairs were 4 pronged chairs of which one of the chairs prongs were broken making the chair lopsided,th, the carpete refrigerator was filthy, the floors were not clean I complained and spoke to CHRIS the manager said he would move us to a 1 bedroom suite the next day.,when we moved the 1 bedroom was nice BUT AGAIN the small bathroom hot water faucet did not work at all, the main bathroom cold water faucet leaked the carpet was filthy the view would have been nice if you could see out the windows they were very dirty,the bed stands need to be painted spend some money for upkeep it would be a great place to stay, not a BUT all the problems not a great experience. one other thing I found out that those units are privately owned in the palms place.

reviews.title: Party in vegas
reviews.text: I stayed in Vegas for 3 nights and stayed at the palms place. It is a condo/hotel where there are residents as well as guests. We got an upgraded suite when we went for comfort reasons. It was a really nice and modern type of suite that fits a good amount of people... If there are any people around. The one complaint i have about the hotel is that it is a distance away from the main Las Vegas strip. The cost of a taxi to the strip is around $20. It did concern me because i wanted to be near all the happening spots. But if your the type that likes to be a little secluded and have a casino that is not as packed as the Wynn, then i suggest this is the place for you. Just know that the palms place is also an indoor 5 minute walk to the main lobby, casino, food court and pool. However, other than the location, the hotel was very clean and affordable with great service.

reviews.title: Amazing stay
reviews.text: This was our forth time in Vegas. I wish we have stayed here before. This place is amazing. Everything looks new and clean. There are 3 buildings on the property. I was able to get the building which has condo style. So one huge room with sofa and kitchen with it. I loved it. There is a big mirror as back board of the bed. 2 tvs. A fantastic shower and jacuzzi. This is going to be my place in Vegas. This hotel is off the strip but close enough where I was able to see hotels on the strip through my patio window. This place is worth one hundred times. We used Uber to go places, it was reasonable.

reviews.title: Comfy and affordable.
reviews.text: We were looking for a place to stay while celebrating a birthday. Single bedroom suite. Lots of amenities. Very comfortable and affordable. This room includes: full kitchen, mini bar, washer & dryer, dish washer, spa tub, and a fireplace. Nice!

reviews.title: Almost perfect....but
reviews.text: The rooms are beautiful and spacious. The bathroom is fabulous.  Room service is not only reasonable, it is fairly fast. We had a King suite on the 31st floor, giving us a wonderful view of Vegas. A little more attention to maintenance would have made this a 5 star across the board review: bathroom light was burned out; the ice maker in the refrigerator  (there is a full kitchen!!) was inoperable and couldn't be fixed during our stay (they had to bring in a mini fridge and hand deliver ice when needed) AND THE SOFA BED WAS HORRID. Not only was the bedding missing, the mattress - especially when compared to the king mattress - was, maybe, an inch thick and totally broken down. The chaise was far more comfortable. Just didn't expect that. With all that said, we'll still be back...just hopefully won't have the cursed room. Staff is very professional and cheerful. Check in is very quick, and check out is easily done on one of the large flat screens in room.  (2 42" in the sitting room and bedroom...and another smaller screen in the bathroom). Be aware the Palms is actually 2 properties in one. If you want a little more quiet atmosphere, stay here...if you want to be on top of gaming, stay at the Palms Casino.

reviews.title: Four out of Five Stars!
reviews.text: We stayed here a couple of weeks ago and had a really good experience. There were a few things I wish were different but they are minor. Fist the room is very nice and rooms. The bed is sooo comfy! The bathroom...my gosh....where do I begin. I could've just stayed in the bathroom the whole trip and been satisfied. An enormous jetted tub, a rainfall shower, wow!! Easy access to the casino, practically next door to the Rio, overall a great place to stay. A couple things you might want to take into consideration... The pool is only open until 6:00 PM which I was very disappointed about because after a long day I was hoping to come back and lounge by the pool. That was probably by biggest "bummer" about the trip. Also, you have this huge awesome balcony in your room...that you can't use. All locked up! Seems a waste of space and money. I am assuming one person ruined it for everybody at some point in time. Also, they charge you $14.99 to access the wi-fi. Seems a little outdated to me - I mean, who doesn't give free wi-fi these days?? If you don't care about the pool thing then I would highly recommend this as a place to stay. Something way cool also happened......we were waiting for a cab at the hotel and the guy waiting in front of us was none other than Nicholas Cage!!!! BONUS!!

reviews.title: Fair priced luxury!
reviews.text: As part of a 3 week trip to America, we thought it was only fitting to make a three day stop in Vegas. My boyfriend had never been, but I had. We decided to have a look at some self catered apartments on Airbnb, and found a studio on the 37th floor of Palms Place Suites, which worked out a similar price if not cheaper than a lot of the standard double rooms available in the popular strip hotels. Looking at the photographs posted of the beautiful apartment, including the show stopping skyline views from the balcony, along with the impressive facilities the attached Palms hotel had to offer, we were sold, and convinced that this was a steal.And we were right! In fact, the photographs and raving reviews did not do the place justice. The apartment was clean, modern, and immaculate. The views were just out of this world, and it was nice to play the high life for a few days- even better when considering the low price we paid. The facilities of the palms hotel and spa were available free of charge to guests of the suites, and were just a short walk across the sky tube (a moving conveyer) The only thing I would say is that whilst the advertisement of only a 10 minute walk to the main strip is true, the walk is on a pavement along the highway. That being said, it didn't bother us- just maybe something to consider for families etc. However, we found that an uber was only a few dollars. Worth every penny- would stay again on next visit to Vegas!

reviews.title: Eta Phi Beta Boule 2016
reviews.text: I personally am writing on behalf of the awesome housekeeping service that I received during my visit from July 24 - July 30, 2016! Yolanda who cleans the 35th floor was perfection. She was very friendly, courteous, and helpful. She made our stay comfortable and delightful. Everything was cleaned properly daily and she always made sure we knew how to reach her if we needed anything while she was on duty. Even though she has an entire floor to clean, it was great to feel as if we were human to her and not just some people in a room she has to clean. Everything else was great as well. I just wanted to give my appreciation to Yolanda because it is difficult being away from home for a week. She made our stay such a delight. Thanks Yolanda!

reviews.title: Not perfect, but damn near close!
reviews.text: I'm local, I live in Vegas and we do a lot of staycation-ing. This is the first time I stayed at Palms Place. My boyfriend and I chose the studio. There was plenty of room for us, since it was bigger than the average hotel room. The bathroom was very spacious with very soft modern lighting. The studio room came with a bathtub which was a pleasant surprise. I'm finding more and more hotels these days only have tubs in their suites. I like to be able to wash up without getting my hair wet so having a bathtub is ideal. The showerhead two options, a rain shower or a detachable showerhead. You could set the shower to use one or the other, or both at the same time. This room came with a mini bar and also a mini fridge, as well as a kitchen stocked with utensils, dishes and cooking supplies. The bed was very comfortable. Real goose down pillows were a nice touch. There were three TVs and the Palms Place offers plenty of great movies. A short elevator trip down to the sixth floor and we found body heat tanning which was amazing. I was pretty pale when I got here so it was nice to be able to get a Spray tan in the hotel. The spa was basic, but very clean and the service was incredible. The pool was intimate but definitely big enough to accommodate the hotels needs. It was very hot the week we stayed so we didn't spend much time out there. We didn't get a chance to eat at palms place, instead we took the sky tube over to the hotel and ate there. The palms has a nice variety of restaurants. Everything from nine steakhouse to Hooters!  So far this has been my favorite staycation in Vegas. It was definitely convenient to have a fully stocked kitchen in a little condo! I will be back!

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text: The hotel is clean, tidy, and the service was great. It also smelled very good and the rooms were big. It's definitely a great place to stay. Includes a casino, and many very fancy restaurants.  I would really recommend to stay here.

reviews.title: Perfect Couple Getaway Spot
reviews.text: My fiance and I made our first trip ever to Las Vegas and after researching many reviews and looking at other guests videos, we we're attracted to what the Palms had to offer. As parents of four, affordability is priority one and the rates were unbelievably affordable. It was cheaper than places we are used to staying but of better quality. I couldn't believe it. What I loved about it was the location. As first timers it felt great to get away from all the commotion after a day of festivities and drive a few blocks from the strip to our room. This may not be the case for everyone but we are country folk and don't mind staying a short distance from the strip. Guest services were great to deal with. Our room was amazing. We felt like a King and Queen while there. Very modern and up to date. There were two huge flat screens on one wall!! No access to balcony, only the owners of the condos have that pleasure, but I can understand why they would keep them locked. Also what I loved during our week stay there was how surprisingly quiet the halls were. Two of the best features were the California king bed, which was amazingly comfy, and the deep tub. I tried to take a hot bubble bath after being exhausted and I honestly had to get out because I almost passed out from relaxing too much! I didn't think that was possible but it was! Last but not least our view of the mountains was inspiring and beautiful. Overall our room was immaculate! Best decision ever!

reviews.title: I wanted to love it...
reviews.text: I wanted to give this place 5 stars and would have if it wasn't for the absolute rudeness I experienced with the shuttle bus driver and absent of help when speaking with his superiors. I stayed in a studio suite. Room was great with a wonderful view. Bathroom was amazing with full size whirlpool tube and ceiling shower. Comes with a fridge, microwave, stove top, and dishwasher. Desk staff was friendly and helpful. The spa is also nice and there is a restaurant located on this side that saves you the walk over to the casino side. I would stay here again but..,The shuttle drive almost ruined my experience. While waiting at the pickup spot at Caesars for 30 mins, when the shuttle came I attempted to board. However I was told it was full and it would not be returning and my option was to call a cab or sit on someone's (a stranger) lap but I could not sit in the floor or stand. He allowed several people to sit on their significant other's lap but quoted he only had room for 14. There were appox 19 people on that shuttle. Not only did they arrive after to me, they were signaled to come in before me. Anyway, I ended up taking an Uber back to the hotel. I was quoted that this was a complimentary service (included in resort fees) and first come first serve and get in the shuttle before anyone else next time. Just rudeness.

reviews.title: My New Favorite Hotel in Vegas!
reviews.text: I absolutely love this hotel! I stayed there a couple of months ago for the first time and fell in love! It is off of the strip, but it's nice to be away from all of the craziness of the strip and it's totally worth the five minute drive for the lux-ness of the hotel. The hotel and the rooms are all so luxurious and very spacous. The furniture and fixtures were so high quality and the friendliness and helpfulness of the staff was out of this world. The pool was also very calm for it being the start of summer, which was a nice break from all of the high energy pool parties The Palms is known for.  And all of the was at an amazing price.

reviews.title: Nice hotel but had maintenance issues
reviews.text: 3.5 Stars. This review is based on my visit back in October.I normally stay at the strip but thought I tried something new. I arrived at the hotel too early around noon but the agent offered me a mountain view since these rooms were available before normal check in. The strip view rooms will be ready at 3 so I decided just wait. You can leave your luggage with the bell staff so that's exactly what I did while I explored the surroundings. This building is connected to Palms Hotel Casino via moving skywalk. There's plenty free of parking outside and indoor garage.My room was pretty enormous. 2 LCD tvs (one in front of bed & one for the living area), nice comfy king bed, separate sitting area, writing desk, modern artsy lighting fixtures, fully equipped kitchen w/ mini bar, 3 spacious closets, jet tub, rain shower and another small tv in bathroom vanity.The room was clean but floors were a little dusty. One of the TVs didn't power at all and I called front desk, maintenance came but they were not able to fix it. I also called about 2 lamps fixtures in the living room that had bulbs out but they also didn't fix them. There was a decent size balcony but only permanent residents can unlock the sliding door. The front desk told me that hotel guest were not allowed on the balcony...maybe for safety reasons but that's a lame excuse. Internet was a little challenging to connect and allowed only certain amount of data access which was weird. If I wanted more data, then I have to pay extra on top of the daily resort fee. On my last day, one of the shower handles came off loose (see pic) but I didn't bother calling the front desk about it cause I was checking out.Overall, it was nice comfortable stay. This hotel was modern and had nice amenities. I just think housekeeping or maintenance should be inspecting rooms thoroughly before guest arrives. This hotel being off the strip, for the price I paid & minor kinks, I'd rather stay at the strip and pay a bit more for a smaller modern room.

reviews.title: Great Stay all around--overall LOW KEY, low intensity
reviews.text: Check in/staff:  We had a late check in...front desk was super nice, we felt welcome right away...in fact throughout our stay all the staff we encountered were great...front desk also offerered us a late check-out, at check in. Room:  Really nice, comfy bed, comfy pillows, quiet, we were on 36th floor, hallways were quiet, no noisy neighbors.  Room and Kitchenette were clean, fridge, ice in freezer, glassware, dishes, etc...Bathroom was lovely...rain shower and beautiful whirlpool tub, plenty of room for 2, marble floors and walls, makeup mirror, etc.  Couch, great view...sliding door, but were unable to go outside on the balcony. --I was concerned about other reviews of this hotel being 'tired'...we didn't find that at all.  Room was in good repair, updated, felt 'new'.Pool:  as another reviewer stated it closed at 6.  I found Las Vegas in general to be a place of little peace and rest...it seems all nuances are pushing folks to go, go, go...I would have LOVED a late night swim under the lights/stars...not an option.  ON the upside, The Palms Place pool was very low key...during the day it was peaceful, ice water available for guests, a little crowded with chairs, and most of the options for seating had 'reserved' signs on them, yet were empty.  Pool bar and seating area.  The crowd was quiet and mostly sparse (I think the party was over at the Palms Pool), could have used a lowering of the volume on the constant POP music, always playing everywhere.  No real complaints though.Spa:  HIGHLIGHT of my stay was the Drift Spa...massage from Steven was excellent, and the Hammam was lovely.  Downside is that after I paid for services I saw a discount in my room for just about the same service, for $40 less...so look in your room before you book...and why wasn't a spa menu in the guest room anyway???  I was able to get a same day massage appointment, but had to search out a menu, etc.Location:  Just West of the strip.  Good and bad...they have a shuttle to and from Cesar's on the strip, it stops running at 8pm...after that I highly recommend UBER and avoiding cabs (bad cab experience).  Nice because it's away from the chaos, but if you want to be 'where the action is', its not a short walk...(although we did walk it the first night we were there, don't recommend this)...so you'll need transport, not a real problem for us...compared to the chaos, it was nice to land in a calmer place.Also it connects to the Palms...so you are close to more 'stuff', but it's peaceful (for Vegas) and low key...which was a HUGE plus for us.Grounds:  In general I did not find a nice, outdoor place to just chill...or any covered area, with chairs just to 'be'...but if you need a break from lights, pop music and noise...go to your room, or go home, or rent a car and drive to the desert?Dining: Nothing in Palms place, but a short walk through a connecting sky tube, and there is eveything from a food court to Hooters, to fine dining to a pass-able, reasonable buffet. Room service was 24/7, and fairly priced for room service. (Eggs benedict $14, Steak and Eggs $18).Casino/nightlife:  Palms casino, across the skytube...a smaller casino, low key, we found the odds pretty good for us, low intensity, but enough going on to keep you occupied.  Plenty of bars and liquor flowing.  Didn't have time for the ghostbar, but would have liked to have wandered up there...No City guide in room, first hotel I've ever been in without one...as first times we could have used it...sometimes it's just quicker than google.

reviews.title: Extremely Disappointing!
reviews.text: My first room was disgustingly dirty. There were clumps of hair all over the bathroom floor. Dirt and dust all over the kitchen and entry floors. No way had  the floors been cleaned recently. Ewww. Elevator reeked of marijuana. Ewwww. Second room reeked of cigarettes. Ewwww. Third room was a suite. The basic rooms are actually nicer and more updated. The suite, while very large with a nice panoramic view was in ROUGH shape - I would have been embarrassed to actually put someone in here if I were the management. The furniture was well beyond its life, most of the walls were badly scraped, kitchen counters and sinks scratched, carpets frayed. TV remotes disgusting. Balconies locked with no furniture on them. Just empty barren wasted space. Ewwww. Decor was out of a cheesy brothel (e.g. pink neon light bulbs in lamps and black furniture). Food in mini bar was stale and had likely been there for years. Will be asking for my money back on two melted and disintegrating Snickers bars. ??!! Freezer next to ice tray had some black substance in it. Ewwww. I can't sleep because I feel like this room is also not clean. I will be checking out tomorrow and going to Mandalay Bay. Nothing fancy, but at least it's clean. No excuse for a hotel room to be so poorly maintained, especially in Vegas, the mecca of hospitality management! They should know that running a hotel requires general upkeep and maintenance. It's sadly obvious that no money is put into maintaining the rooms AT ALL. All I wanted was a clean room where I could comfortably relax. Total fail on the most basic stuff. Everywhere else is a better bet.

reviews.title: Second time around--still wonderful
reviews.text: I stayed at the Palms place two years ago and I came back with a little trepidation, having read negative reviews. Well my fears were inconsequential because my stay at the Palms Place was GREAT on every level. Beau and Christine were so nice at the front desk and concierge desk and I had a gorgeous studio on the 52nd floor with strip view. The place was spotless and very well maintained. I enjoyed the quiet and peaceful scene at the Palms pool during the week. The Ditch Friday party was CRAZY but a lot of fun. I enjoyed the convenience of the Food court. The $5 Monday movie was great at the Palms cinema. The shuttle was great and the shuttle driver was so nice. I really love the vibe at both the Palms and Palms place. I also travelled all over Las Vegas and a ton of fun. I only wish there were more concerts at the Pearl and more music around the bars, casino etc. I looked forward to coming back again. Thanks to everyone for a great and much needed vacation.

reviews.title: Pool and spa close at 5?!!!!
reviews.text: After a longer drive and 103 degree weather, I was looking forward to relaxing by the pool.  We arrived at 6:30pm only to find the pool and spa close at 5pm.  I have never stayed at a hotel where the pool closes at 5.  Upon first impressions, the rooms are nice, and modern with kitchenettes, but the hotel is starting to show some wear, seats are getting ratty, couches have stains.  Outdoor patio has no furniture.  Our room also lacked toiletries and had a wad of hair left in the shower drain.  They took care of it when we called housekeeping.  My husband and I were returning from hosting a memorial for my father and had been exhausted from closing down his apartment and wanted to relax and have a nice night before heading home.  It was disappointing having to address more issues.  I realize it's not a 5 star hotel, but the common areas could be better maintained.  The large glass windows that face the pool from the snack bar haven't been cleaned in a long time.  Perhaps when it first opened, it was grand and beautiful but the failure to pay attention to details is leading the hotel to slide.  We are enjoying a beautiful view though.  Paying the high resort fee and not having a chance to use the pool or spa is very disappointing.

reviews.title: 2.5 Stars - Nice property that is neglected
reviews.text: I usually stay at Wynn or Venetian. I tried this place as I just needed a night and has no time for gambling. Pros:Check-in was easy (as there are not that many people) as well as the parkingNice size rooms. Cons:1. 5$ for wine opener, really??? I called the front desk for a wine opener and was told it would cost 5$. That's a shame. 2. Away from the strip and you don't get the Vegas feeling. Not a whole lot of dining options. 3. old and damaged furniture. scratched my leg because of the furniture strip sticking out. potential law suit right there but the property lucked out as I am not a lawyer and have not time for it :)I don't recommend this property, for the same price (may be 20-30 more) you can get a better hotels on the strip.

reviews.title: Great place to stay
reviews.text: This hotel was amazing!!!   The entire staff is friendly and helpful, especially the concierge Christine Smith.  I had a million questions and she had a million answers.  I am impressed and that doesn't happen often.

reviews.title: Very good first time experience
reviews.text: I was looking online at different hotels and came across this hotel.What sold me was how relaxing it looked since it was off the strip. On their website the photos looked beautiful and the rooms look great and after seeing the prices for a room I went ahead and booked the room. Of course I decide to read reviews after booking the rooms on Trip Advisor and Yelp and  had seen some good reviews and some bad...like every hotel out there. But what stood out the most was that the rooms seemed to be very beat up, with broken furniture, ripped furniture and stains on the walls and balcony's that we did not have access to and were locked. Balconys...not a big deal for me. I was a little hesitant after seeing photos of the rooms, being it was my first trip with my significant other i wanted to have a pleasant stay in a nice room. We arrived to a very calm and relaxing lobby. Very classy and zen (lol) kind of dark though. The front desk assistant manager checked us in and he was nice. Didn't really speak with anyone else that worked there besides the bellman when we left. Our room was on the 27th floor and our room turned out to be perfect! Had a view of the mountains which was not bad at all. SOME dings,wear and tear here and there but nothing that would ruin your stay at all. It wasn't very noticeable unless you really looked for a problem lol.There was a skytube to the Palms Casino which was cool and convenient but really long walk. Overall i would stay there again. It was a nice hotel to relax and be away from the craziness of the strip.

reviews.title: Fantastic rooms
reviews.text: Palms Place caught our attention because of the good rates offered through various websites. Rooms are huge and have everything. Wifi is at a charge which is so 2005. Come on guys: just offer it to your guests! Pool on 6th floor is nice yet a little small perhaps. Loungers at pool are comfy. All in all a good place to stay if you do not mind being approx half a mile from the strip.

reviews.title: Wont recommend
reviews.text: Start was horrible.Me and my wife were coming from different cities ,she reached  hotel 2 hours before me,reception staff didnt let her check in even though her name was on guest list and the amount was fully paid.They seemed very unprofessional and were not able to explain that why they did not allow her.We were tired and decided to leave the arguement and check in..When entered our room the first thing we saw was a broken table from which a metal rod was coming out and was very unsafe and could really hurt someone seriously..We complained a few timed but the staff did not take any action

reviews.title: An Okay Stay
reviews.text: The price for the hotel room was fair, but then they tack on an additional $30 "resort fee" what that includes I do not know. The room was relatively clean when we entered. The shower was horrible, less than 5 minutes into my shower the drain began to bubble up with old water and hair that was not from me. The shower would not drain at all. The resort was called, they said that they would send someone up right away to take care of it while we went to a show. The next morning I went to take a shower and found that the shower was never looked and all the same issues were still present. The 24/7 cafe had dirty tables and the menus were plastered with food. I plan to comeback to Vegas, but I will not choose this hotel again.

reviews.title: Incredible views, sensational staff!
reviews.text: One bedroom suite spacious and soooo modern! Stayed last year here also and was the reason we came back. Wife loves spa, pool large and quiet, people so nice. Yes it is a few minutes from the strip but we found that part of it's greatness. We'll be back next year! All the mod cons for business or family travelers (we are both! who isn't these days?!) ... staff all friendly and security is tight which makes us all feel better these days.

reviews.title: It's OK
reviews.text: It was a very nice room, very nice hotel, the best view in town, very luxurious we love it. But the service was poor, nothing special. I would expect a better customer service in this kind of hotel, but it was the same as staying at a cheaper one. You can find pretty hotels everywhere but good service is what makes me want to come back.

reviews.title: Great Base
reviews.text: Our room 38308 on the 38th floor was in UK terms excellent, I'm sure that American visitors would point out the slight wear on some pieces of furniture but for my wife and I it was ideal. The view over looking the strip was superb; especially at night with all the lights.The Palms Place is one of 3 accommodation towers and the furthest from the casino area but for us that was a positive, we could get away from the hullabaloo and sun bathe at the 6th floor pool area, we found the staff both friendly and helpful without being overbearing.

reviews.title: Great service from Christine from the concierge team
reviews.text: I asked the concierge team for a number of requests at short notice, including car rental, dinner booking and tickets for a show, and Christine stepped in, leaving a meeting she was in at the time, and provided perfect service.  Thanks.

reviews.title: Palms Place needs an update.
reviews.text: Spent 2 nights at Palms Place at the end of May, 2016.2nd time at the hotel.The first time was awesome.This last time was...meh...ok at best.While the rooms are nice, they are beginning to show their age.Scratches on a lot of the furniture.And the style is looking a little...dated.The Jacuzzi tub was awesome.The shower is damn nice.But, the look of the room now seems pretty cheesy. Still awesome service.Quiet. Away from the Casino, which never had a Bacarrat table open while I was there, which sucked, because that's what I play.At one point a few yrs ago, I would call this a 4 star. Not now.Furniture was to "used" and dated looking.Other than thatThe rates are good and I'd recommend it.For $59 its worth it for the 2 person Jacuzzi in the room...

reviews.title: Wish we could have stayed longer!
reviews.text: We found a great deal for our one-night stay in Vegas at the Palms Casino Resort. When we checked in at the Palms Casino, they gave us a room here at the Palms Palace instead and for the deal we received, we didn't fuss too much about having to move to the other tower. The Palms Place is a short walk through the parking lot from the casino. There is no indoor walkway from the casino. They have their own front desk and valet entrance. Our suite was sweet! We have a king bed, roomy living area, modern kitchen and large desk. Our bathroom was not as roomy, but it was clean and comfortable. The shower is an "area" on the way into the deep bathtub. Our room was on a high floor so the views of the city was a nice treat for our short stay.I requested a laundry bag and when it didn't arrive after 20 minutes, I called housekeeping back and spoke to the same person I originally placed the request with. She told me there's a fee for the laundry bag so it wasn't sent up. I wish I would've been told this on my first call. The error was corrected by giving me the laundry bag free of charge, but it never came and we had to leave. Moving on.

reviews.title: Deferred Maintenance Rules
reviews.text: Upgraded to a corner suite on arrival.  This place could be spectacular, but the spacious room was completely worn out.  Loose wood flooring, banged up stainless steel kitchen, chipped paint, smelly carpets, locked balconies, frayed artwork, non-working TV......the list goes on.  Other reviews cover the deficiencies in detail.  That being said, we made the best of the amazing view and ended up enjoying ourselves.  Parking is easy. The pool looked decent, although small and crowded midday.  Staff was friendly.  I've been told Red Rock Resorts now owns the property, hopefully they'll upgrade.

reviews.title: Perfect place for a family.
reviews.text: My 16th trip to Vegas. Stayed 5 nights. The last couple of years we've stayed at TheHotel/Delano as we now have kids. Decided to try Palms Place as it was a suite layout and it was a non-casino Hotel. The experience was great. The location is lined up to the centre of the strip so it was very convenient to get to any location up and down the Strip by Arville without getting stuck in traffic. Being a 2 minute drive from all the wonderful restaurants on Spring Mountain Road is a definite plus. We saw MJ One and MJ Live which were located on the two ends of the strip so being lined up with centre strip made it an easy drive. Parking was easy to access right outside the Hotel without having to go trek into a parking garage like the strip casinos. The Palms Casino was easily accessable by walking the skytube. It was nice to have a food court and theatre so close for the kids. The kids were able to go to The Palms day club pool Mon-Thurs along with the Palms Place pool. The suite was nice and having a kitchenette was great. The view was spectacular! It is a hotel with a younger clientele and had a nice energy to it. Somehow buffet charges were made to our room which we didn't incur but the front desk took care of it. We will definitely be back and would recommend it to young couples or young families. The layout and accessibility to the pool, gym/spa, parking is better than any strip resort. There's no smoke issues and everything was clean and pristine. You also get the peace and quiet of a boutique hotel with just a 5 minute walk to the excitement of main Palms Casino. This was the best view of the strip we've ever had. Some nights my wife and kids would just shut the lights off and enjoy the view of the strip.

reviews.title: The Non-smoking policy does not apply
reviews.text: This business uses tools provided by Tripadvisor (or one of its official Review Collection Partners) to encourage and collect guest reviews, including this one.

reviews.title: This can't be Palms Place...
reviews.text: I'm a local so I hear a lot of great things about the Palms. So when a friend invited me up to her Palm's Place room on the 35th floor I jumped at the chance to see what Palms Place had to offer.At first glance the room is spacious with a nice looking kitchenette and huge bathroom a living area and a nice sized bedroom.But then things started to pop out at me. For example the art work that had a corner peeling up, then filthy windows that had smudges from dozens of people. The carpet that was pulling up in places. The freezer that wouldn't stay shut, we actually had to put a chair in front of it.Then we noticed no cooking utensils.. (though from reading other reviews and calling to the desk (thinking someone stole it all) it is provided on request. Not a big deal, a little inconvenient but not a deal breaker.The interesting part was the room had a wrap around balcony. The bad thing was the doors were locked and there was no way outside to enjoy the view. We called downstairs and they said for safety issues the doors are kept locked. Well from the cigarette butts and the smeared glass outside.. someone was out there enjoying themselves. If they aren't going to let people out there, why is it so dirty? And why hasn't anyone thought of cleaning it?I have friends that work at the Palms and they love the place, they love their jobs so I was so distraught to see this room in such disarray. It just looks like the room was let go... I hope that this was just a bad experience and not a taste of what the Palms Rooms look like.For the price of the room and location, (they didn't even have free wi-fi) t am sad to say there are better options in Las Vegas. But I hope this experience was just a fluke...

reviews.title: 1st Timer 😊
reviews.text: Upon arriving at the hotel it took forever to check-in. I visited on the busy Memorial Day Weekend & they audaciously only had 1 person at the counter. After 30 minutes, I finally made it to my room, the studio suite. Romo was gorgeous & spacious. The staff is very friendly. The cafe 6 has great salmon & salads. It doesn't take long to walk over to the Palms Casino. When I wanted to get the the strip, it only took about 6 minutes in the Uber. The ride cost about $7 if there isn't a surge happening. I overall enjoyed my stay & definitely will return.

reviews.title: Palms Casino Resort
reviews.text: I just visited Las Vegas and stayed here for three nights.  I will start with the room.  We stayed in the Palms Place building which is a hike from the main hotel and casino.  The room was a studio suite and very nice.  Quite large and comfortable.  A kitchen with no cups, utensils or plates.  Had to call and ask for them.  The bathroom was large and modern.  The shower was awesome.  Had the regular shower head and the rain shower head.  Two tvs and a sofa.  All in all the room was nice.  There was a pool on the 6th floor of this hotel and I liked it a lot.  Smaller than the main one but with a bar and bathrooms.  And free!  The main pool was big with lots of people wanting to be seen and if you get there after 12pm, it was $10.  Crazy.  Drinks were very expensive so we didn't get any at the pool.  I was not impressed with the casino.  It wasn't as big and as nice as the ones on the strip in my opinion.  The cocktail waitresses did not come around very often.  I didn't gamble there too much so can't make a comment on the payouts.There were many dining options.  We ate at the Chinese restaurant and Hooters and they were both good and had good customer service.  We ate lunch in the food court.  That was a good option to save money.  We would Uber to the strip and it was fast and affordable so it wasn't a big deal being off the strip and their shuttle to and from Caesars ran until 8pm and we used that once also.  Las Vegas has become very expensive.  That is not this hotels fault, just an observation.  I remember when it was more affordable. You will spend a lot of money here.The Palms is a nice place all in all but I would probably stay on the strip next time so I can just walk from casino to casino and be in the middle of all the action!

reviews.title: Wow
reviews.text: I usually always stay at MGM properties, but this time a friend of mine wants to stay here. So to make things easy I booked my room here as well, wow! I am so surprised. The room is so nice, BIG. I love the room smell, the living room area and the balcony. I am sold now and will stay here from now on. Plus the price is really nice! $60 per night. This is call value.

reviews.title: Save your money
reviews.text: Waited 25 minutes for the pool to open......chronically late employee, then there were no towelsTV and remotes work poorlyEntrance looks like the back door of other hotelsStaff........not very interested in guestsWay over priced for VegasKitchenette, but no pots,pans,or utensils,   Dah

reviews.title: Pleasantly Surprised
reviews.text: Visited 16th-22nd May.Having booked our holiday as a package with flights and accommodation combined and for a good price we were a little worried that the accommodation would not be up to its 5 star rating.Being a 20min walk off the strip this didn't bother us and it's only a $5-7 Uber (cheaper than Vegas taxis) if you don't want to walk. Ubers were great by the way, loads of them around and pretty reasonable. We arrived at the hotel around 3pm for check in which was quick and easy however be warned about resort fees!! I think we were $210 for the week, all hotels have this few I believe, which seems a bit of a con to me but we figured we were not paying much for the hotel in the first place so didn't kick up a fuss. We asked for a strip view room, instead of mountain view, and were duly obliged. On the 27th floor, about half way up we had a good view of the strip from our room. It was very clean upon entry and large. Nice marble flooring in the initial hallway which extends into the bathroom which has a large walk in shower with a jacuzzi tub big enough for 2!! 1 sink and large walled mirror and toilet just off, but with no door on the toilet which is a tad strange. There is a small kitchenette area before the bedroom with a sink, dishwasher and microwave. No oven or hob. Plates, cutlery and glasses can be acquired from reception at no extra fee thankfully.The bed is huge, I think a super king sized one, and also the most comfortable I have ever slept on. Sheets were clean and changed every second day. Rooms were cleaned every day if desired. Plenty of space for clothes and storing suitcases too. Also a large wall mounted TV at the end of the bed.There is also a nice living area at the end of the studio room with a L shaped sofa and another wall mounted TV in this area, literally feet away from the other one which seems a bit unnecessary.The only downside to the room is that you cannot get access to the balcony as the sliding window doors are permanently locked, which means the outside balcony looks quite dirty which spoils the view slightly. Overall I thought the rooms were great and the hotel wasn't a usually fancy Vegas one, the building is separate to the main casino building so a bit quieter. There is a skywalk with travelators to get between to the two meaning you don't need to go outside. There was also a pool at the casino resort which was quite good and also a quieter pool at palms place building. There was nothing I would complain about in this hotel other than the lack of places to eat but mostly you head out to the strip for that. We enjoyed our week in Vegas and the hotel accommodation was a pleasant surprise to us. 5 star quality but maybe 4 star service.

reviews.title: Beautiful and Accomodating
reviews.text: I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at Palms Place.  The studio unit was just perfect.  It was clean, spacious and room service/housekeeping were both fantastic!  It was an easy phone call to get all kitchen utensils.I was also able to check in early without any problem.  Always a bonus after hours of traveling!The location of the resort is wonderful, just across the bridge onto the strip.  The pool is quaint and charming.  I'm looking forward to returning to Vegas and booking this same studio unit with Hoteltron.com

reviews.title: ONE OF THE WORST HOTELS I EVER STAYED AT
reviews.text: We booked three rooms. One of the three rooms was not available until 11 p.m. because "housekeeping" did not have the room ready. We finally got into the room after 11 p.m. and we discovered that the toilet did not work. They sent someone up who tried to fix it but it didn't work. The next day I asked to speak to the manager. He/she couldn't be bothered with me and sent an "assistant manager" out instead after a few minutes. They said that it couldn't be fixed (I wonder if they knew about before we checked in and that is why it wasn't ready) and gave us another room and offer a whopping $30.00 credit for a room that didn't have a working toilet. That was insulting.We had another problem the second of our three rooms, That room had an odor like a sewer. Again, we called down and they supposedly sent someone up. The odor did not go away and they had to switch that room too. Even a staff member (who will remain nameless) said that they didn't know how we could stay in the room with that odor.We also had an issue with a hair dryer that was sparking. We went to the front desk to ask for a new one. They refused to take back the sparking blow dryer and said that engineering had to look at it. They sent someone up to our room and even he was confused as to why he was there since he said housekeeping should replace it.We also had other issues which were minor: (1) Not having the coffee refilled by housekeeping (2) shampoo bottles that we nearly empty and (3) no sponge in one of the rooms.The rooms were nice and have potential. It is the management that is lacking and not responsive. I did not get the impression that they even cared about the issues in the room. The Palms Place appears to be a  condo. People buy them and the Palms "manages" (I use that term loosely) the condos for the owners which are then used as "hotel" rooms. Maybe this is why the management doesn't seem to care.I have stayed in many hotels in the US, Canada and Europe and this would have to been one of my worse experiences. I would not go back to this "hotel" since the condition of the room is a gamble and the management doesn't seem to care.

reviews.title: Bachelor party
reviews.text: I just visited Las Vegas for my bachelor party and stayed at Palms Place at The Palms Resort and Casino. Overall it was a good experience however the suite did not completely live up to expectations. I stayed in the 2-bedroom suite. There were 2 large balconies that we were looking forward to using, but withhout anyone letting us know we found out that they were inaccessible! One of the televisions did not work until an engineer came up to fix it. I also called the hotel ahead of our trip to verify that our suite had some sort of sound system or radio for the bachelor party and I was assured that there was. After finding that out I did not bring my wireless speaker. We showed up to a broken i home and no other options! The entertainment and food at the resort was AMAZING! He gaming and service were also highlights. If you are going for a fun weekend or bachelor/bachelorette party I would recommend n9ne steakhouse, Ghostbar, and Ditch Friday's(pool party). Once again overall it was a good experience. Although since I stayed OFF THE STRIP I was expecting nearly flawless and there were definitely flaws!

reviews.title: Poor customer experience, won't ever return
reviews.text: The rooms in general were nice here, very large, but the overall experience of the hotel was a disappointment. Not only did they close the pool at 4pm, well before sunset, we had massive attitude from the lifeguard when we got there at 3:45 immediately after checking in for the one afternoon we would have there. The spotty and clunky wifi was limited to a single device per room...I haven't experienced this in even cheap hotels in the last five years, when we had a package arrive the front desk said we needed to come down and carry it up because they were short staffed and when we checked out we had a $30 "resort fee" added onto our bill on top of other taxes and fees that was not disclosed at any point before. Quite rich in a place where we specifically felt like every nice bonus you expect in a hotel of this calibre was non-existent or not open for us to enjoy. Also be aware if you want to pop in and out of the strip easily, even though this hotel is close, a major highway sitting in between makes it almost impossible to walk.

reviews.title: Not your average Vegas Hotel!
reviews.text: Check In was easy. Pool gorgeous. All Palm Place guests have full access to the palm Casino and Pool. Shuttle to Caeser's Palace Shops was prompt, comfortable and in a luxury air-conditioned Mercedes van. A nice dark safe ride. I waited a bit during rush hour to check out but they were nice and accommodating. This place is No smoking so it was nice not to have to deal with that smell. No icky Casino vibes, Palms Casino is elegant and clean. It's a great place to gamble and enjoy yourself. Casino is a short walk through the walkway. I liked Palm's Place a lot because of the large rooms. Fridge was great and available for personal Items. Bathroom was gorgeous. I like large bathrooms with amenities and this place has it. Spa was a $25 fee. I LOVED the steam room with Eucalyptus! Whirlpool large. And the co-ed steam room (The Hannanum) was nice too. Very shiek. Very relaxing. Liked the spa period. Worth every penny. The whole spa was well done. I felt very comfortable there and I am picky about this stuff. I don't like smelly or places that can be germ breeding grounds. Spas are wet and they can be but the staff at the spa was present and on top of everything - temperature of saunas, towel service, and overall cleanliness. I am checking out other places to stay next time. But I am tempted to revisit and rebook the Palms Place. I stayed in the Studio Suite high up on one of the upper floors. It was quiet. i never heard so much as a whisper any time I was in my room. Yes the balcony is locked, sigh, but I managed. The view was gorgeous regardless. Television worked well. Bathroom tub was cracked all around. they should get the contractor that did those tubs to re-do all of them, it seems to be mentioned in a lot of reviews. Overall Palms Place gave me exactly what I wanted a sense of luxury, a room with a view, a decent spa experience, good food (when I did not want to leave the hotel) Access to the strip but tastefully removed from the chaos. Cafe 6 was not an extensive menu, but I liked what I ordered (kale caeser salad and sliders). The bartenders know how to make good drinks. Rojo is a nice lounge spot for a drink. Everything is visually appealing. Did not love the pool bar. Something was not quite right there. Needs some life, some music, something. It was like a ghetto corner of the place. Extensive beer menu in Cafe 6 not available at Pool Bar.. BOO!! Prices were way over the top for the size of the drinks coming out of pool bar. Did not like that. I like my pool staff to be a little more attentive and not be wearing bikini up the butt while serving me. Sorry there is fine line when handling food and drinks and walking around in a skimpy bikini. Wear a sarong at least girl. Not hating just think for a classy place the staff pool attire needs a make-over. They also gave plastic fork to eat my salad out there. Eek!Overall I loved Palms Place. And I will be back.

reviews.title: Nice overnight room
reviews.text: The room at Palms Place was nice and big.  We had a great view of the strip from a high floor.  There was a kitchen with gourmet appliances, Refrigerator, dishwasher stove and microwave.The bathroom had a jacuzzi bathtub that was huge!! There was a raintree shower upon entering and exiting the tub.  Roomy vanity area and a separate water closet made it very convenient for couples and families to be able to use.There is a walkover to the Palms Casino, which a a little long, but there is a moving sidewalk for a portion of it and it is covered so you can remain cool in the summer and warm during the winter months.  That is the one downside, the distance to the eating facilities and casino, although there was a place to eat at Palm Place. I would definitely stay there again.

reviews.title: Home away from home
reviews.text: Palms place is a hotel that makes u feel like your at home with expensive taste and amenities! I love the staff and how they catered to my needs. I love the rooms, full kitchen and wonderful views of vegas!!! I loveeeee stay here! I had the 2 bedroom penthouse with the pool on the balcony. I felt like the President.

reviews.title: 1 night stay at The Palms
reviews.text: My boyfriend and I stayed for one night at The Palms, in 'The Place', which is the residential tower without the casino. This doesn't make a difference because there is a simple indoor walkway between The Place tower and the Casino tower. Being located off the Strip the hotel offer a shuttle service to and from. - we didn't use this but they told us about when we checked in. The room was massive with a 'L' shaped sofa, big comfy bed and 2 TV's as well as a big bathroom.  The hotel had loads of restaurants; both fast food and fine dining as well as plenty of other things such as a cinema. We went to the pool based in the residential tower and it was really nice with great music being played.The main reason for staying at the hotel was so we could go to the Ghost Bar. It has the most incredible view of the strip at night. It was happy hour between 8pm and 10pm so we went up early so we could get 50% off drinks and photos without other people in the way! I would recommend this hotel, however having stayed on the strip I would recommend staying on the strip due to location or do what we did and have the best of both worlds; one night off the strip and three nights on the strip!

reviews.title: Over the top kindness!
reviews.text: I booked and paid for a trip to Vegas through a fraudulent vacation rentals company. Cascadevacationrentals.com.We arrive at the Palm's place with or fraudulent paper work. The front desk associate Thedda Eslava  could not find or reservation, because I got scammed. She took my cell number, gave us pool keys until she could figure out where are reservation was. She called me back and told me I was scammed. We returned to the front desk where Thedda greeted us with a smile. She informed us that it was indeed a fraudulent company. Before I could ask what we could we do she offered us a comparable suite at about the same rate. She made a bad situation a good one!! Thank you for your excellent service and kind heart. All the staff we interacted with at the Palms were nothing but pleasant and helpful! We will be back and tell everyone! Thank you again Thedda!!

reviews.title: Stylish Modern Suites and away from the Strip
reviews.text: Lovely spacious suites with decent kitchen, nice bathroom with huge tub, twin flat screen TVs, everything you need for a self contained stay.The Palms Place tower is away from the resort and casino so is nice and quiet, the Palms Place resort is busier and has the pools etc, so choose which tower you prefer.The whole complex is about a mile from the Strip and if that suits you it's a perfect place to stay away from the madness.Excellent value, friendly and helpful staff.

reviews.title: A surprisingly great location off the strip.
reviews.text: This was my first time staying at The Palms property and I had found a deal online that made Palms Place, the property's upgraded tower, very affordable.As you approach the tower you immediately realize they've created a place where you're close enough to the action to be apart of it, while at the same time having the option to seclude yourself in an environment that's far more calm and relaxing than the main property. The suite was built in a condo style with a spacious living area, full kitchen, and a large bathroom that sported a Jacuzzi tube and shower with a Swedish shower option. The suite was kept very clean and well maintained and the view from the 31st floor was amazing. There was a balcony but it was not accessible as the sliding door did not open (normal in Vegas hotels). The staff was very polite and helpful. The spa & gym facilities were very nice and easily accessible. The pool area at Palms Place was separate from the pool at The Palms. Smaller, more intimate, more of a relaxing environment than a party pool. But if a party is what you're looking for you have access to The Palms pool too. My stay was a great experience and I'd definitely stay there again.

reviews.title: What a great hotel!
reviews.text: Stayed there for a week! On the 42nd floor! Amazing view! The great thing about this hotel is that it takes you 10 minutes to check in and you're in your room 5 minutes later where as it can take you up to 2 hours to any hotels on The Strip. Like any hotels food is not cheap! But there's a lovely bagel place right next door to the hotel called Einstein Bagels. We went there every day! The pool is small but perfect for a morning swim. The hotel is about 20 minute walk from The Strip but I hired a car for a week as we wanted to explore. Driving is super easy and all hotels have free parking!

reviews.title: Incredible
reviews.text: We upgraded to a 1200 square foot suite and it was worth every penny!  What an amazing room on the 31 floor overlooking the Strip.  The suite has 1 1/2 bathrooms, a beautiful gourmet kitchen with a fridge, cook top, microwave and dishwasher.  Floor to ceiling windows, fireplace and air tub in the bedroom. The decor and furniture is modern and comfortable.

reviews.title: Great Spot
reviews.text: I visit Vegas annually with the fellas for NFL action and stay at a different hotel each time. We got a smoking good deal at this hotel and it was too good to pass up. You pretty much are staying at The Palms. When checking in we were able to upgrade to a really nice suite. Great way to set off my trip. It was a very nice room. Even though it was off the trip, it was worth it. I wasn't too thrilled with the pool area, but that's it. No casino, but that didn't matter as you literally are just a short walk through the parking lot to The Palms.

reviews.title: Best Hotel off the Strip
reviews.text: Best Luxury hotel for anything off the stripHotel Itself: Clean, luxury, no casino. These were suppose to be condo's but they converted them into hotel rooms. Very Modern, sleek and worth the price. Dont confuse this with Palms Hotel. This is this the Palms PLACE Hotel.Rooms: Some of the best. It rivals Aria, Cosmo and yes, even Hard Rock. Clean, modern, sleek, and the beds are amazing. Good view of the strip tooService: couldn't ask for anything betterRoom Service: Top notchWould I stay her again? - I travel to Vegas twice a month, I always stay here because I want piece and quiet and I like the luxury qualityDownfalls - you need to uber/lyft/taxi to the strip... which only takes a few minutes.

reviews.title: 1975 Concert Weekend
reviews.text: Resort fee high for the property but the biggest issue were the elevators, completely inadequate to service to the building. Always waiting, forever, no matter what time of day. The in room coffee service was a one cup machine.

reviews.title: NEVER again - dont do it!
reviews.text: Just like the previous customer we arrived having travelled 25 hours to be told our room had been cancelled by "an unknown third party" and there were no rooms available. they gave us a room in the Ivory towers - no kitchenette- at an EXTRA cost of 300$ We were exhausted and it was 2am back home so couldnt contact our travel agent. Room was booked in Feb. Travel agent fixed it eventually today. Reception advised us to stay where we were - however we needed a fridge thats why we booked the original room. What a hassel.Still havent got it. Eventually we decided to try out the pool. What kind of idiots run this establishment? We are 57 and 50 and "guests" but had to provide ID in case we wanted a drink from the bar - give me a break!! Ok Id like a little sun so we did that. I went ahead of my husband and took a lounger - half hour later he joined me asked other guests could he take an unoccupied lounger - well the crown jewels are not as well protected. Attendant told him he couldnt take it - he apologised and asked why he couldnt move it 20 feet to my lounger..... the child in charge responds by muttering into his walkie talkie and 2 burly security personnel approach.
