APPALLING!!!! We left immediatley. I have NEVER been treated so disrepectfully. Unfortunately we cannot just leave this hole right now - we are here on business.

reviews.title: Loved it!
reviews.text: My boyfriend & I booked this hotel for 7 nights during the Viva Las Vegas rockabilly weekender as The Orleans & associated hotels had sold out by the time we made the decision to go.For those considering this as an option for next years event (The Orleans sold out whilst we were there), the Gold Coast is within walking distance & they run 24 hour shuttles to The Orleans for VLV.We had no issues with checking in - very smooth process & were even offered an upgrade at a special price. We declined & I'm glad we did as the basic room that we had booked more than met our needs.We were on the 12th floor with views of the Palms Casino & the Strip (no access to the balcony for 'security reasons' though). The room was massive. Easily bigger than my 1 bed flat at home! We had a spacious bathroom with separate whirlpool bath & rainfall shower. Toiletries were provided & more could be requested from Reception.There was a kitchen area with mini-bar, fridge & dishwasher. Be warned - do not even open the door to the mini-bar! We opened the door before we realised there was a fridge below where we could put our water & even doing this must have activated a sensor as a bottle of water showed up on our final bill. This was however removed by the Receptionist without argument when we checked out.The king-size bed is one of the most comfortable I have ever slept in & we both slept very well (after we put in ear plugs to drown out the very effective AC).The living area was also spacious & comfortable & we ended most nights just sat on the sofa with a night cap looking at the view.The room itself was clean, tidy & didn't show any signs of wear & tear. The 2 large flat screen TV's in the living room & the little TV in the bathroom (which the boyfriend thought was hilarious to watch when he was in the bath) showed a range of American channels. You could also view your hotel bill on the TV's.Housekeeping were lovely & friendly - nothing seemed like too much trouble for them. The few times that we spoke to reception (trying to figure out how to log onto the free Wi-Fi) they were also very friendly & helpful. With regard to food, I would definitely recommend the buffet at the Palms Casino. We stayed 2 nights at the Golden Nugget in downtown following a mini road trip to Arizona & was surprised that their buffet was more expensive & didn't include beer & wine at lunch & dinner.We ate at the buffet at least once a day for breakfast, lunch or dinner & all meals had a large variety of quality, hot, well presented food. The staff here were also very friendly & helpful & kept topping up our drinks - even the mimosas when we went for Sunday brunch :)There is a complimentary daily shuttle bus from The Palms Casino down to Caesar's Palace Forum. It runs from 11-8 & you just have to show your room key to the driver. The Casino is easily accessible from Palms Place by a 'sky tube' as they called it. Go to floor 2 & follow the corridor round. Keep going over the travelators & down the lift at the end & this will bring you out in the casino. Keep to the left, walk past the Sports Bar & another bar & you'll come to the main entrance where the shuttle picks up/drops off.The one night we spent on the Strip, we got the last shuttle over there &, if you get a taxi back from The Mirage, you avoid having to go onto the Strip & get stuck in expensive traffic.All in all, we had a great time at the hotel & didn't feel too disadvantaged about not being on the Strip. We have decided to go back to Vegas again &, if we couldn't get a Strip hotel (it has to be done after all), we wouldn't hesitate to stay here again.PS we did find the whole resort fees thing a bit confusing. Travel Republic offered the room at a much cheaper rate but didn't mention resort fees whereas booking.com had the room at a higher rate but this included some fees. Be careful to read the small print so you know what you are getting as part of the nightly rate.

reviews.title: Not the worse, or best
reviews.text: The Studio Suite was nice, but I don't think the Palms Place will be my first choice my next trip to Vegas. Spacious, however there were too many little things "wrong." The whole left wall did not have electricity so my lamps, clocks, and outlets didn't work (which was inconvenient when we were looking to charge phones and tablet). By the time I was unpacked and realized it, it would've been another inconvenience to move to another room.Also, they provide an iPod dock so guests can play music... However it is outdated and doesn't fit any model past an iPhone 4 (which hasn't been sold for over a year). So we just blasted music from our cell phones the best we could, but had to keep it in the same spot since I could only charge my phone on one side of the room.It was also an inconvenience that there was not a dresser or any place other than the closet to put clothes. There were shelves under the tv, which left all the wires exposed (tacky in my opinion) since there was no cover, and didn't have any drawers for me to place my intimates and folded clothes. I expected more for a Palms hotel. How do you accept pets but not have smoking rooms? It's all a preference I suppose. It was also a HUGE bummer that the outside door was locked and didn't allow guests out on the balcony. It was tease to have a balcony, but not be able to walk out and enjoy it. At least have a window to crack for some fresh air.

reviews.title: Million Dollar Views-spacious, modern
reviews.text: We stay for $53 plus $25 resort fee.  Got a room on the 26th floor, facing the strip.  Incredible view.  This property is a little older but can't really see it.  I believe units are individually owned, but seems like they are kept standard with same furnishings.  Our room was huge.  Full kitchen, which we didn't use.  Very modern bathroom with rain shower and large jetted tub.  Two big screen TVs.  King bed (very comfy), and an L-shape sofa.  One good restaurant.  But Palms Place adjoins The Palms.  This is where you'll find the casino, buffet restaurant (breakfast included in our rate), a food court, big pool area, Hooters, another 24-hour cafe, and the fabulous Ghostbar.Only drawback for some might be that it's a few miles off the strip.  But that's why the view is so great.  Get a rental car.  Very inexpensive and parking is easy.

reviews.title: Very good hotel with hidden charges
reviews.text: I reserved a room and paid several days in advance. When I arrived , they charged me extra $33 "hotel fee". Why? I did not have time to argue and payed.  It's not honest. I reserved hotels online hundreds times and always paid only amount shown at time of reservation.

reviews.title: Great Room, not so great location
reviews.text: When I first arrived, it was late and they couldn't find my reservation.  I had prepaid for the room so I knew it was in there somewhere.   It was odd, but after a while, they found it.   By the time I got into the room I was over it.    This is where things turned around though as the room was absolutely beautiful.   It was HUGE too with an incredible view of the strip which was waaaaaaaaay over yonder.    The bed was incredibly comfortable and I slept like a baby, thank goodness.      So the next day I woke up in a much better mood.   I had a convention to attend during the day and again, it was waaaaaaay far away.   I pretty much had to wait for a taxi no less than 10-20 minutes every time I had to go anywhere.    That was pretty frustrating.   On the last day of my stay, I finally had enough time to check out the casino and wow was I disappointed.   At 11pm it was all but empty and those who were there were older, and to me, a little shady.    I was disappointed as i was hoping to watch a bunch of people gambling and having fun.  (I don't gamble but I like to watch those big loud groups playing craps and roulette)       The next day I went to the pool which and had a really nice lunch and a few drinks before heading to the airport for my flight home.   The pool definitely was a redeeming factor, for me anyway.   I was ready to relax and it wasn't loud, wild or crazy.   It was pretty tame for a vegas resort poo.   But like I said, I was ready to relax so it was great for me at the time.   Had I wanted a little more action, I might have been disappointed.

reviews.title: Nice Interior, Poor Service!
reviews.text: I was attending a major conference in Vegas, and found this hotel online. Based on their website it seemed to be very nice place to stay, offering various rooms and good deals. I wanted upper floor suite, with all major assets, and nice view of the city at night. I wanted to relax with a drink and sit on the balcony - watching the lights of sin city. The customer service told me (on the phone) that my suite has all of those things, including nice BALCONY WITH A VIEW! Great. So I booked 6 nights, and showed up to find the following: balcony with a view is LOCKED and you cannot access it due to "safety reasons" (the front desk actually said that), the hallway on my floor smelled of marijuana every single day (so strong - that you will get high second hand), missing drinks in the fridge (and they will try to charge you for it), 3 TV sets inside the room, but very POOR cable reception (almost unwatchable)... Plus, the front desk service has some very unprofessional employees who need serious training in customer service (I guess they care only about that rich guy on the top floor who drives Ferrari and gives large tips, so they abandoned middle class guests)... Just sayin' - what I experienced myself. The bottom line is: this hotel looks nice from the outside and has a nice website, but there is clearly FALSE advertising involved here, and you will NOT get what you're paying for (unless you consider free get-high-experience as a nice gift). Oh, did I forget - the faucet handle is broken and a bottle of water costs 6 bucks in the Pool Bar (the pool closes at 6pm, but the advertisement shows "shiny happy people" around the pool enjoying a nice evening around the fire (good acting for sure). I'm a film director, I spot those things... So, my advice is - find the "palm" elsewhere. Peace.

reviews.title: Las Vegas Best Kept Secret
reviews.text: This hotel is a five star self catering apartments. It was stunning and so were the views. We were on the 27th floor facing the strip what a view! We checked out of our strip hotel for a cheap weekend just off the strip. We were up Flamingo road which is central to the strip and the strip is so accessible by the free shuttles and a bus out the front of the hotel. The casino is linked at Palms you just walk through the sky walk. The pool was quiet and in a sunny position it was so peaceful. The rooms are outstanding with two TVs in studio one in front of the bed and one in the lounge area. There was even a TVs in the bathroom. There was a spa bathe and a walkin spa shower. I would definately stay here again and look forward to booking this later this year. The best kept secret in Vegas and you won't be disappointed.

reviews.title: Good, would recommend to others
reviews.text: Everything was fine; I was there solo for work and liked being off the strip. Lovely spa, gym, pool. The only thing was that i had a wonderful terrace but the door was locked and they said I wasnt allowed to use it, bummer! Wish there was more coffee in the room.

reviews.title: Will Not Stay Again
reviews.text: I actually like the rooms at the Palms Place and Spa, but I find the front desk staff to be one of the worst I've experienced.  Having traveled all of my adult life for work, one comes to expect basic things... like having the room I reserved available.   More than once, I have been informed that I need to pay for an upgrade or I can have the room I reserved at the Palms Casino... not acceptable.   I'm tired of "rolling the dice," so to speak on whether my room type will be "mine" at check in.  Even though I arrived after midnight, I cancelled my room and moved to another hotel.  They don't deserve my money for the room... or for gambling at their casino.  Goodbye Palms...

reviews.title: Nice hotel would stay again
reviews.text: We've been to Vegas a lot never stayed at the Palms thought we would try this resort it was a nice surprise.This is hotel is located near the Palms casino which you can access by an indoor walkway which is convenient and if your not a fan of staying in casinos this is great for you.We like having fridge and microwaves because sometimes we just come to chill and don't always want to go out so always nice to have somewhere to store snacks.The room is set up great has everything you will need, 2 tvs large, couch/living area as well as a balcony with a great view of the strip.Bedding is excellent as are the linens, towels and water pressure in the shower was greatWe enjoyed the the hotel and amenities will stay again, was a little surprised that some of the areas were over looked, needs some touch ups done in the rooms.The tub areas was moldy due to the tub and shower being enclosed, needs to be redone asap.But a nice stay off the strip and a great condo set up, fitness facilities were great, didn't use the pool as it was cold.Wifi was included in the usual resort fee scam

reviews.title: Absolutely magical
reviews.text: I am an Expedia Elite Plus card holder, the highest tier I believe of their rewards program (which isn't saying much), but Palms Place is a Expedia VIP Hotel. I had a corner 1 bedroom suite for five days, and it was one of the most brilliant experiences in Vegas, and I am there A LOT. Don't listen to these negative reviews. Sure its a bit off strip, (ohhh watch out a few blocks), there is always the ample shuttle. The resort is so quiet, and the Suite at Palms was heavily insulated for the ultimate in privacy. The layout of the corner room is stellar. If you are going to base not booking there on tiny negatives about frosted shower doors, etc, then you really are in the wrong town. The place is extraordinary. I will never stay anywhere else (save Mandalay Bay), when I go to Vegas. Treat yourself, it's simply an oasis to escape to and into.

reviews.title: Hotel okey
reviews.text: We checked in at this hotel in las vegas,as my daughter already had a good experience in staying at this hotel.true enough, its home away from home..the only thing i dislike is the bathroom.though its clean and tidy. In the  toilet bowl area.. It smells stinky, and i see no dirt, but the smell gets inside my nose, i still need to spray a little perfume to lessen the odor. Maybe they need an exhaust to fix the problem.i also like the location, its not along the strip, which was so crowded almost always, and this hotel is also near to many restaurants which are not so expensive.

reviews.title: Going down hill
reviews.text: I have stayed at Palm Place for many years and have enjoyed it until this last stay. Furniture falling apart, toe nail clipping in the carpet room not clean. Customer service not the same as it used to be.

reviews.title: Palms
reviews.text: Too far away from all of the action.  Rooms are very nice.  Spacious, clean and modern.  They need more people working the front desk.  It can get little spooky at night because it's so dead quiet.  Wouldn't wanna stay here again

reviews.title: Clean but so many issues!!!
reviews.text: The place is clean, and the beds are triple sheeted, but we had so many issues I would have a hard time returning.  This place is so dark it is almost dangerous; even with every light on in our room it was too dark to see- esp the bathroom when putting on makeup. Perhaps it is to hide the 70's veneer furniture that is so dinged and damaged I was shocked it was still in use. We had a suite which I believe is the standard room, but the kitchen has nothing in it but a broken leaky coffee pot. They don't even have towels or anything to use in the kitchen, which is ok since all we found were 2 mismatched coffee cups. Not even a fork to eat my leftovers from a restaurant. They never restocked our coffee or toiletries either.      We had breakfast included with our room but the wait time was so long it made it impossible to utilize. We waited  over 45 minutes in line with only 9 people in front of us; by the time we were seated they had stopped breakfast so we were stuck with the dregs. It was strange because there were at least 20 empty tables, and yet we waited.  Once seated we waited 10 minutes for lukewarm  coffee served in a paper cup. Never got a refill or top off despite asking twice. It did look like a nice breakfast from what we could see from the remains. The staff acted like we were a bother at the restaurant and pool, and you can't sit in the shade without a hefty fee.  We have been to Vegas many times but this place may as well have been a Motel 6! I can't recommend this place- I don't require a lot over cleanliness and some basics but come on,  at least deliver what you promise- even the "free" wi-fi" was a joke unless you paid dearly for the normal speed.

reviews.title: Nice and comfort place
reviews.text: My wife and me went on vac. last November and we booked a fly with hotel, so we really did'n know what to expect from the hotel, the price was really good to be true, so I look at the pics and everything looks awesome, but you know how are the sites when talk about pics, sometimes they are fake. Well we drop the coin to the air and went there, we were surprise to find a nice and luxury hotel and Spa as the palms place, room clean, big and a huge hot tube, 2 flat tv's, the bed soft, kitchen also clean.  The personal always kind and the best part its connected to palms hotel, so you have movie theater, hall concert, fast food area, casino, night club and so many more things to do.  They have a shuttle from hotel to Cesar's Palace, which save you lots of many on cabs, and from there you can move to anywere.

reviews.title: Great spacious premium room
reviews.text: Room was very spacious, clean and modern. Amazing bathroom. House keeping do an excellent job. Fast wifi. Swimming pool could be cleaner.Watch out for extra charges - resort fee per day. Otherwise great stay. Staff are friendly.

reviews.title: Awsome Pool
reviews.text: A Diamond in the rough! Listen the Palms Place just doesn't get the kind of credit it should. I'm guilty myself that I haven't gave them much of a chance because after being spoiled on the strip with MLIFE and all the MGM hotels I really had no need to stay here. My only gripe would be the customer service but I won't ding them too bad because the property and pool is beautiful. I came here last week for a private party that hosted a pool party. When I walked in and asked the front desk or concierge person about this party they apparently didn't know anything about it and the lady was rather rude about it. Gave me a look like I was from outer space. Weird but anyways it's a good thing that another guest standing by knew something about the pool party and was able to direct me in the correct place. Not the job of a guest but sure glad they knew because I wouldn't have got up. You would think that for big events everybody would be in the loop but that wasn't the case. The pool itself was amazing and the entire property was so clean. We went also into one of the suites and again just spectacular! No complaints on that end. If you are wanting something off the strip and away from all the strip craziness then this would be the place!

reviews.title: Lots of Flash, but Lacking Some Substance
reviews.text: I am the type of person that doesn't spend a lot of time in his hotel.  I use it as a "home base" to go see things and then come back and crash.  As far as that is concerned, this hotel was fantastic as it was reasonably priced, didn't not have an exorbitant resort fee, had a convenient location for both getting into the main parts of the Strip quickly and also for getting out of town.  The valet was quick at getting the car and made it easy to hand off my car to be parked.In regards to the hotel itself, it is definitely very flashy.  The drive up to the valet will be met with a lot of hot cars parked outside; in the time I was there (3 nights), I saw a McClaren, Rolls Royce, several Ferraris, a Lamborghini, and the like.  Additionally, Nicholas Cage was supposedly staying at the hotel.Customer Service could be a little slow at times -- or non-existent if you tried to call the valet or something; it was better to just walk down and hand them the ticket -- but everyone seemed friendly and they got the job done.I did not get to see the pool on account of other activities and windy weather that closed the pool area.We had a room on the 52nd floor and the view was awesome even though we weren't looking at the strip.  Unfortunately, this was a little hamstrung by the fact that they have a balcony, but lock the balcony doors.  The room was spacious and elegant-looking.  The bathroom was big and the shower was awesome, with the ability to do both overhead and snake head shower; even at the same time -- or take a bath.Upon closer inspection of things, however, some of the amenities seem a little dated, such as a TV in the bathroom that takes DVDs.  Additionally, simple things like turning on the lights or plugging in your phone charger or trying to connect an Amazon Fire Stick to the television seemed overly difficult.  There are two refrigerators, one for your use and one stocked full of alcohol and the like.  The one for personal use wasn't bad except that there was no way to get it to stop making ice, which was not only a bit noisy at times, but if I wanted to use the freezer for something else, it required that I dumped the ice out first and then expect more ice to be dumped on top of whatever I put in there.The Internet Wi-Fi was free, so long as you want really slow Internet.  You have to pay up to $15 a day to get Internet as fast as my cellular; I just used my phone as a hotspot to stream movies instead.The bed was really comfortable, but the pillows left a bit to be desired.The room does have a stove top and a nice counter, but with rather uncomfortable seats to sit in.  There were two televisions in the room: one in front of the couch area and one in front of the bed.  I didn't bother using the couch and/or the second television as it didn't make much sense for the two of us -- we'd rather lay and bed and watch the other television -- and the couch was rather uncomfortable anyway.One definitely plus of the room is it seemed to be completely sound proof.  I can't recall hearing anything outside of my own room, ever, and never felt like I might be impinging on others if I had my television loud.The casino is not in the hotel, but it is very close by; besides, if you're like me, you tire of casinos quickly and it is actually nice to walk into the hotel and not be met with one.All-in-all, for the things that I did in Vegas and the convenience it provided, I would likely stay in this hotel again.

reviews.title: Upscale hotel but a but worn and rough around the edges
reviews.text: Overall our stay was great. Everything from the check in staff to the valet/door attendants to room service to check out. We never ran across a staff person that was unfriendly.Rooms are large and bathroom/shower was very nice. We had a great view of the strip but they lock the balcony door which sucks because we could not enjoy standing out there and enjoy the cool morning and evenings. We stayed there because they had balconies but if I knew we could not have used them I would have stayed elsewhere.Room was clean enough, a few very minor details were overlooked but I'm very picky so most people would not even notice. Our room had Dishwasher, stove, microwave , blender, toaster, fridge  and coffee maker.

reviews.title: The dumb blonde of hotels!
reviews.text: I've stayed at this hotel 11 of the past 13 weeks as my company has a corporate rate and I have no choice.  All style no substance.  Great looking rooms.  Very stylish.  But that's it.  There is nothing comfortable about it. Lousy couch, lumpy beds and horrible pillows.  Bag that "they don't want you in the room" Las Vegas rhetoric. There is no casino (except the adjacent Palms).  Customer Service is non-existent.  If there is 1 person in line or 15 you get one front desk associate.  The other associates do a great job of not noticing the line and moving quickly away from the front desk as they pass.  Because I arrived on the same day and time each week, the same guy checked me in 9 times.  He still asked me every time "have you stayed with us before?".  My response of, yes XXXX, you checked me in for the past 4 weeks wasn't even met with a knowing glance up.  Just the robotic "well welcome back".  That said, this is most definitely not a complaint.  In fact I find the entire thing kid of funny.  It's a good hotel.  Just like every other hotel room in Vegas.  "Average".

reviews.title: Feels like home
reviews.text: I've stayed at the Main Palms hotel this is on the other side which is more of a residential section. ( it's a bit of a walk to get to this side it's like a maze but after a while you get use to it) I have to say the rooms are way better and the suites are ridiculous!!! The only thing is you do not have access to the balcony. Which defeats the purpose of the beautiful view of Vegas. The restaurants at the Palms are to die for. Ghost bar was pretty cool at night but the day party on Saturday was off the hook!! I usually took an uber to go to the strip it's much cheaper. I will definitely will be staying on this section of the palms.

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.text: I found a deal for the Palms Place online and was initially hesitant because it wasn't on The Strip, but the deal was too good to pass up! I am so glad I jumped on the deal! The room was gorgeous and very clean! The bathroom was amazing: jetted soaking tub, waterfall shower head, tv! Since it was a family stay, I greatly appreciated that we didn't have to walk through a smoky casino to get to our room! The pool area was gorgeous, but we didn't get to spend much time there because there was a very chilly wind most days! I would definitely recommend this hotel!

reviews.title: Big rooms. That's it.
reviews.text: Stayed here because our booking at the Hard Rock was messed up. If you're traveling without a car be prepared to drop a lot on taxis to get around the place as the Palms is a long way from anywhere. The studio suite was big, a little worn but well appointed. I'm not sure why you'd ever need 2 TV's next to another but just go with it. It's a shame there is no balcony access but I understand a few have ruined it for everyone. Perhaps glazing out the balconies would ensure guest safety and provide adequate access.

reviews.title: Great hotel!
reviews.text: Awesome Hotel! Great fitness area! Accomodating staff, clean and big rooms that do not smell like smoke! Not a young party scene here. The shuttle is perfect arrives on the 1/2 hour, takes you into Caesars Palace forum shops. Uber is about $5-7 from the hotel to the strip.

reviews.title: Enjoyable
reviews.text: Nice place. They have a shuttle between Palms and Caesars Palace, but you must show room key. Spacious room. Mini kitchen with fridge and dish washer. Plenty of closet space. Room had a balcony but the door to it was locked.

reviews.title: Better than a casino hotel room
reviews.text: The room was awesomely decorated and laid out. 2 flat screen tvs, gas fireplace, full kitchen. Pretty sweet views of the palms towers and the strip. 2 large balconies that weren't accessible to guests anymore. The amenities were bare to say the least (full kitchen yet only 2 coffee mugs and 2 small glasses, upon asking for more the front desk said we had to pay for them?) The front desk and management staff weren't very helpful either. Our original room that we got thru Expedia wasn't going to be ready due to a maintenance issue and instead of doing their best to fix the situation, the front desk was just going to put us in lesser rooms. Obviously not ideal so after my wife made a few direct comments they magically found us ideal rooms on a lower floor. Given all the choices in Vegas, I don't think we'd stay here again.

reviews.title: Palms Hotel Review
reviews.text: We stayed in the older section, not the towers, in a room with 2 queen beds.  Even though we reserved a king, they had evidently overbooked their rooms.  We didn't use any of the "resort" amenities, like pool, etc.  Our room was facing the strip.  The beds were just ok, the pillows were hard and uncomfortable (kink in neck in the morning), the bathroom was adequate, however, the sink was very slow draining, cheap toiletries, no shower cap, and the shower door was European style i.e.  the "half" shower door where the shower water runs over the edge of the floor--not a good design for comfortably using the shower, but probably pretty cheap to build.  The bed sheets were rough, and I doubt they even cleaned the coverlet on the bottom of each bed for awhile.  All in all, it was a basic, "bare bones", cheap Las Vegas hotel room. I will not be returning to the Palms anytime soon.

reviews.title: upgraded to palms place-LOVED IT!!
reviews.text: very chic and upscale. condo style hotel rooms. They even have door bells.   the room is spacious and had a whirlpool tub-we didn't want to leave.   Great romantic valentine's weekend.  One drawback was the balcony os inaccessible...it looked nice and had room but you cannot use them :(

reviews.title: Great place, and free strip shuttle!
reviews.text: From the moment we walked in to the moment we checked out I was in love.  Unlike the Casino hotels in Las Vegas you walk in, hop on the elevator, and there you are! The elevators are fast, and there are no long waits.  Now, the room.... everything you need, and for sure more!  Fridge separate from the mini bar, cook top, microwave, coffee maker, dishwasher, toaster, oh my goodness, and thats just the kitchen. Now, the bathroom the usual, toilet, sink, tv, hair dryer...now for the good stuff!! The shower is a stand alone shower with a rainshower shower head and also a detachable shower head.  You can switch between the 2, whatever you prefer which is nice. Next to the shower is the tub, or mini pool, mini hot tub, however you want to play it.  It is for sure big enough for 2 people, the jets work, and everything is clean! Moving on the bedroom/living area the bed is super comfy, more than enough lighting, seating, and storage space.  There are 2 tvs, 1 for the bed area, and 1 for the living area so that is 3 tvs total in this studio.  The balcony is locked off so you cant actually go out, but the floor to ceiling windows allow for an amazing view of the strip and mountians...beautiful!So, Palms Place is connected to the Palms so you dont have the crowds, but it is easy to get to the food, bars, clubs, and casino.  The Sky Tube allows you to walk between the 2 without going outside.  It is a bit of a walk, but its nice to not have to deal with the desert elements.  You are off the strip, but they offer a free shuttle that takes you down.  You are picked up in the casino are of The Palms, and they drop you off at The Forrum Shops which is where you will be picked up when you are ready to head back.  They do only offer the shuttle between certian hours, but its enough to get you to the strip for free.All said and done highly recommend Palms Place! Can't wait to return

reviews.title: Chic Trendy Hotel and Casino
reviews.text: Large stylish room with sleek kitchenettes and also great views of the city. Definitely a hotel for adults not so much for children. Although the few dining places we tried were upscale and good, the Palms could benefit by having more dining choices.

reviews.title: Great View With So Much To Do!
reviews.text: The problem with so many resorts on the Strip is that they are often overpriced.  And while large resorts are impressive and easy to admire, they aren't convenient for someone staying there.  Palms Place isn't huge but it offers a lot and it's where you want to go when you honestly want to relax and intermittently enjoy Vegas life.  Transportation to the strip is offered for guests so getting there isn't a problem.  Definitely take advantage of this since it's not a nice walk to the strip and doesn't cater to pedestrians.  The view of the strip is gorgeous and you can see all the way from the Stratosphere down to Mandalay Bay easily.  We were on the 23rd floor and our panoramic view was lovely.  Getting to the Palms is accomplished via an indoor walkway.  The Palms itself has a food court and many dining areas.  It has a movie theater and nice bars and lounges.  With the Gold Coast and the Rio nearby, there's a lot to do if you're staying at Palms Place.  Our room was gorgeous with a nice modern look.  It's very spacious and looks inviting.  There's a kitchenette and dining area so eating in the room feels comfortable.  The room has 3 TVs.  One in the living area where you can relax on the corner couch.  The corner couch is also a great place to relax and read with the adjustable lamp lights.  Another TV is found across from the bed and yet another is in the bathroom to watch while you get ready.  The bed is comfortable and if you like having lots of pillows the Palms has every other place beat.  I think it was a bit of overkill and we threw most of the pillows on the couch and didn't need that many.  The bathroom is really nice.  You have a nice hot tub with adjustable strengths on the jets.  On top of that, the jets have different modes.  One mode causes undulating waves or you can simply enjoy the constant stream of pressurized water giving you a massage.  There's a detachable shower head or you can use the shower head on the ceiling for a nice simulation of rain.  If the bathroom had twin vanities it would've been perfect.  We didn't get to check in early and I'm used to that at all other resorts.  I've usually been allowed to check in anywhere from 30 minutes to 2 hours early.  I understand that our room wasn't ready and at least we didn't check in late.  They held our bags for us no problem and the lounge was a great place to wait and relax.  The next time I feel like relaxing in Vegas, Palms Place will be a heavy contender.  It's worth the visit in every way I can imagine.

reviews.title: Meh
reviews.text: We booked this place as an 'off the strip' non-gaming hotel in order to get away from the casino vibe in LV. Much to our chagrin, we discover that there is no breakfast restaurant in the non-gaming wing- instead we have to go into a nasty casino to get a coffee in the morning. The room was stale and cold, cheap, fake wood floors, scratched up from use, laminate countertops, and scratchy sheets. The 'resort fee' does not cover use of the gym, and if the pool is closed (which is was), then let's be honest, its just a deferred cost to the room. So we're off the strip, with casino based food options, near a strip mall- worst of both worlds. The staff at the desk were nice, which counts for something.

reviews.title: Great hotel for the price!
reviews.text: My husband and I were passing through Las Vegas on our way home and selected this hotel due to location and price. We were pleasantly surprised by the hotel when we arrived. Initially I was a but concerned because we were not staying on or closer to the strip, however an $8 uber ride cured that concern quickly.  They also have a shuttle from The Palms Hotel & Casino to Caesar's Palace.  The only downfall is the last shuttle is at 8 pm. We took the shuttle to CP and then uber back. The hotel is just a block down the road from the Palms Hotel & Casino. They offer complimentary valet with welcome gratuity. The lobby of the hotel is simple yet modern and has a small bar and hotel shop. We enjoyed a drink at the bar before heading to our room and found it to be pleasant. Our room was on the 9th floor which was quiet, spacious, contemporary, and very well situated facing the strip. The bathroom was large and cleanly decorated in marble and glass. Overall we were quite please with this hotel! Though off the strip you can save quite a bit on your stay and spend a little each way to uber to the strip and back.  Definitely would stay there again!

reviews.title: First visit to The Palms...
reviews.text: This is our first visit to the Palms. Valet and check-in was easy, and simple. Nice to be greeted with a smile and some real friendliness. We booked through Expedia, and we were granted a 2pm late check. That was unexpected and nice perk. We were given a 50th floor room with a view.  Nice full kitchen room, although you had to request plates, glasses, and utensils. They had now problem bring them up promptly.  Some great dining options, with a food court for munchie time or feeding the kids. Full casino options, however not sure if they have a poker room. Recommend for a great weekend!

reviews.title: The condo suites are the best...
reviews.text: We booked a great deal on the condo suites which are 600 sq feet. Living area beside bed. Big screen, wifi and a small but very useful kitchen. Bathroom was large,clean and had a over sized tub. Staff were pleasant and profesional. Great restaurants in hotelshort drive to the strip without any traffic dilemmas. Over all way better than many hotels on the strip unless you are willing to pay top dollar.

reviews.title: Vegas Trip
reviews.text: The Studio room was excellent!! very clean & comfortable! The casino is excellent! restaurant were on point! Didn't like that the beautiful balcony was locked with a key for guests and if your were not an owner it could not be opened per the front desk! Also the WIFI is paid for service.

reviews.title: Superb Rooms!  Palms Place is in an oasis away from the typical Vegas scene, but close enough to Palms Casino
reviews.text: Superb Rooms!  Palms Place is in an oasis away from the typical Vegas scene, but close enough to Palms Casino

reviews.title: A little below average
reviews.text: We stayed there for 3 nights in response to a promotion that included breakfast. The pictures marketing the hotel are quite deceiving. The rooms although spacious are not nearly as beautiful and glamorous as their pictures show. The hotel is unappealing. The lobby is huge and empty, like a train station. The rooms are not well taken care of. Our room looked very tired. The beautiful wood like floor had a lot of scratches and really the room was not spotless. One day they didn't even wash the soap dish. The breakfast buffet is located in the casino that is connected to the hotel by a long and impersonal walkway. The buffet food is very average. The bed was comfortable. I will not stay there again.

reviews.title: Quiet, Clean, and Very nice rooms!
reviews.text: I spent a trade show trip at the Palms Place Hotel.  The trade show was at the Sands, so it wasn't exactly the closest to the location, but that wasn't bad.  Thank goodness for Uber.  be forwarned that when using Uber, they default to the Palms Casino entrance which is a bout a 2-3 min walk.  The room was very nice and modern, with a kitchen and great view of the mountains.  Towels were always fresh and every day for the 5 days i was there it was very clean.  House keeping was very cordial and friendly.  I liked the button to inform them of a do not disturb or house keeping.  I had two TV's but only one had sound. not that it mattered to me, i didn't watch much TV during my stay.  You have to walk (moving walkway) from the Palm Place to the Palm Casino to eat and get to the casino, vending and bank machines..  Remember that you need to get off on the 2nd floor of palms place to get to the moving walkway.. then take the elevator down to the main floor of the casino.I managed to get to the pool area.  Seemed very nice, but it was too cold during my stay in vegas.Not alot of local walking distance things to do in the area.  WiFi was free with the room, but it was only at 1MB.. way too slow.. that would be my only complaint.  My cell phone LTE service was faster. if i wanted faster i had to pay 6-12$ per day.. not going to happen.Overall i enjoyed my stay and would come back again.

reviews.title: Beautiful room but disappointing features
reviews.text: Was really excited to stay here, but was disappointed in a few things. The room was large, great furniture and views, also quiet and relaxing.However: the balconies are all locked. So no access is allowed. I was very excited to use the hot tub at their pool, but it closes at 5. A little early for Vegas no? I understand 10pm, or heck even 7... But 5pm? So instead we used our jacuzzi tub for relaxing, but the water smelled like mildew. In fact the next day the entire bathroom smelled of mildew just from using the tub once. Also, no ice makers, and our freezer was broken, so we had to call room service every time we needed ice. And no free wifi like I understood there would be.With a few adjustments catered toward their visitors, this place COULD be amazing.

reviews.title: Overnight
reviews.text: The studios are sleek and modern. Two TVs and luxury shower. Bed sleeps well and kitchen is practice and useful.  Nice views of western Vegas away from the strip.  I would recommend this place.  Use Priceline or their website to get a good deal.  I was on the 25th floor.

reviews.title: Nice, but very dark
reviews.text: The room was very nice and gave an exceptional view of the Las Vegas Strip.  The casino was quite a walk as well as the buffet restaurant and food mall area but still very nice.  The hotel was very dark...which may work for others but felt very depressing. My first night there - the front desk gave away my room key to another guest who walked in while I was sleeping - then they called me to say I was in the wrong unit.  Really?  So of course that deactivated my key and since my husband couldn't sleep - he walked downstairs and when he returned couldn't get in the room. Again front desk called me and asked me if my husband was staying with me. Duh.  Bad first experience - but rest of stay went smoothly.

reviews.title: Very comfortable without all the headaches from the Strip!
reviews.text: Upon arrival, I was created with a warm smile and great sense of humor from the lovely young lady at the front desk. The check in process was quick and painless without that HUGE line that you'll get from most of the hotels you get on the strip.  It was like walk up to the counter.. check in.. go upstairs. Why can't every Las Vegas hotel be that easy?    The rooms are beautiful and spacious. The bathrooms have huge jetted tubs with separate shower with rainfall shower head as well as a detachable shower head.  The beds are huge and there's also a living room area with a huge sectional couch. The kitchenette has a fridge, separate mini bar, sink, microwave, electric range, and even a dishwasher. We mostly used the microwave and fridge, but I think if you need more kitchenware, you have to call housekeeping. There's also a couple glasses, mugs and a coffeemaker. There's also a safe in the closet!   The 6th floor has another restaurant (which looks like amazing burgers!) a spa, gym, and pilates studio. I was so busy this trip, I didn't have time to take advantage of the workout facility, and it was too chilly to use the pool. But it looks amazing!   The 2nd floor has a sky bridge that leads to the main Palms hotel/casino which has more restaurants, fast food court, and movie theater.    We decided to stay and extra night, so extending my room was quick and hassle free.  The housekeeping staff were very respectful to the do not disturb sign (which is a switch you turn on or off), but long story short, this is one of my favorite places to stay in Vegas. It's clean, swanky, great staff, close enough to the strip to still be by the action, but far enough to be away from the craziness. I can't wait to stay here again!

reviews.title: Cheap.  Time for a refresh.
reviews.text: I knew I made a poor choice when the hotel marquis boasted Panda Express and Hooters.  The rooms were big but tired.  Chipped furniture, dusty.  A half eaten snickers bar in the fridge upon arrival was gross.  Being charge for the half eaten bar was a problem (they did remove it from the bill).  It is work mentioning that The Palms Place has no restaurants and room service is served in "to go" containers.  You can walk from The Palms Place to the Palm but fast food is all you can get for breakfast.  Would not stay there again.

reviews.title: Beautiful Room, Wi-Fi Disappointment
reviews.text: We were greeted upon check in with very friendly staff. They kindly gave us a room on the 33rd floor after I asked if we could have a room with a good view. The room was clean, spacious, and had a gorgeous view of the strip. The bathroom had a jetted tub and separate shower with 2 shower heads. There were 2 large flat screen TV's in the main area, and a small flat screen in the bathroom. There was a full kitchen (with utensils, supplies on request), an in room safe and large sofa. Our only complaint was that free wi-fi was advertised as part of the resort fee, and we had none. I tried resolving this with the front desk multiple times with no resolution. We were greatly disappointed by this. Also, the room has a blow dryer, coffee maker, toaster, dishwasher, sink, microwave, fridge with a mini bar, and 2nd empty fridge for your items.

reviews.title: Epic Vegas trip
reviews.text: We stayed at Palms Place for three nights at the end of our 4 weeks in the USA. Visiting Vegas was by far one of the highlights of our entire trip.Plans place was a fantastic place to stay. We got a great deal on one of the Studios, which was amazing. Bed, sofa, TV, bathroom (including great bath and shower) all luxurious and top quality. Recommended as a great value option for staying at one of the top hotels in Vegas.Off the strip location was quite refreshing and probably gave the more relaxed feel of the casino and pools. Really easy to travel to and from using the hotel shuttle. Taxi costs hardly anything to get back late at night. We spent more time at the rooftop pool in palms place, which was great. The private booths were all a bit worn down, but they were all reserved anyway despite no one using them! Absolutely brilliant pool for chilling by though.The time of year we went meant there wasn't as much going on in the hotel - less parties and events due to the run up to the halloween festivities, but I think this actually meant for a really relaxed stay at the hotel. We made up for this when we went out on the strip though!Casino was also great from the perspective of someone that doest play much else other than blackjack! Isn't as much traffic through there, more relaxed and less pressured than the main casinos in Vegas. We went to the rooftop bar the first night, which has stunning views of the strip, and is a great place for drinking and dancing. Didn't visit the other bar as we went out the other nights.Otherwise, interns of other recommendations for things in Vegas:We saw a Cirque Du Soleil show - which we couldn't recommend more...probably the most amazing show we have ever seen. Also walked through all the hotels on the strip one night, ending up at the the Paris Las Vegas, with he club at the foot of the Eiffel Tower which was also great.Would highly recommend to anyone visiting Vegas.

reviews.title: I loved the hotel being separate from the casino!
reviews.text: I would come back to stay, the location was just what I needed, not on the strip and in a great neighborhood environment. My stay was wonderful. But I had one big problem the tub deep Jacuzzi looked so good, I had to get in and enjoy the comfort of a long bath with bubbles. The problem is that there is no handles to hold on to, to get in and out. The tub had no grips to stop you from sliding or slipping. I was a little afraid being by myself it was not safe. I think that the hotel managing team should re-evaluate the jacuzzi grips on the bottom and the handle grips to get in and out is very much needed. Thank you

reviews.title: Fantastice room view, clean and friendly staff
reviews.text: Wife and myself just stayed at the Palms Place in Las Vegas for a Builders show. The room was located on the 38th floor and had a fantastic view. You could see the entire Vegas strip along with the surrounding mountain range. Just at 1 mile from the strip center, a quick and cheap UBER ride gets you there. Use UBER, not the taxi service and you'll save drastically. The room itself was very nice, contemporary with a big walk in shower and big tub. The bed is very large and comfortable. Only issue with our room was at night as the temp would fluctuate and you would either be really cold or extremely hot. All in all a fun business trip and we would recommend the Palms Place unless you want to be on the strip.

reviews.title: Palms Place isn't what it used to be
reviews.text: I have visited the palms/palms place for the past 4 years with a group of friends booking multiple rooms for an annual guys trip each time booking through the hotels website. The rooms were clean but showing some wear and tear. We usual like Palms place due to their balconies as we like to watch the skyline and shoot the breeze in between gambling. Last year however the balconies were locked. This was brought to the attention of the front desk who couldn't of had more of a so what attitude. I asked to speak with the manager, who's name is Dustin, but he did not offer any explanation of why there shut down eventhough the balconies can be seen in several photos while booking. The only option were given was to upgrade to another room for $800 more per night. Another issue with the palms is the casino and clubs within are not popular at all anymore. From Friday to Tuesday none of the venues had a significant crowd. Also, please use the in room safe. I left a necklace in the room and after cleaning service, it came up missing. The front desk did radio the maid but to no avail. This year we will move our guys trip to strip, since the amenities we liked about the palms are no longer available.Safe travels!!!

reviews.title: Great place off the Strip
reviews.text: This property is nice and away from the Strip and somewhat of a walk to the main Palms Casino but it's all connected.We arrived around 1AM after delays and other issues getting into Vegas. The staff at the front was great and so was the Valet service. The nice attendant at the desk upgraded us when asked to a Penthouse.All around the penthouse was a great room, wish we had more time to enjoy it. We had a large kitchen and eat in area, living room and bed room along with a large bath with steam shower. We also had a balcony that overlooked the mountains along with a spa with glass wall.

reviews.title: First Time
reviews.text: I travel a great deal, more than 200 nights per year.  Vegas has lost it's appeal to me from a vacation perspective, mostly due to coming to work trade shows several times per year.  With that said, I avoid the strip unless I absolutely have to stay on it.  This is the first time staying at this hotel after visiting it in November to get away from the strip.  I have to say, there are good and bad things about it.  Being realistic, no hotel is perfect.  With that said, the good:The 1BR suite I upgraded to on the 50th floor was spectacular.  You walk into marble floors, spacious living room and a very nice kitchen area.  The bedroom has a large jet tub and plenty of closet space.  The bathroom (the full one after I found a half one right when you walk in the door) has two shower heads and waterfall head above you.The bad, the carpet had repaired and you could see the seam.  The shower handle broke off when I turned it on, but maintenance fixed it by the time I returned to the room.  The shower also had a burned out lightbulb as well.  The sink handle had a leak and would drip when water is running.  Valet is VERY slow to respond, and hardly ever answers the phone if you call. The restaurant on the 6th floor has a limited menu, but spectacular view.  Lastly having two balconies, it was a shame that you are not able to walk out on them because of some crazy hotel policy.Ultimately for the money you cannot beat this place, especially if you are staying of the strip.  Granted, there are things that can be improved upon, but, no hotel is perfect.I more than likely will stay here again next time I am in Vegas, even though I am also tempted to check out some other properties off the strip as well.

reviews.title: A very Nice First Stay...
reviews.text: Stayed at the Palms Place for the first time earlier in January for work trip.I was upgraded from a studio suite to the one bedroom suite and...my gosh...it was just magnificent.1200 square feet of goodness. 35-301 had a view of Downtown Las Vegas, with partial views of the Strip and mountains.Enjoyed such goodies as the full size refrigerator, triple headed shower, whirlpool tub, and separate bedroom and living areas. There is a balcony but unfortunately they are kept locked unless you own a unit.A couple maintenance issues here and there were taken care of quickly.Access to the main hotel and casino is through a SkyTube on the 2nd level.Cab rides to the Strip are like $10...but the Flamingo Rd double decker city bus goes by frequently and will get you there in 10 minutes. A Day Pass is $5.Planning another trip for the Spring and the Palms Place is definitely on my list...

reviews.title: The best hotel in Las Vegas
reviews.text: This was the best hotel!!!!!! This was my husband and I first trip to Las Vegas it started out really bad, upon arriving at the hotel we discovered that my wallet was left on the airplane. Even though I was not allowed to check-in at the moment. Andrea immediately got on the phone and computer to locate the proper people I needed to talk to quickly to resolve this matter. They put our luggage in a safe place until we got back from the airport. My wallet was found!!!!!!! Once we got back to the hotel, due to the fact the we started out having such a hard time on our 5th year wedding anniversary we was upgraded to a one bed room suite. Needless to say it was breathtaking.... ABSOULUTLY BEAUTIFUL!!!!!!! Our stay here was wonderful!!!!! If you think that's all I got think again. Here is probably another reason why every time we come to Las Vegas we will always stay here is because, we ran into some more trouble this time with our card. For whatever reason our card stop working completely the last day in Vegas...Can you all imagine this having no cash!! Oh my goodness this was another most stressful times that I had ever encountered. With our flight leaving almost less than an hour away. Once again our hotel staff pulled together for us and made it happened... Starting with Andrea, headed to manager. While Cam printed off our boarding pass, Paige (manager) set up ride for us to the airport at her expense, and Christian the bellman driving us safely there and making sure we arrive on time. Without this crew at Palms Place our trip could have been so much worst. My husband and I would like to thank you all greatly from the bottoms of our hearts for everything you all did for us. On top of all this the hotel was amazing, the food was amazing the spa was amazing.... I could go on but you people must check it out for yourself. you will not be disappointed....

reviews.title: Return visit. Same issues. Seeming indifference.
reviews.text: This was a return visit to the Palms Place and sadly not much had changed since my previous visit. On arriving in the room, there was strange stains on both the couch and the walls - so in credit to the reception they did move us immediately. Strange smell in both the old and new room - I guess the product of having a kitchen so any previous guest who cooks, then you get stuck with the smell.Room just didn't feel clean - albeit incredibly spacious. Shame that the balconies don't open but seemingly a hotel policy. Rates at this hotel always seem cheap, but I just don't think its worth it - especially since you have to trek back and forward to the strip.

reviews.title: Nice off strip
reviews.text: I loved this place because it has such a beautiful view of the strip mostly and it has a balcony. I will stay again . It has everything you could possibly want. Not on the strip but that makes the view all the better.

reviews.title: Spent New Year's Eve in the Palms Place
reviews.text: This was a great pick if you want to be off the strip! I was a bit skeptical about this hotel after reading a bunch of reviews, but our experience was very different...the Palms Place didn't disappoint! Stay in room 31-306 it has the best view :)

reviews.title: I Like It Here
reviews.text: I really liked this location, the rooms, the atmosphere and the staff. I spent my birthday here and while they have a "no party" policy enjoyed the night and made our way to ghostbar. The room was clean and the bed was very comfortable. I would recommend this hotel to my friends.

reviews.title: Mini Apartment
reviews.text: I have wanted to stay at the Palms for a very long time but Palms Place went beyond my expectations for a hotel in Vegas.  It has a very nice bathroom with a Jacuzzi tub, and a nice kitchen area.  The only draw back was the wifi was only free for one device.

reviews.title: New Years Eve fun
reviews.text: I have to say that my initial perception of the check in was NOT enjoyable. After a grueling flight delay (due to de-icing the entire plane) and the insane shuttle ride from the airport to the hotel which took an hour due to the strip being on lock down for NYE, we were told our rooms would not be on the same floor, let alone next door to each other, and we would have to take a double queen room even though we paid for Superior King rooms online a month in advance. When we asked for this to be corrected we were told we would have to  go to the casino side to make room changes as they could not access that part of the computer from their side. So we had to drag all our luggage over to the "other tower" which was no small feat, up the elevator, thru the sky tube, down another elevator, all the way through the entire casino before reaching another desk. Again we were told about the lesser rooms. I politely told the girl this was NOT okay with me. I booked well in advance, paid for king size rooms and requested our friends be in the room next to ours. This was my first trip to Vegas, I was exhausted from all the travel (from Ohio) and delays and I wanted the room I paid for so we could clean up and go enjoy New Years Eve. The young lady immediately sprang into action and went to speak to a manager. It was only a few minutes and she returned to tell us they would take care of this by giving us side by side, upgraded, King size Suites at no extra charge. We had to make the long trek back to the other tower but it was well worth it. The rooms were gorgeous. White marble tiled bathroom, multiple flat screen tvs, Stainless steel appliances in the kitchenette, luxury king bed, contemporary living room and a balcony with a breathtaking view of the mountains from the 51st floor. So even though we had a rough start, The Palms did go above and beyond to salvage my first trip to Las Vegas. Everyone was amazing, and it was so fresh and clean. Just the escape Experience I needed. I highly recommend staying here. It's off strip but well worth it.

reviews.title: Lots of Other Hotels to Chose From
reviews.text: My sister and I have stayed several times at the Palms Place.  We liked it because its close to the food fair and slots, has a nice pool that's not too busy and large, apartment style rooms.  The last time we went was in September 2015 and sadly, I believe it will be our last.  Check in took hours - our room wasn't ready.  The large apartment style rooms are looking run down and in need of some TLC. One plus, our balcony door opened so we could enjoy sitting outside)....I'm not sure if this was a mistake, or not as not many balcony doors are unlocked in LV.  It was fun watching police chases with helicopters from our balcony).  The staff at the pools are like gestapo wardens.  If you move your lounge chair an inch, they will be at your side, telling you to move it back.  There were actual arguments between staff and guests at the pool where the Manager had to be called in.  Ridiculous..oh well, got a few free drinks out of the stress of having to listen to loud, angry voices.  I also noticed this time a lot of "undesireables' hovering around the front of the hotel.  Women with not much on and questionable men.  Scoot them away Palms Place!!  Makes your hotel look like a brothel.  So, all in all, there are tons of other hotels in LV.  May be giving this one the miss next time, unless they had some unbelievable rate and the CDN dollar goes up!!

reviews.title: Only average, lots of other places to stay
reviews.text: The other reviews hit it on the head.  Palms Place could be really great, but it's just average.  The views are good.  The rooms probably were terrific once.  It is not well maintained, the little things are pretty poor (e.g., bedspread was visibly stained after housekeeping made the bed.  Why didn't you change it?  And after I called at 9 p.m., they never came to change it until the next day or housekeeping.  There is an option to get dishes, which we did.  But housekeeping took them away, and didn't replace.  Etc.  One night roomservice rang the doorbell, we had the privacy light on and didn't order anything.  it was the wrong room)  This would be more than acceptable at a 3 star extended stay hotel (not trying to slam the courtyards of the world, just giving a comp).  But for a purported 4 star/diamond place it is pretty weak.I could go on, but it's really just like the others say.  For a really cheap price, I might consider staying again, but frankly I like so many other places in Las Vegas more -- even off strip -- that it is tough to advocate for another visit to Palms Place.

reviews.title: Desert Oasis with Phenomenal staff!
reviews.text: The Palms Place remains my favorite property in all of Las Vegas. We just checked-in tonight, and plan to stay another couple nights. Standards remain stellar, from Valet ("Tom") to the Front desk ("Brendan") and even the PBX (operator "Janet"). The Bellman was exceptional, and went out of his way to provide us with a couple items we left at home. Everyone on staff here is fully invested and committed to making every guest's stay special. Brendan worked magic for us, even after we arrived much later than we expected. He found a beautiful suite overlooking the pool and lights of the city. Our suite has everything you can imagine, including a Cleopatra free-standing jacuzzi tub, full kitchen with dishwasher, sub-zero, two bathrooms a fireplace and even a washer & dryer! Cutlery and dinnerware, including pans, etc., are provided with one quick call to room service. There is even a Waring pro blender with a glass pitcher, Cuisinart toaster and tea pot, etc. The suite is more than roomy, and is actually a luxury apartment (there are full-time tenants residing in several units in this beautiful location). The palms place is incredibly understated and quiet, providing a zen-like environment from the central lobby to the suite. No stale odors, no cigarette smoke, or ringing chaotic casino sounds to greet you upon entering. The entrance to the palms casino is accessed via the skywalk, and everything from nightclubs, restaurants, and even a movie theater is just across the connecting corridor. The palms place has it's own amazing restaurants and spa, private pool with cabanas, etc. The management team is unparalleled and always eager to help make your stay memorable and enjoyable. I am overwhelmed by the reception and hospitality we have received so far, and exceedingly grateful that such a resort still exists in Las Vegas.

reviews.title: Too Many Hassles
reviews.text: There is only one elevator in service, it's taking almost 10 minutes for it to arrive at your floor or the lobby. Actually had to skip a show as I hadn't allowed for this 20 minute round trip. The rooms are large and nice, but there is sewer smell in the shower stall. Also it's a tough place to self park, and the valet doesn't seem to be covered by the 38 dollar fee they charge as a hotel fee. They have wood floors that are "floating", so they aren't glued to the floor. So they make noise, at least the one above me is.

reviews.title: My new favorite place in Vegas
reviews.text: Vegas is the nearest "big city" to where we live in Utah so we visit frequently to travel or visit specialty doctors. This weekend our dog needed surgery so I searched travel sites for somewhere reasonable to stay for a night. I chose the Palms Place based on price ($79/night for 600 sq ft. studio). I wasn't expecting to be WOWED but let me say that I really thought this was by far the nicest place I've stayed in Vegas. The room was huge, clean, impressive! Our view from the 12th floor had a great view of the strip -- we could see all the way from Luxor to Stratosphere and everything in between. The bathroom totally rocked! The soaking tub was huge and the jets were powerful. nice floors throughout and the bed was SO comfortable!! The room was also really quiet. I appreciated that. We ate at Cafe 6 which was next to the pool. It was really great food! I am pretty hard to impress, but overall this was one of our best trips to Vegas. I'll def stay here again.

reviews.title: Penthouse Condo overlooking Las Vegas Strip
reviews.text: We arrived at this hotel at 12am after a long flight.. Purchased our room via Expedia and was already paid for. Come to find out our room had been taken BUT we got upgraded to a fabulous 1200 sqft  penthouse suite that was amazing!This hotel books very quickly and is well worth it because you're less than 7min away from the strip and close the express way and the airport.Our suite had a FULL stainless steel kitchen! The only thing I would suggest is for the rooms to come equipped with cutlery for its guest. Other than that our stay was perfect to celebrate 5 year wedding anniversary. I would stay here again!

reviews.title: Superb Room-wish I could stay longer
reviews.text: Arrived at 11pm en route from Riverside to Salt Lake. Room was spectacular corner suite on 20th floor with views from two glass walls and two balconies, even through fireplace which had glass front and back. Suite had two bathrooms plus jacuzzi in bedroom, king sized bed, 42inch TV in living room and bedroom, plus smaller TV in bathroom. Huge shower with three shower heads. It also had full kitchen and wonderful furniture throughout. I would have liked to stay longer but had to leave at 10am.The room was exceptionally quiet.

reviews.title: Staycation
reviews.text: The 29th flr. has a great view.  Excellent Vallet.  Not so friendly and informative Front Desk. The room had a stale smell in it but roomy and the bed was comfy.  Excellent Lighting and enough elec. sockets.

reviews.title: Facilities were first class, customer service nonexistent, spa was a ripoff!
reviews.text: The living/sleeping accomodations were excellent, it is too bad that there was no customer service and the spa was a total absolute ripoff, I was charged double what I was qouted, did not get the service I requested and after contacting management 4 times - 0 response.Plus the advertised rates did not include hidden fees! So buyer beware!

reviews.title: Poor Palms Place
reviews.text: We were excited to stay here for our staycation to celebrate our anniversary as we do in several hotels here in Las Vegas.  Looking at the photos we expected a beautiful, clean and modern environment.  The front desk girl was great so nothing regarding the staff.....but upon entrance to the unit we were hit with the reality of huge disappointment.  We step onto severely scratched, creaky wooden floors that seem to almost break when you step on them.  The stainless steal was something we thought not possible...stained.  The carpet is heavily worn and dingy with stains resembling bodily fluids we would rather not speak of.  The view is something we were really looking forward to and our eyes quickly led to the eaten shrimp tails on the deck.  My boyfriend then comes out of the bathroom to tell me there is a false eyelash next to his foot by the toilet....really?!  On top of it all there is a $500 locals deposit.  Enter at your own risk.....not worth the money....hopefully I get my $500 deposit back.....

reviews.title: Not What it Appears to be!
reviews.text: From what we could tell Palms Place is part of Palms Casino which is closer to the strip. Palms Place is in no way a hotel as it consists of units which are privately owned in which they are then rented out to the visitor. They do have a front desk for check in and internet which we found difficult to get on even with their help. There are no restaurants in the hotel and if you order room service it comes in take out boxes with plastic utensils. The units themselves are quite nice with comfortable beds but don't count on someone to clean your room and make your bed as we had to beg them to do this and eventually it was done. If you want a nice room as a reasonable price this may be the place but it's not a hotel. Last it took us a half an hour to get a cab to the strip and should you want to gamble you have to go through a tunnel to Palms Casio next door.. Would we stay there again, the answer is no!

reviews.title: Nice place but poor housekeeping
reviews.text: The hotel has a gorgeous view but the housekeeping was non-existent.  For the four nights we stayed the room was only cleaned and linens changed once and then we had to ask.  The first night we stayed the room looked very nice but when we came back the next day after being out all day the room was the same as when we left.  We rescued some towels off the floor and then went to down to the lobby to enquire if we had to do our own.  They advised that they would look into it immediately and everything looked great that day.  We expected everything would be good after that but our room wasn't cleaned again the next day so we phoned down and asked for clean towels.  Staff were helpful but won't stay again. Definitely not a 5 star.

reviews.title: We Will Return
reviews.text: My wife and I stayed here for a few hours, and we really enjoyed for the small amount of time we were here. The room is completely functional with all the amenities needed. Our only issue was the dirty ice bucket. But the room had a Strip view, stove, microwave and a shower that you could see through (romantic) from your bed. Makes for a great night!

reviews.title: Nice place to make you feel at home
reviews.text: Beautiful rooms beautiful views, good food we felt safe And actually roamed the hotel to see what we could see everything was exceptional. nice staff with good attitudes easy access to the strip. Amazing rooms I consider this hotel low key spot clean rooms and bathrooms

reviews.title: Daily Deposit
reviews.text: We called ahead of time to check on whether of not the pool is open , we were told we could use the heated pool at the Palms Resort and Spa. So we booked through Expedia and we also requested not to get a handicap room . When we arrive we were then told of a $50 daily deposit so that was $300 right off the bat and then of course the resort fee of $28 a day . When we got to the room at 2am it was a handicap room so the next day we had to change rooms . When we went to the "heated pool" it was not heated ,so that was a bust . We will not be staying at the Palms again .Off the strip and no pool and a daily deposit on top of the resort fee .

reviews.title: Worst hotel experience ever
reviews.text: I have never had to write a negative review online, but for Palms Place, I believe I need to. (YES Even after 4-months!) The experience at Palms Place was AWFUL. To top it off I wrote a letter to them on their website and they never responded.  The letter said: "My boyfriend and I booked 3-nights, August 2015.We arrived excited but when we checked into our room, it was terrible. There was a piece of metal hanging in the walkway from the kitchen counter, stains all over the walls (looked like vomit), the bathroom wasn't clean etc. We snapped a few photos to show downstairs. "David from Columbia" was the rudest employee we've ever encountered! He insisted this was "normal wear and tear," and said we could wait to have our room cleaned. When we got upset about the inconvenience he told us, "You can leave if you want to, just let me know." We were so applaud we cancelled our entire stay, and had to book another hotel, last minute. This put a negative damper on our trip."In short, we left the hotel and had an excellent experience at Vdara, but we spent way more money than we intended to! DON'T BOOK AT PALMS PLACE, STAY AWAY!!!

reviews.title: Disappointing! Another big LV hotel with no personal touch!
reviews.text: I stayed here one night while passing through Las Vegas on business. I was disappointed. The Palms brand is one I heard of and thought this would be a nice treat to stay here. I would have preferred a chain hotel catering to business travelers any day over this hotel! This hotel is not 4.5 stars. The latest scam by Las Vegas hotels is the "Resort Fee". A mandatory $28 charge giving you stuff you won't use and don't have time for. The only thing that made me OK with the resort fee was free internet. But NO, not so fast. The free internet was so slow you can't hardly send an email. If you want average Internet it's another $10 per day. For $28 a day resort fee, they should provide lightning fast internet. Why would it be an option to pay more for faster speed capable of sending an email when the resort fee is to include "free" internet?!?! Just charge a flat room rate, include basic quality services you would expect of a 4 or 5 star hotel and leave it at that. To top it off, I simply asked for a wine bottle opener. They charged $2.50 plus a $1.00 service charge to deliver a cheap plastic bottle opener that probably cost $0.05 and was virtually impossible to use to open a wine bottle. Hardly 4-5 star service!!! Avoid all mega large Las Vegas hotels charging "Resort Fees"!!! Service is horrible and the hotels are scamming people with "Resort Fees"!!!

reviews.title: Yuck!
reviews.text: Challenging to get in.  Valet parking was full, so parking was quite a schlep.  Room was kind of interesting, but you could see someone in the shower from anywhere in the bedroom.  Most disturbing, when we moved the sliding table over a bit (as it is designed to do), it was absolutely filthy!!!  We talked to the front desk about this, and frankly, she just didn't care!!!!  What a disappointment.  I don't prefer to be faced with inch deep filth in a place where I stay.

reviews.title: Amazing experience!
reviews.text: I stayed at Palms Place a while ago and I'm only getting around to reviewing it now, but Palms Place is an amazing hotel! The rooms were gorgeous with great views of the strip and even the base room has a ton of space. The bathroom was amazing. It was all-marble with a Jacuzzi and a separate rain shower, and a TV over the sink/vanity area. The rest of the room had 2 big TVs, one in front of the bed and one in the living room area. There was also a full kitchen with a giant minibar, dishwasher, fridge...everything. The staff was also very nice. It's not on the strip but it's very close, and since it's just off the strip it has amazing views of the whole strip, which was beautiful to look at. The Palms Place was great!

reviews.title: my stay at the palms
reviews.text: i recently stayed at the palms while i was on holiday.its a fantastic hotel with stunning mountain views over las vegas.very comfortable rooms.nothing to fault.was incredible opening the curtains every morning to that amazing view.the staff were all very courteous and polite and respectful.id previously said i was unaware of the resort fee and security deposit you have to pay on arrival..id like to make it clear this was an error on my part and i unreservedly apologise to joseph and the staff at the palms.this information was indeed on the site id booked through and it was my fault for not reading the booking properly...half hour walk into the strip or you can get the shuttle i didnt mind the walk was super weather.wouldnt hesitate to return and stay at the palms when im in las vegas again.

reviews.title: Modern condos off the strip
reviews.text: This is a great location if you have a car. Parking was easy, and it was easy to drive to hotels on the strip and park there. All parking was free.These are more like condos with a small kitchen and big bathrooms. The room was modern, comfortable and clean. The bed was a dream to sleep in. Note, that although there are balconies, they are locked off unless you are an owner.Only suggestions I would make to the hotel is that 1) There is some wear and tear (Ex. tub needs recaulking) that should be taken care of.2) When you pay 28 per night for a resort fee, that should include the "fast wifi". Only the slow wifi is included. (It was, however, just fast enough to stream netflix or youtube)We have stayed a lot of places in Vegas, but really loved the comfort and style of these rooms. We will definitely stay here again!

reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text: When arriving in the room we found one tv not working, the shower door wouldn't open and the safe was locked. This was fixed on the spot but should have been fixed before we checked in.Service is poor, room cleaning and restocking of mini bar seems not be a daily routine, so beware if you stay longer than 1 night.Location is good, if you have a rental car it only takes minutes to get to the strip.

reviews.title: Best time EVER!!!
reviews.text: e Palms Place Spa amd Resort was a wonderful place to spend our honeymoon.   It's located just off the strip, it has so much to do you really don't ever have to leave the property.   We stayed in the 1 bedroom suite. ..AMAZING!! Could stay forever! The best views of the mountains and the Strip!!  Room is equipped with full kitchen/washer/dryer, fireplace,  1.5 baths and beautiful soaking jacuzzi in the bedroom overlooking the Strip. The only problem was that the pots, pans, plates etc were not in the room and had to be specially requested, several times before being delivered.   We had a little bit of difficulty with the front desk. ..only 1 person to check a long line of people in and kept us waiting all day for an upgrade to the 1 BR suite,  meanwhile they had us check out of the first room so by 6pm we were trying to get management to place us in a new room. We will definitely be back. ..we will be sure to request that the kitchen be equipped with dishes etc prior to our arrival.  Great buffet,  many restaurants,  great casino.  Housekeeping was awesome!!

reviews.title: Wauw what an experience
reviews.text: We booked a suite in this hotel for one night. Wauw this was great; The suite at least 200m2 with a livingroom, bedroom, kitchen, big bathroom and a spa in the livingroom ! The whole suite was full of windows so we had a great view over Las Vegas. On top of that the price was absolutely not expensive!
