In NYC we had a very tiny room for this price.Takes 10 minutes to go to the Strip by taxi, they are in front of the entry of the hotel. Very friendly staff,Take note that Palms has two buildings, the "chique" resort and the "regular" Palms Casino hotel; We slept in the regular.

reviews.title: Excellent stay. 5 stars all the way.
reviews.text: The place more than meets expectations. Over the top style, very comfortable. These are suites, not hotel rooms; streamline design. Bathroom is big, room is big, bathroom has a whirl pool bath with a ceiling shower and a glass door...TV in bathroom, two TVs in space; one if front of bed, and the other in front of couch and living area. Over the top amenities and easy access to the strip. Free parking. Thoroughly enjoyed our stay there. Pillow top bed, really comfortable. Beautiful view, we were on the 25th floor. Balcony, but no access, all balconies are locked. Classy and elegant. It's such a good deal just a 5 minute drive to Strip, easy access...couldn't recommend more.

reviews.title: What an amazing stay!
reviews.text: I was a little concerned given some of the reviews. This is a new building, built or rather opened within the past decade. The entrance is not busy, drop off is available or valet. We just parked and walked in, or I would drop my wife off at the door due to the wind during our trip. We were very happy with our room. We wanted the kitchen and really wanted the Jacuzzi. The kitchen is nice it has an extra fridge, which isn't stocked, so you have room for some of your own groceries or drinks. We asked for some glasses and other kitchen items. The room was clean having some minor damage to one of the televisions, which I only saw when the morning sun hit the screen. The bed I was concerned wasn't going to be comfortable when I first saw it, but we both slept great on it. The Jacuzzi tub is a great size for 2 people, plenty of room to be comfortable and able to move around a little. We had the strip side view and enjoyed the quiet smoke free environment. We loved the Brenden Imax theater, at The Palms Casino, which has a Monday 5 dollar movies all day. A great deal that you can use the sky walk to access from the 2nd floor. Didn't use the spa like we wanted to, but if we stay again we will try next time. It would be nice if the spa was a little more affordable for guests. They charge $25 per guest to use the Hammam at Drift Spa, this isn't included in the resort fee which is $28.00 per night with tax. Parking never was an issue. We were able to park on the ground floor of the garage or out in the open parking just a little way from the entrance to the hotel. I would recommend this to couples, the room is very accommodating. If you were with a friend, or family member it would not offer enough privacy to make the room comfortable to shower, use bathroom and dress in. If someone is wondering why only 4 stars... I've stayed at better places and don't want to overrate a place solely due to it being very good in all categories. If I could I would give The Palms Place a 4 1/2 star rating.

reviews.title: Wonderful but not perfect
reviews.text: My husband and I stayed here as a last minute vacation. We prefer not staying on the strip because we always rent a car and its more quiet and laid back than the strip. We chose the Palms Place because our last minute trip gave us limited choices for our price range. We originally had reservations at the Palms hotel in a standard room. After I booked it, I started reading all the negative reviews of the shabby looking standard rooms and how the superior rooms were renovated. I called the Palms and asked about upgrading. The rep I spoke to said for the same $20 a night it cost to upgrade to the superior room at the hotel, I could upgrade to a studio in the Palms Place condo next door. That was the best money I ever spent! We not only had a panoramic view of the strip, we had a mini kitchen, a humongous room with 2 flat screen TVs and a king sized bed, a 3rd TV in the marble bathroom, and a jetted bathtub. A million times better than a standard room with two queen beds! The only minor things were some of the furniture was worn and needed replacing. The WiFi wasn't strong and we had trouble connecting. I was also hoping for a washer/dryer but not in this room. Also, when we arrived, we asked the concierge for a good place to get a burger. He said McDonalds. Not funny, Jerk.  A concierge is supposed to be helpful and answer your questions, give you suggestions when you ask for places to eat, and offer to make reservations-not be a Smart Mouth. I would tell management to transfer him to housekeeping so he can be Mr Funnyman to a toilet brush. Otherwise our stay was terrific. My other highlight was my trip the Spa! I got a Massage/Facial Package for $99 and it was lovely. The ladies who worked on me gave me a terrific recommendation to get my hair cut at the Palms Salon by Tory. Best haircut I ever got!!  We're so coming back to Palms Place.

reviews.title: Great weekend stay
reviews.text: Stood here this week and this place was amazing. Beautiful studio suite but was offered a 1 bedroom suite for $50 more a night. Although I didn't upgrade that's a lot cheaper than their listed rates. Had an issue with the safe in the room but security showed up in 5 minutes to open the safe for me. Love this hotel.

reviews.title: Ahhhhmmaaazzziiinnggg!
reviews.text: This is probably my favorite hotel I have stayed in Las Vegas. I love the proximity to everything without all of the crazy strip traffic. Upon Check-In, Chris T. was extremely helpful and ensured that we would have a pleasant stay. Be sure to find out everything that is covered by your resort fees (i.e. gym, transportation to the strip, etc.)This is one hotel you will not leave smelling like smoke-there is no casino in the actual resort. However, if you want to gamble, you can just walk through the sky tube and you will be in the Palm casino.The rooms were fantastic. They have everything you would need- refrigerator, microwave, teapot, toaster, etc. The restrooms were beautiful with a huge jetted bathtub. This is a place that you can spend a week and never feel crowded or that something was lacking. I cannot wait to return, this is going to be the first place I check availability when I am traveling to Las Vegas.

reviews.title: disappointing
reviews.text: when we arrived, there was a long check in line, and with only one person at reception, it did not get better.  Finally we were able to check in after about 30 minutes.  The room itself was nice and we were happy with the accommodations themselves

reviews.title: Changes are occurring. Some good, some...
reviews.text: This has been one of my favorite hotels since it opened. Just make sure you are booking Palms "Place" or you may end up at The Palms which is OK if you are a 24/7 Party Animal. Nine Steak House is really good. Not among the Top 5 but definitely in the Top 10. They have ruined Simon's restaurant. It is basically "Johnny Rockets" with a luxurious surrounding. Can't say if I will go back or not. P.S. Certain staff Members are absolutely wonderful.

reviews.title: Nice but not really a hotel
reviews.text: This is a service apartment, so don't expect the level of service of a hotel. The rooms are modern and comfortable. Check-in took 45 mins as there was only 1 staff working. It was good valve for money

reviews.title: Not to far away but far enough
reviews.text: we loved the palms place. Rooms were clean and well kept. We absolutely loved the beds and the waterfall shower head. The full stove and kitchen was also a nice addition. Would definitely stay again. Enclosed walkway/access to palms for gambling is also very useful.

reviews.title: 1 week visit
reviews.text: spent a week for work.  600 sq foot suite. 2 large screens; nice kitchen set-up. quiet room.  great cocktail bar in lobby.  have to take 2 people movers to get to casino; no biggy.  large sports bar. very good staff.  close to strip

reviews.title: Palms Place: Sanctuary Among Vegas Madness!
reviews.text: Loved staying at Palms Place. The studio/condo I rented through AirBNB was perfect for my week long stay during a busy trade show. The staff and check-in process was seamless with a nice option to valet park or self park not too far away. Since I rented through AirBNB, I didn't pay a resort fee, so that was nice as well. The room was wonderful with a stainless kitchenette stocked with a toaster, blender, utensils and coffee machine. The bathroom was all marble with a delightful rain shower overhead. The only reason I didn't give the stay a full five stars was due to the fact that the second TV and other showerhead didn't work. Other than that, it was awesome! Oh, and if you want to hang out in the casino and eat a quick meal, it's a short walk through the Sky Tube to Palms Casino. Easy breezy!

reviews.title: Pleasure trip
reviews.text: Family vacation. Room, spacious, kitchen usage...3rd stay at this locatin...loving it every time....will stay here again.  Hotel should offer some special discount for us regulars. It s great that we re just minutes away from the strip.

reviews.title: Great stay at Palms Place Hotel
reviews.text: To be honest I was a bit worried due to some of the reviews on here but we booked it as it looked great.It is off the strip - which is why we chose it, but to be aware of this, if you want to be in the centre of the action. Also note, that Las Vegas isn't really designed for walking! We hired a car and there was loads of free parking right at the hotel, which was great.Had nothing to worry about - all the staff were really friendly, the hotel was spotless, room was massive, the bed was super comfortable, the bathroom was amazing, with a drench shower and normal shower and whirl pool bath, the water was always hot. It had the most extensively stocked mini bar I've ever seen in a hotel - you could do some damage with that collection! It was just a great stay. We also had a great view, despite not managing to get a room on a higher floor. It was also very quiet (despite being very busy!), which in sin city, is amazing. There is a shuttle bus that goes from the Palms hotel to Caesars Palace - I would say, this could go on a bit later than 8PM? Seems a bit early to finish. The breakfast is through in the Buffet Bistro bit near the casino, the selection was fabulous, and the food was really nice. I liked the fact there wasn't a casino directly in the hotel but should you wish, it's right next door. The only downside, was the hotel trying to charge me for breakfast - when it was included in what I'd booked with Booking.com. So check your bill on leaving the hotel!! I would definitely recommend staying here. We also stayed at the Trump hotel, and I'd stay at Palms Place again over the Trump hotel....

reviews.title: Rather Disappointing 4.5 Star Hotel
reviews.text: We booked this hotel through Priceline.com so we didn't know the hotel name, but it was listed as a 4.5 star property. This property is actually a residence tower associated with the Palms Hotel, but apparently they rent out some of the studios and one-bedroom apartments on a nightly basis to hotel guests. As such, and considering the 4.5 star rating, I expected a very nice property. Unfortunately, it missed the mark in a number of areas to be rated this high.  At most it is a 4, perhaps a 3.5.This hotel, like many these days, charges a resort fee on top of the nightly rate.  For this, you get the use of the pool, "free" valet parking, and "free" wi-fi. The vehicle approach to the hotel is rather odd, almost as a second thought through the parking lot of the Palms. The entry is also small and tight and unable to handle the arrival/departure of more than just a few guests at one time. This is probably due to the fact it was designed primarily as a residence, and not a hotel. Despite the wait, the valet parking and bell staff where excellent once we reached the front of the line.Check-in staff were swift and courteous. We were given a studio, which compared to a hotel room was very generous in size and included a small kitchen. I'm not a fan of the ultra-contemporary interior design, but that is a personal preference. However, the furniture and flooring have seen much wear and are in need of replacement: Scratched wood flooring; scratched and chipped laminate and wood veneer furnishing. Ignoring those issues, the view from our room on the 35th floor toward the Strip was fantastic, especially at night.We visited the pool, which is of a nice design. However, there are three cabanas near the entry to the pool area that seem to have been (for the lack of a better word) abandoned or turned into storage space for old pool furniture.  A very odd greeting to the pool area.  In addition, the cushions on the lounge chairs were simply filthy!  This was remedied by covering them with towels, but this is simply unacceptable for a hotel of the stated star rating. The pool waitress was attentive in serving us outrageously priced drinks. ($14 for a beer? Really?)We stopped by the cafe just off the pool for a late afternoon snack.  We were never greeted, leading us to believe it wasn't open, although we saw two tables at which people were eating.  We waited a sufficient period of time, but left and moved on to a restaurant outside the hotel.Check-out was painfully long, with only two staffers at the front desk. Not sufficient for the number of guests checking out.It is hard to complain considering what we paid via Priceline.com.  However, this hotel is over-rated at 4.5 stars and I wouldn't deliberately select to stay at this hotel again.

reviews.title: Rooms great, lobby ?
reviews.text: The room was five stars, the check in area and corridor to the casino we encounter a few shady characters. Because it is not a true hotel, but a individual own condominium there is a somewhat bare bones staff in the lobby area.

reviews.title: Great experience
reviews.text: Really enjoyed staying at palms place. One of the best places I have ever been to! The room is amazing, and we got great view as well. Fairly cheap, and the food at the bistro buffet was good. Couldn't believe the beer and wine was included with the food!

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: Upon arrival at 12:00am, we could not pull our car upfront because of a bunch of limousines and huge monster looking trucks. We parked in self park and had to carry our luggage to check in. Then at check in there was a long line with only 2 people working. I complained and was given an upgraded suite. Our reservation had been in the hotel but the so called upgrade was next door. We had to carry our luggage all the way over to Palms place. The room at first glance seemed nice, had a great view of the strip. First of all the balcany was locked so you cant use it. The pillows were feather instead of down and very uncomfortable.  The marble tile floor had years of filth built up in the grout and corners. The spa tub was nice if you dont mind looking at molding caulking around the rim. I have no idea how this hotel is rated a 4 star resort. The casino and hotel over all has lots of differed maintenance.

reviews.title: Not impressed
reviews.text: I've stayed at Best Westerns nicer than the Palms Place. When I checked into my room, the overall cleanliness of the space was dismal. The remote for the tv was covered in something sticky... There were false eyelashes on the night stand... The glass on the balcony which you can't even used was completely smudged. For a "4.5 star" hotel this one did not make the cut. While the public areas of the Palms were lovely, the room itself is not one I will pay to stay in again.

reviews.title: Oh palms... What happened to you?! :(
reviews.text: Having lived in Southern California, I am a frequent visitor at Vegas.  Over the past 2 years, the Palms Place had become our favourite.  They have updated and pristine rooms, and the drive to the strip is very short as well.  They late night view of the city from their 37th floor elevator window is both comforting (beats the windy streets) and mesmerizing.  This time like many others, we traveled over the Halloween weekend.  We booked 2 neighboring rooms on the 39th floor with a king bed and a pull-out sofa bed (dreaded sleeping on this! :-/ ).  Following are the issues we found with 1 of our rooms on entering:1. Bathroom door did not lock (someone came in to fix it, but was back to square one the next day)2. The ice maker in the refrigerator did not work (No ice machine on the floor, however housekeeping sent us a bucket on request)3. There was a pair of used socks!!! (ewww!!) in the shelf below the tv!!!On mentioning these issues to the manager/front desk we were not given another room (Halloween weekend, all rooms were apparently full within 5min of us checking in (when checking in we were given the option of other rooms)!!)  While they did send in someone to fix the lock, given multiple issues in the room I think (sadly) the hotel's standards are degrading.... It's not old enough to have so many issues and if they continue with this kind of housekeeping, the day is becomes comparable to all the substandard hotels on the the strip wont be far.Please make things right, you aren't far off yet!P.S: The wifi doesn't reach the rooms either :(

reviews.title: Do not waste your money on an upgrade
reviews.text: I would recomend that you stay at one of the strip hotels.  We stayed at the Palms Place one bedroom suite and even though we paid for an upgrade to a higher floor we were not allowed to use the balcony, when asked they said it was not part of the deal and balcony use is owners only.  After complaining to the manager Nathan he said he would allow it but they did not do it and when the did come up after several calls we were told that due to keys broken in the lock they cannot accommodate the request, he gave us $50 food credit really? Stay at the strip hotels!

reviews.title: Expected much more
reviews.text: To far of the main strip, to much transportation expenses.Hotel clean! But very stale, deserted, depressing.No coffee shop attached. Need to walk to casino to get all you need. But even the casino was empty. Hooters food horrible.

reviews.title: An honest review- Nice room, horrible check-in, bad service
reviews.text: This is probably the only bad experience I've had with a resort in my 10 or so trips to Vegas.I called ahead and notified I would be arriving past midnight. They said it was fine. Arrived around 1:15am to the lobby, there was only 1 person at the desk and 2 guest ahead of me. Took exactly 51  minutes to check in. The man at the front desk helped a girl that had barely arrived to check in ahead of me when he saw I was there first and I had been waiting for nearly 30 minutes. He then tried to give me another room at the Palms casino because they were out of rooms and the one reserved for me had a "crack" on a window. He told me I wouldn't have to pay the difference for the other room at the Palms Casino. While he showed me pictures of the other room on a Ipad, I looked at the reservation prices on my phone at hotel.com.The room he was offering was a lot smaller and about $20 less than the one I had booked. Hmmmm yea I wouldn't have to pay a difference because the room was less.  I told him no and I'd take my room as is.When I finally got to my room (around 2:25am), I inspected all the windows and glass panes with a flashlight. I found no crack. I like to give credit where credit is due so I will say that the room itself was really nice, bed was comfortable , restroom was nice.Wifi is limited to only 1 device per day.Room had 2 TV's on of the remotes batteries was dead and the balcony door was locked. My girlfriend took a $3 Snicker's from the mini bar. She told me it was hard as a rock when she bit it. I thought maybe it was cold from the refrigerator but when we checked the expatriation date, it had expired almost 2 years ago!I called room service and explained them the situation. The lady who answered was very apologetic and removed the charge from my bill.I tried to fill the tub only to find out the Hot tap wasn't working, I had to fill the tub with the shower head which took over an hour.At night there was 1 closet light that wouldn't turn off when the door was shut. The light would illuminate the room through the middle crack. The second night I folded a piece of paper and placed it between the door and the switch and that did the trick. Overall the room was nice and modern, very roomy, but I've never stayed at a place where I could count the number of things wrong with a room with my fingers. I'm usually not one to ask for special services and I didn't even complain for the things wrong with the room (minus the candy bar). But the service at the check in left a lot to be desired. Perhaps if I had checked in during "regular" hours the service might of been different. But the way the man at the front desk tried to "solve" my scenario was not the best. Would I recommend it to a friend. Probably not. Would I stay here again. No.

reviews.title: Great rate off the strip
reviews.text: I had a one night stay in Vegas so I wasn't going to have time to enjoy the strip so I decided to stay at the Palms Hotel and Spa because it was significantly cheaper. I got a full kitchen, fridge and a large premium bathroom for pennies on the dollar. Overall a nice stay and the extra savings was a bonus.

reviews.title: Hidden Gem in Las Vegas
reviews.text: Having stayed there close to 200 nights, it's still the hidden gem!  From Tony at the Bell Desk, to Casandra @ the front desk, Henry in Valet, they are always incredible with greetings and asking if I need any help!  The rooms are Excellent for the value.

reviews.title: Palms
reviews.text: Overall the hotel and casino was pretty good. The room was clean and quite large, with a good view over the strip. The bathroom was luxurious for the amount we spent. The strip was a distance away, but there was a shuttle that takes you straight to Caesars Palace which was great. My main gripe is the 'resort fee' that was not disclosed at time of booking and came as a shock at the end of the stay. At $28p/n for use of the pool/gym and WIFI, I thought this was excessive and came as a shock. Another thing was that the door to the room balcony was locked, so we couldn't fully enjoy the view.

reviews.title: Large and Comfortable
reviews.text: We stayed at Palms Place for a few days whilst in LV. Palms Place offers you humongous clean and comfortable serviced apartment rooms. The views from the room is magnificent. Coming back to the room at nights and seeing the lights on the strip is excellent way to finish the day. It is located off the strip. Having a rental car helps solve the location issue. There is no parking fee for self parking. Price is reasonable for such a large room off the strip.

reviews.title: Big rooms, beat up facility
reviews.text: Palms Place is really a condo building offered as a hotel. So if you like big rooms, this is a good place.  Buying a package on Expedia, we stayed 5 nights (Sunday thru Thursday) in a 1 bedroom condo with great views of the strip for $158/night plus $28 resort fee.  And a big one-bedroom, with 2 bathrooms.  That is something you'll find hard to match.The location is actually pretty good.  The attached Palms Casino was overhauled in the last year, and is pretty nice for gambling.  You can easily walk to Gold Coast Casino for breakfast or lunch, or next door there is the Rio with nice gambling, food and the Penn & Teller Show.  Walk the opposite direction and it's a short stroll to the Orleans for other gambling and food.  Or, if the weather is nice it's a pleasant 2 mile walk to the strip and all it offers.  There also is a shuttle available to the strip from the Palms at no charge.  Like everywhere in Las Vegas, parking is free.  There is self park or valet, your option.But, this place is beat up.  We've stayed here 3 times in the last couple of years, primarily for the big room at a good price.  But wear and tear is obvious.  Don't expect an Aria room at this price.  Also, service is spotty.  We arrived at 5:00pm and the room was not available.  Surprising.  Most housekeeping seems to happen between noon and 5:00.  There are no ice makers, since you are expected to have ice from fridge in your room - but whether the ice maker works is spotty.This place is spotty, but it is a good value.

reviews.title: A Great Room, But There Are Issues
reviews.text: We stayed here because of the price - I got a deal on hotwire, and it was a Friday night, and my usual hotel of choice was fully booked.  For what we paid, (about $100 plus the dreaded $28 resort fee), it was a bargain.  For some reason though, the way they are running the place succeeds in minimizing the assets they have.Check-in was slow.  Although there were only a handful of people in front of us in line, and three people were working the desk, it took a long time (20 minutes) before we were attended to.  Once we reached the counter, though, the staff was polite and friendly, and gave us a room key quickly, on the 34th floor.  When we went to the room, we were immediately impressed.  It was huge, with a king-size bed and a pull-out sofa, a full kitchen, a jacuzzi bath, enormous windows that looked out on a balcony, and a great view of the strip.Then we started to notice things.  Many of the lights didn't work.  There were no sheets for the pull-out sofa, either on the bed or in the closet.  The door to the balcony was locked.  There were no plates or silverware for the kitchen.    We called for plates and silverware, and they were quickly brought up.  We called for sheets for the sofa bed, and we were told, pretty abruptly, to look in the closet.  When I said the closet did not have any sheets, they said they would bring them up.  40 minutes later, still no sheets.  I called again.  They said they would bring them up.  Then housekeeping called back and told me, in an exasperated manner, to look in the closet.  I assured them I was looking in the closet, and there were no sheets.  They said they would deliver them. I don't know when they did, because I went out, but when I returned the sheets were there.  Even then, though, the sofa bed was not made with the sheets, but they were tossed carelessly on the main bed.I called about the balcony, and was told it could not be opened for security reasons.  I have no idea what that means.  Whose security?The internet is limited to one device, works at a relatively slow speed, and is capped, unless you want to pay extra.To top things off, when I went to check out, there was a minibar charge on the bill although nothing inside the minibar had been touched.  When I called, they removed it, but told me that if housekeeping found anything missing, it would be added back on.There is so much right about this place - the facilities are terrific, parking was easy very closer to the entrance, you don't have to walk for miles to get to your room, the location is great both for the Strip and for the amazing Chinatown area.  It is a shame that there are so many challenges for the staff to overcome in running the place.

reviews.title: Nice hotel, off the stip, very quiet
reviews.text: This hotel is off the strip and not as close as I'd like it to be, but I guess that costs extra. It's one of the three hotels on the Palms property. We didn't really explore it much since it just seemed to have a lobby with one bar (it was very nice though). It has a modern feel to it and the room was very nice; it had a lot of storage space and extremely spacious. I just wish the bathroom had better lighting.

reviews.title: A week at Palms Place
reviews.text: The room was LARGE....actually 2 room, 1 1/2 bath suite.Living room and bedroom completely separate with sliding doors.  View was great with walls of windows. Very modern room, mirrors, shower big enounh for 4 people, Jetted soaking tub.Gas fireplace.   However, it is away from strip, but a shuttle takes you to Ceasers-but only until 8PM(cab back $10) The casino is nothing special-will want to go to strip, but coming back to nice big room relaxing  It is like a codo apartment rather than hotel room.

reviews.title: Nice hotel.  Great room.
reviews.text: Big room for the price.  Had a room on the 52nd floor with a great view.   Would have been nice if the door to the balcony opened but understand this could be a liability so no big deal.   The room had 2 TV's but the one in front of the sofa had a poor picture so just used the one in front of the bed.  Bathroom was nice but lighting was a little dark.   Would be better if the wall between the bathroom and the rest of the room was darker.  If someone turned the bathroom light on in the middle of the night or early morning, it lit up the whole room.   I found the room to be very quiet.  An advantage to not staying on the strip.  They did offer a free shuttle to the strip which runs every 1/2 hour from 11-8.  Would be nice if it ran later.  They were putting in new carpeting and wallpaper on our floor but by the 2nd day it was finished and never did hear the workers.   Staff was polite and helpful.   We didn't use the either pool but checked out both of them.  I did see dirty cushions on the chairs and the cabanas were small and didn't look clean.  Wouldn't pay extra to use one.  The food was great.  Would definitely stay here again and would recommend staying here.

reviews.title: Great Value for Price
reviews.text: We returned to the Palms Place because of the quality experience we enjoyed on our previous visit. I had requested a high, west facing floor both times, and was given rooms on the 52nd and 53rd floors. We enjoy the spaciousness of the studio units (600 square feet) and the fabulous bathroom with its rain shower head and individual sprayer, and the deep and roomy soaking jacuzzi tub. We have enjoyed the multiplex movie theater, food court, and Nove (the Italian restaurant) in the adjacent Palms towers. The price for our midweek stay was one of the best in the entire city.

reviews.title: Do Not Stay Here. It's Awful. !!!
reviews.text: I come to Vegas few times a year and I will NEVER stay here again. The people that work here have zero customer service skills. Internet and TV ISSUES: As we got to the room the sound on the TV was not working, neither was the free internet. I had to sit on the phone for 45 minutes with the internet provider to get the internet to work. When it finally did it was very slow. The next day I paid for the higher speed internet and it was still very slow. The TV sound got fixed by a technician but the channel line up is pretty lame.On the second night we decided to order a movie. The screen was blocked and said it was not available for my room.  When I called guest services they wanted me to get dressed, go downstairs and give them a credit card. This is after they charged me resort fees and took a rather large security deposit. In addition to that the cell signals have been knocked out so my LTE only had one bar. Balcony ISSUE: Balconies do not open, you are stuck in a room without ventilation. When I called and asked they gave me 6 different excuses why.DIRTY POOL CHAIRS: The chairs by the pool are disgusting. Full of gross stains and cigarette burns. Black Out Curtains ISSUE: Badly designed curtains that let a lot of sunlight in, especially on the bottom. Expect to be woken up with sunrise.

reviews.title: Nice stay, but a few issues
reviews.text: Stayed here for two nights mid-week, mid-October in a studio suite. I was very impressed by the size of the suite. The sofa was way bigger than expected and fairly comfortable. The bathroom was a really nice size, too, bright and spacious. The whirlpool tub, which my friend said was heavenly, was a bit odd because you had to walk though the shower. The kitchen had a nice fridge, a minibar, a dishwasher, and an automatic ice maker - which was a lifesaver. But don't expect any soap or glasses or dishes unless you call down - and you probably won't get enough.Like other reviewers, I noticed that the place is kinda getting rough around the edges. Dirty cushion here, peeling wallpaper there, gross corners, etc. A good deep cleaning would make the place sparkle. Yes, the entire building is a bit dark by design; I didn't mind it much. My biggest problem was with checkin. I specifically reserved a studio suite in the Palms Place building. But without saying a word, they assigned me a room in the regular Palms towers. I actually had to pull out the Rocketmiles reservation email to show her and then I was given the correct room. It's aggravating because I've read others that had the same issue, and I dislike the bait and switch tactics. Would I stay here again? Yes, but I know what to expect.

reviews.title: Key card did not work... Not a 4 star hotel.
reviews.text: I booked this hotel through hotels.com because it was rated 4.2 stars and the price was  decent.  We booked two rooms for four adults for two nights.  We couldn't get the key card to work for one of the rooms.  We were on the 27th floor and we had to go back to the reception area 4 times before they finally decided that they had to call a technician.  I asked to have our rooms changed and the receptionist offered a room on the 30th floor.  I was traveling with family so I wanted us to be on the same floor.  She tells me that there are no vacant rooms available at all, which was hard to believe.  She gave us two tickets for complimentary drinks and that was it.  No free upgrade, no waiving of the resort fee, which was $28 PER room PER night for the amenities we never had the time to use.  The hotel was not completely outdated but it wasn't managed well.  I could see it wasn't cleaned properly, bathroom wasn't very clean either.  The worst part of the room were the old mattresses on all four of our beds which gave us back pain the morning after.  We booked this hotel because we had a rental car, but if you don't plan on renting a car, this hotel is completely off the strip and it's not walking distance unless you plan on walking for 30 + minutes under the scorching sun.

reviews.title: Would not stay here again. Not a 4 star hotel.
reviews.text: Spent a couple of nights at this hotel but it  was truly disappointing.1. The lobby area is dark and very unwelcoming. 2. Our initial room reeked of cigarettes which I'm very sensitive to. After repeatedly reporting this to front desk, we were reluctantly given a different room. 3. Front desk staff are very unpleasant and lack people skills. 4. Rooms have a stale funky smell, like a drain or sewage smell .5 . There is no ventilation as balcony doors are locked. 6. Even though the room itself is modern it feels cold and non 'hotel -like'.Rooms lack attention to detail and seem to be neglected.  7. Wifi is limited to one device per room with a limit. 8. There are no kitchen utensils, if you'd like to use some you have to request it. 9. In all honesty the bell man,engineer and housekeeping lady were the only pleasant staff around.

reviews.title: Pleasantly surprised!
reviews.text: We were extremely happy with our room and stay at the Palms Place Hotel.  No question we would stay there whenever we are in Las Vegas again.  The bathroom was especially beautiful and unique.  We were there with friends and I know they loved the accommodations too.

reviews.title: Nice stay at Las Vegas !
reviews.text: We stayed 2 nights at Palms Place Hotel & Spa.Front desk staff were very efficient & kind,  and we had a lovely studio facing the Strip on the 51st floor !  ( what an incredible view !) Our Studio was extremely comfortable, spacious, and clean ! The incredible view was definitely a plus ! We enjoyed the pool at the Palms Casino, as we had access to both swimming pool: Palms Place & Palms Casino.Breakfast was ok (buffet style breakfast), but it's not very convenient to go all the way to the Palms Casino to enjoy it. Other than breakfast, the hotel is nice and clean & location is fine We were able to explore Las Vegas & Downtown very easily.

reviews.title: Could be great, but....
reviews.text: Palms Place has wonderful rooms with great views of the strip or the mountains. The rooms are spacious with stainless steel kitchenette and wet bar. The bedding was great and clean with duvet. Rooms needed urgent maintenance. Floors were clean but because of cheap material choices looked scuffed up and dirty. Internet experience was awful slow and capped. It also seemed like they blocked cell signals to sell their internet cap update. After all it could be great, but....

reviews.title: Stay
reviews.text: Awesome place. We had the view. Of the city      Great place to stay..they just have to upgrade the cleanlinrss of theirvroom. The desk receptionist are accommodating. Their night club is free when you stay. A lot of restaurants to choose from.

reviews.title: 2 Fatal Flaws...
reviews.text: Palms Place COULD near perfect if they could just fix two critical flaws.First, the good. I got a stellar deal of only $77 per night for two October weeknights. The location is close enough to the strip for a quick taxi over, but too far to walk (remember, Las Vegas blocks are looooong).Also good, not being attached to a smokey casino. The rooms were spacious with a kitchenette that would be perfect for families. Facilities were relatively new and modern. The studio had 2 TVs, with thoughtful plugs on the lamps by the bedside. The restaurant on the 6th floor gives a nice view of the small pool area. The salmon with veggies dish I ordered was better than expected. Now for the bad.1. Not only does Palms Place charge $28 per day resort fee, it doesn't include unlimited Wi-Fi Internet access. The Internet included is some sort of slow, capped package. You can upgrade to 2MB per day for something like $14 per day. What?! Either that was a typo or I misunderstood it. Any file these days is larger than 2MB. And to make things worse, that was PER DEVICE. Yes, you paid $28 resort fee for 1998 Internet, then another $7 to $14 for "upgraded" Internet that was just a tad faster, capped with a low ridiculous limit, and for only one device.This alone would make me consider boycotting Palms Place out of principle. If enough people complain, hopefully management will wake up and change this stupid policy.2. As described in other reviews, there's a sort of funky odor in the bathroom emanating from the drains. Anyone familiar with Vegas knows what I mean. It's that sewage stench in the streets and in certain restrooms. It's faint but obvious. For someone used to Asian countries like Taiwan, it's not a big deal. For others, I can see how it would be. I simply kept the bathroom door closed so it didn't leak out. But considering the nice facilities, the funky smell was offputting and out of place.So there you have it. Expensive, crappy Internet and a funky smell. Two fatal flaws in my opinion. If they fixed these two issues, this would be a no-brainer 4 star.Hello management?

reviews.title: Not what we paid for! Staff has zero customer service skills or empathy.
reviews.text: So we originally was booked with The Palms and this was the last 3 days of my honeymoon. While at the Palms I saw the pools hanging out of the hotel and told my wife we needed to splurge on the last night and get a pool suite. I called the operator (Billy) who told me those suites were $35,000! Okay not splurging that much but he did have a pool suite at Palms Place. He said as soon as you are ready we could check in to Palms Place. We packed went over checked in at the front desk, got our keys and headed up to the Penthouse suites. When we got near our room there was a ladder next to our door with part of the ceiling ripped off. We went in to our suite and was over whelmed by a sewer smell, it gets better! We went to look at the pool and the glass wall surrounding the pool was covered in blood. (no joke looked like CSI scene) At about the time when I was telling my wife their is no way I am staying here, 3 housekeepers came in and asked us what we where doing in the suite. I told the ladies they checked us in. She said the room wasn't ready and they shouldnt have checked us in. So back down to the front desk, gave us new keys and up to the 58th floor where are keys wouldnt work! back down to the desk and new keys. We got into the room and it looked great but the pool (jacuzzi) was cold. Called down and had engineering up to fix it because this is the reason we booked the room in the first place. So to make this short we had engineering up to that suite on 3 more occasions trying to fix our TV. Our engineer was a really nice guy and I wish I could remember his name but he was the only employee of this establishment that cared or even apologized for what we dealt with on our last day here. So to make matters worse by the time we where finally ready to get into the pool. (jacuzzi) it was so hot we couldnt get in. I had enough of people coming into our suite on our last night so we called it a night. When I checked out in the morning, I explained the situation to the guy at the front desk and I kid you not it was oh well you owe $$$. Not even sorry for your inconvenience. This would have been amazing if they could have sold us what we paid for. On a positive note, the views from the 58th floor are breathtaking and I was with my wife who always seems to make bad situations great. The Palms Place needs a lot of customer service training because I have had better at a Motel 6.

reviews.title: Off the strip - rooms need some attention
reviews.text: Our first visit to Vegas we did not realize that choosing a hotel on the other side of the highway would make visiting complicated. The hotel offers a free shuttle service that ends at 8pm. Rooms are large and modern but show signs of wear. I did enjoy the large windows and mountain view. The casino is a bit depressing compared to the ones on the strip.

reviews.title: Out of the way
reviews.text: Rooms are supposed to be modern, but instead feel cold.  Loose wiring on shelves and lights hung uneven.  Hallways smell bad.  It is really a condo that has been converted to a hotel.  Long walk to Palms next door

reviews.title: Construction!! Yikes!! No warning!!
reviews.text: Woke up to construction in the hallway, construction workers ripping up the wall paper and carpet.  Fumes, dust everywhere! Otherwise the room was awesome.  Great layout, clean, beautiful. Need better service at the front desk.

reviews.title: Luxurious and Roomy
reviews.text: I was pleasantly surprised to find the suite was quite large. Free wifi is available. The bathroom was also very nice and large, designed with floor to ceiling marble and a jetted tub. The customer service however was not as polished as the hotel itself. Several calls to concierge and valet went unanswered.

reviews.title: Very nice hotel with many small problems
reviews.text: The hotel in overall is great. If this was a 2/3* Days Inn, I would be happy to give it 100% rating. But from a hotel like this one, you are awaiting to be perfect and it was not.What was our biggest disappointment was that the pool was closed for a private party. As the pool was one of the main reasons to choose this hotel, it was a great disappointment. I think that it would be fair if the hotel gave a notice in advance so that you can rebook or gave some kind of compensation (e.g. discount from the resort fee, drink voucher or something). However, that didn't happen even when I complained at the reception.Second, the WiFi is poor. They call it high-speed internet, but once you log in, you see that you are limited by 1mbps. I think that was high-speed like 10 years ago. Also, there is only 1 device per room! In present, when everybody has a smartphone and the room is usually occupied by more than 1 person, it's definitely not enough.Thirdly, the service. As there is a kitchen in the apartment, we wanted to cook dinner (finally, after 2 weeks of staying in hotels and eating fastfood/restaurant food). There are no kitchenware in the place and you have to call for it. It took my 3 calls to finally get the kitchenware after more than an hour from my first call.And many other small gabs.On the bright side, the room was very nice and spacious, the hotel looked luxurious and there is a pretty good casino downstairs. It was about 5-10mins of taxi ride to the Strip and the hotel also provide a shuttle each 30mins (not working in the evening).

reviews.title: Good Stay @ The Palms!
reviews.text: Great deal on Travelzoo, was hoping they would've honored the second breakfast buffet deal for us with a lunch as we were leaving early, but the front desk said 'no' and wouldn't allow me to speak to management. Also check in took forever~they might need more than 2 clerks when there's a line-up 12 people deep!! Room was great and the pool was refreshing. We like the location away from the crazy strip. Would stay again.

reviews.title: Rude People
reviews.text: Hello, we stayed here from October 5-9, 2015. Hotel staff are rude and give bad service. We called front desk because the jacuzzi wasn't working, never got fixed. At the end we were overcharged for things we didn't even used and to top it off my husband got one candy bar and one coke from the mini fridge and were expecting to be charged for two candy bars and two drinks. I guess since we were two persons they just decided to charge us double. Very unsatisfied with everything. Will never stay here again. Thank you

reviews.title: One of my new favourites!
reviews.text: Super impresssed!!  We got a great deal on this hotel so wasn't too sure what to expect.  And some of the reivews weren't good, I really don't know why?!  The rooms were massive with fridge, sink, dishwasher, microwave, sitting area etc.  Bathrooms included a glass shower as well as a soaker tub and lots of mirrors. We had a great mountain-view room as well. Everything was clean and the staff were awesome.We had never stayed off the Strip before but the free shuttle is super handy and even taking a cab wasn't as expensive as we thought it would be.  Its also a non-gaming hotel so felt like a retreat coming home to. If we were in the mood for gambling or wanted different restuarants, the walk over to The Palms is really quick.Definitely recommend :)

reviews.title: A less expensive alternative but don't expect much
reviews.text: Located about a 30 minute walk from the strip,  the hotel is relatively inexpensive compared to the ones that are on the main drag.  The hotel staff is quite inexperienced and not very helpful.  Example would be upon checking I was given a room on the 38 th floor.  When the elevators opened up I was treated to a floor that had no wall paper,  carpet broken sheet rock and lighting provided by portable lights.  Returned to the front desk and after showing them a picture I took of the area,  they realized the floor was being renovated.  They had never seen what the area looked like.   Asked the concierge for directions and advise for dinner.  Had no clue.  So basically you are on your own.  Sometimes not a bad thing but be prepared.The room is a bit dated but you have a couch, bed, kitchen area and bathroom.  Hot water takes a while so start the shower and relax til the water gets to temp.  Had a view of the strip from the balcony but as many have said before the balcony is locked so you have no access.The gym closes at 7pm and when I asked if they had a sauna,  they do however it is a 25 dollar surcharge per use.   I asked if the resort fee of 25 dollars per day covers this and they said the resort fee covers the ability to get a newspaper in the morning at the front desk,  the ability to print a boarding pass and wifi.   Wifi,  well access is available in the room,  but at close to dial up speeds.  They do offer two other plans but at a substantial surcharge.  And remember it's only one asset per room.The Palm casino is close,  about a 5 minute walk and you have a moderate casino and some dining choices.  Tried Hooters for a quick bite and it's the first one I went to where the staff really made you feel like they didn't want to be there.  Maybe they didn't realize you don't go there for their great food choices.All in all,  it was an uneventful stay once I got to a room on a different floor,  but don't expect the services and flair that you find at some of the better known places along the strip.  You basically get what you pay for.

reviews.title: Brilliant hotel off the strip
reviews.text: After reading mixed reviews about this hotel was a little apprehensive to say the least.However our stay and room were brilloantCheck in was smooth and easy. Our room on the 9th floor had a brilliant strip view (shame about the locked balcony but safety first i presume).The room is self is huge and mosern. Very comfy king sized bed, seating area, two huge flat screens and the kitchenette area was a bonus- fridge especially.  The bathroom is fantastic!! Huge marble jacuzzi bath and rainforest shower Superb. AC was spot on too.Pool was calm and quiet if a bit small (palms itself has a bigger, more party orientated pool).All in all a brilliant hotel off the strip (half hourly shuttle to the strip provided til 8pm) and only about $7-8 for a uber into the centre of the action!! Ace!!

reviews.title: Really disappointed.
reviews.text: The hotel looks great on the Internet, however in reality it is dirty and in need of updating. We arrived after a long day, on entering our room it was clear it had not been cleaned, and there were random pills on the floor. We have a baby and a toddler so we were very concerned, and we didn't want to spend our holiday worrying what the kids might or might not find on the floor. We spoke to the management who were not bothered about this. Fortunately our Bellboy witnessed how bad the room was and got up moved to another room, which was very adequate, but no more.

reviews.title: Superficial Style Lacking Attention To Detail
reviews.text: I was hopeful this was going to be a great stay after looking at all of the reviews.  I did not  rely only on TripAdvisor as I booked this stay on 10/5/2015 via Expedia.com.  The staff were more than friendly and I thought this would be just as nice as my last three stays in The Cosmopolitan.  I checked in and walked through the "sky tube" to the tower and up to 29308.  There was an odor in the room I couldn't identify but it wasn't enough to ruin the stay.  It is a very nice room. Large and it has a view of the strip and the valley.  The balcony is inaccessible to those lodging but it was raining so nothing to miss there.  I actually booked the room because I was attending a party in the Paradise Tower (25201) and didn't want to worry about traversing Vegas once the party shut down.  When I got back to my room and it was time to wash and sleep I began to focus on the details.  There appeared to be significant water damage to the unit above (30208?) and the damage spread to this unit.  The odor could have been mildew.  The tub was a bit dirty and so was the shower.  I opted to forgo the tub.  The bedding was ripped in sections and the carpet was soiled.  Still, it was quiet, and well appointed for the lack of care in maintenance.  This property is on the bubble.  I hope they keep things going nicely as it has plenty of potential and I can see where it was once a great gem.  Do not pay >300\night for this room.  You will be disappointed you didn't grab a room on the strip.

reviews.title: Nice contemporary hotel.
reviews.text: Great place to stay if you like an European contemporary style. It is spacious, has all the amenities and doesn't have a casino in the lobby. Free self parking, wifi and a nice gym. Unfortunately the balcony has been locked at all times. The marble tiled floor in a shower stall is slippery. The kitchen cabinets, by design are lacking the door knobs. The $25 a day resort fee was unexpected surprise. I would still come back to this hotel and wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to my friends.

reviews.title: Vacation
reviews.text: Really nice place to go. Hallway had a little smell, really good place to stay. Really clean place, friendly people. I definitely recommend this place, wifi had a 12 hour limit for free. Not too far from the strip and not too busy in the surrounding area like the strip, best of both world.

reviews.title: Hidden Gem
reviews.text: This hotel/ condo was ideal! The room was huge, the pool was great, entire spot was very modern. There is a shuttle to the strip as well as reasonable price for taxis. Its nice to see the view of the strip from the room! Amazing view!

reviews.title: Great stay, huge room!
reviews.text: The (off-strip) Palms Place Hotel is a condo style setup- don't expect 5 star hotel service.The studio suite room was large and well appointed with a big bathroom and plenty of room for the family, one king bed plus sofa bed, and useful kitchenette.  Great view of the (nearby) strip. The pool area at the Palms Place is lovely and relaxing, but if you want action head to the adjoining Palms Casino hotel pool for a more vibrant scene. The hammam is a great space, very relaxing.Join Club Palms even if you are not much of a gambler- great buffet food offers for members. Great stay!

reviews.title: Feelings just like home!
reviews.text: I stayed here three nights, for the Electric Daisy Carnival.The room was beautiful and it included and full kitchen. The staff was very friendly. Just know that they don't have bell boys, so enjoy carrying all of your bags.

reviews.title: It started off on the wrong noteand ended on a worse one.
reviews.text: Where to start. I wish I could show video that would really drive this review home. So we got married on 9-12-15 in Boston, ma. We decided to do something different and go to Las Vegas for our honeymoon. Thinking that we would have so much fun and enjoy our time. When we arrived it was around 1 am. The person at the desk handed us a note saying that we were being placed on a floor with construction. I questioned if there was any other location that they could put us in because I was worried about the way the floor would smell and noise. He told me he would put us in a strip view because of the fact that there was construction. I questioned him again because i had called earlier in the week to confirm everything and we were never told about construction happening. To be honest we would have gone to their other property instead. I have asthma and dust is a huge trigger. We get to the 9th floor and there are no signs as to where to go, no carpet, the floor smelled like glue and it was so overly dusty that honestly no one should have been on the floor. We get into our room finally and the floor was dirty. Because our suitcase is a rolling one we brought even more dirt in with us.  I told my husband that I would call in the morning but I was so sleepy from the long travel. We get up in the morning and I call the phone number on the sheet. I ask for a manager. A lady said the manger was busy but she could help. I explained to her that we work up to the noise of construction workers spakling the walls and talking very loud and it was only 8am. She told us that she had another room she could be moved into but it would take 1 -2 hours. I said no problem and said thank you. Well we waited. Three hours later I called because and the lady said oh yea it will be ready in an hour to 2 hours. We decided to go out to the pool since we made a reservations months before for the cabana. We get there and the bar tender (which was so nice and sweet) told us that the first three were the best ones. We took the second one from the bar and there was stains on every pillow in there. The walls were dirty and it just didn't look clean. I went and got towels (again they were really nice) and I placed them down so we could sit down. We got drinks  and something to eat but I couldn't finish my food in there. We left and closed out our account because it was so bad and had no plans on coming back. We ended up giving the bartender a 60 dollar tip because of the minimum amount that you had to spend. By that time I was sure that they room was ready. We went back up and I called and they lady told us again it would 1-2 hours. (if you are keeping count this is the 3rd time) So we decided to take a nap. When we work up to the noise of something being mixed and out room smelling like Paint. I went and opened the door and I couldn't get out because the door had been covered in full plastic. I called down again to the manager that told us this time she had a room she could move us into and someone would be right up to hep move us. Well, No one ever came. 30 mins later my husband packed everything and said we are going down stairs. One of the works on the floor cut us out so we could leave and we had to wait out there until the elevator came the workers outside asked if we wanted masks (because they were painting and they had them). So, I thought you are telling me that they thought it was ok to put people on these floors, breathing this stuff in when they workers had things because it isn't stuff that you should be. So, we get down stairs the guy at the desk was a jerk that i was in tears. I explained that this was ok and they whole issues that I had. He said we because we upgraded you that should make you happy. I told him the point is that this should have never happened in the first place. I would have never stayed here if i had known and further more I didn't appreciate the tone that he was making it sound like I asked to be on that floor in the first place. We get to the new room and while it was nice I was so upset about everything that happened. So our first day was completely ruined and the customer service was horrible. On Thursday of our stay I called to speak to a manager because I was in a elevator and someone that had the same problem was telling us that they didn't have to pay for the day and was moved into the same kind of room we were. So I called downstairs and I was told they couldn't do anything plus they put the complaint in as just a noise complaint not as what it was. I didn't appreciate the customer service, the fact that they thought that this was ok to do and then the fact that they treated people differently. I will never stay there again and I will make sure that my friends and family doesn't either. Just a side funny note, the floor was done two days later. So I would say that maybe they just shouldn't have put people on the floor until they were done. If you want to see the video I did post on their facebook site.

reviews.title: Lipstick on a Pig plus Extreme Resort fees!
reviews.text: Stayed here Monday through Wednesday, you walk in and it's fairly modern stylistically, but as the old saying goes you cant just slap lipstick on a pig. Staff was fine, courteous and nice. The experience however was awful! We went up to our room on the 35th floor and from the moment we stepped off the elevator you can just kind of tell that the stay wasnt going to go well. From the peeling wall paper, to the scratches on the walls down the hallway, to the missing arrows on which way the rooms were counting up/down this is hardly the 4 and a half stars priceline rated it at and 4 stars that trip advisor rates it as. The room, again, just like with the hotel lobby, you walk in and are relatively impressed by the ambiance, the modern look, and the view.. or lack there of. Well lets start simply by saying if you're not a shorter person the functionality of this room is completely lost on you. Unfortunately i'm taller so everything is a strain and a pain in order to use. Then you get to actually using the room for it's functionality and that again is where the problems arise. The floors were dusty and could use a cleaning, the decor has seen better days and looked to be beat up (chips, scratches, dirt everywhere), the furniture looked to be purchased second hand with the amount of fabric rips and upholstery missing. There are 3 tv's in the room.. 1 didnt work/had no remote to the second tv was a standard old lcd tv and the third was right in your face in the bathroom. The rain fall shower however was nice, but it wasnt designed properly so unless you messed with the shower head you were going to have a pool escaping your shower into the main room. The kitchenette was fine.. standard amenities there.. the dual fridge was ridiculous.. The top of which being the mini bar with extremely dated products inside of it. The bottom being a college style dorm fridge which clearly hasnt been properly cleaned in some time because it smelled of something fierce. Now onto the resort fee.. I'm sure everyone and their mother has complained about this evil of Las Vegas so i will not waste my time other than to say. $25/day plus tax for wifi that was ridiculously slow for only 1 device per room?! took this bit of Vegas thievery to unprecedented heights!!!.  Long and the short of it, I fell into the allure of the star rating on websites and wanted to stay in a nicer place this is one that I will not be attempting to stay at ever again. No, thank you! Keep it!

reviews.title: Nice hotel but bad management
reviews.text: This place could easily get better ratings if not for the following reasons:- the rooms are nice but already showing signs of wear - the chairs all have scratches and marks on them, the floor has scratches all over it, and the furniture is definitely looking a bit sad. - the room hasn't been cleaned very well, the toilet smells pretty bad (as if it hasn't been properly washed in quite a while), and the everything has minor smears or stains on it.- took a very long time to check in - definitely more than 2 attendants needed at key check in times- the wifi sucks!! Only one device per room allowed?? And it's quite slow. Considering you pay a $25 resort fee which includes "complimentary wifi". So basically $25 for slow wifi on one device.- WORST OF ALL: the pool was closed all three days due to a "private event". I've paid good money for this hotel and the facilities that come with it, especially the pool, and it's unacceptable that I can't use it on any of the days that I stay here. Not cool.Like I say - nice hotel, but a lot of things wrong with how it's being run.

reviews.title: Quiet Reprieve From The Strip
reviews.text: Since I do not gamble, I wanted to be in a non-casino atmosphere and not right on the strip. After reading some of the negative reviews, I was a little concerned about what I'd find upon arrival. My room was a studio suite on the 36th floor and happened to be a nice view of the strip and mountains to the east. The room was plenty big for one person. The bathroom was immaculate, although I'd have to say the lighting was poor. It was hard to see to shave even with the lighted magnified mirror. The only other negative aspects about the place were that some of the furniture was a little worn, which was no problem and there was thick dust on the shelf of at least one of the closets. The wood part of the floor could stand to be refinished. Also, the feather pillows had an unpleasant odor. At first, I was afraid this might be body odor, but the more I thought about it, I think it was actually the feathers that stunk. It has been many years since I've slept with feather pillows and it might be that they get foul with age. I did not bother to complain because I could position myself to not pick up on the odor. The more I think about it, I probably should have requested new pillows. The room was quiet at night which is what is very important to me in order to sleep. I tried to relax in the mornings at the pool area. The second day the weather was bad so that put an end to that. The third and last day there were shards of glass found around the pool so the decision was made to drain the pool, sweep or vacuum it out and refill. This would be at least a 36-hour project, so there went that relaxing morning. You could get in the hot tub, but I didn't want to do that in the middle of the desert!! I did not rent a car. The company that I booked the trip with sold me a roundtrip shuttle ticket from the airport to the hotel. You can go to The Palms and catch their shuttle to the strip which leaves every half hour between 11 AM -8 PM. They drop you off at the Forum Shops at Caesars. I would catch the city bus at night on Flamingo between Caesars and Bellagio to return to The Palms. I'm sure you could do the reverse route if you wanted to go to the strip before 11:00 AM. You will encounter the casinos and smoke when you go over to The Palms. Most of the eating places near Palms Place are actually at The Palms. I ate breakfast over there every morning and would sometimes get a late night snack. You have a covered area between the towers where part of the walkway has moving sidewalks, but not all of it. Walking does not bother me. I would recommend Palms Place, especially if you want to get away from the casino atmosphere for the most part and the madness of the strip.

reviews.title: I loved my king suite!
reviews.text: Not sure why there is such a mixed bag of reviews on the Palms Place but for my 1 night stay it was awesome! I walked into my room & was floored by the huge bed, sunken jetted tub & shower that had a rain shower head as well as a regular one... Kitchen was great, it was more of a time share type of room with a stove, and dishwasher along with a toaster/microwave and coffee coffee maker. Had a large king bed & sleeper couch, 2 flat screen TVs and a big desk area along with lots of closet space. Had a nice balcony but it just overlooked the parking garage. This place has a walkway to the Palms Casino for any gambling... I also went to their theater to catch an afternoon movie, very comfy. They have an IMAX theater but my movie was y showing in there. Lots of choices to eat at their "food court" and several different restaurants to choose from on the property. They have a spa & pool although I didn't use them I could see them from the pool area. Pool has cabanas you can use too... I would recommend this place and will try to come back for a longer stay to try out all the amenities.

reviews.title: Never again
reviews.text: Was recommended to try palms place for our stay in Vegas. We spent the money and booked a one bedroom suite for a 7 night stay - our stay lasted less than 24 hours. Checked in and immediately noticed the suite had an unpleasant odour. Before making a call we had knocks on our door on 2 occasions offering a deodorizer due to complaints about an odour (1st alarm bell went off realizing this wasn't just us being picky). After 2 hours and a 14 hour flight no improvement. Call made to the front desk and suspicions were confirmed when we were asked if it was a sewage smell - rather than being offered an alternative maintenance was sent up to pour something down the drains.  Went for dinner and returned back to the odour worse than when we left. A call to the front desk and we asked to be moved - we were told to hang tight and expect a call back immediately. 30 minutes later and being put through to 3 different people at 10.30pm we were told that we could move to one room for the night and would have to again be moved after the first night or stay until another suite became available - during this unhelpful phone call I was able to book a similar room in a much better hotel on the strip. Due to the complete lack of customer service we advised we were leaving and that someone from the bell desk would be up to assist. Another 30 minutes and phone call later someone finally came to the door. The bell hop was lovely and complained about the smell the minute he walked in and asked why we weren't offered another room after our first complaint - completely understood that there was no way my husband, son and I should have to tolerate the odour. Prior to leaving we were advised that a refund would be made for pre payments that had been made. One week later after checking the credit card statement I was quite shocked to see that we hadn't need refunded but charged again for another night and a resort fee. Several phone calls later and having to explain the situation this was eventually rectified. Am pleased to say that despite the rocky start we thoroughly enjoyed the rest of our stay in Vegas at our usual hotel on the strip. As for palms place - it will always be known by the name given to it by my son "the stinky palms" It's a shame as a frequent traveller to Vegas had the experience been better we would have returned once a year. Unfortunately for an establishment that is supposed to pride itself on it service and presentation our experience was quite the opposite.

reviews.title: I wouldn't recommend it to my friends
reviews.text: We were disappointed with our suite as it was very dirty (dusty furniture and the floor, dirty windows, dirty mirrors and walls in the bathroom), some of the lamps didn't work. Pool area wasn't clean either. Though the management tried to solve these problems for us, we wouldn't stay at this hotel again. Besides, you have to pay for the internet and amenities when checking out, even if you don't use them..As for the good points, it is quiet, you can relax at the spa salon and the pool. The pool area could be much better though. We liked the dining places and bars in the neighbor Palms Casino Resort. I should also mention that the buffet was good and it's staff was super friendly and helpful.Overall, it's ok, but not 4,5*.

reviews.title: Great Experience
reviews.text: We got a studio suite. We spent a day at the pool, the staff there was wonderful with great poolside food and of course drinks. All the hotel staff as well as casino staff that we encountered was great. The housekeeping was wonderful, always managed to get to our room no matter how late we slept in or any odd hours we kept. Off the strip, if thats a factor for you.

reviews.title: Lovely Suite but lacks amenities and service
reviews.text: Stayed here recently and the suite was phenomenal, however, this didn't seem quite like a hotel but more of an apartment. Housekeeping was wonderful to interact with but when it came to the front desk staff or the concierge, it truly lacked any feeling of staying in a hotel. The front desk couldn't recommend a place that would deliver dinner, any restaurants were a good 10 minute walk through the casino and once there limited in food.  Tried to order a plain grilled cheese at a place in the casino, however, no one would take my order. It's pretty bad when the front desk recommends papa john's as a pizza place. The location is a bit away from everything and was around a $15 cab ride to anywhere down the strip.

reviews.title: Nice Modern Place!
reviews.text: Very large and comfortable suite, loved the idea of having a kitchenette! Clean, modern and with class. The only thing I'd ask from them is to keep the pool hours of operation longer as it closes super early at 6 pm. The rest was great!

reviews.title: Better every visit
reviews.text: I have stayed here 3/4 times in the past year. can't say enough great things about the property. rooms are Huge and beautiful. If you appreciate a beautiful room and bathroom. This is the place. Pool scene is relaxed and chill. Casino is a short walk over . Food on fl 6 is epic ( burgers are choice). Helpful staff. Easy parking.  It's my favorite suite hotel so far.

reviews.title: Past reviews are true, slowly going down
reviews.text: All the recent past reviews are pretty spot on when it comes to this place declining slowly. The rooms are OK and getting to be very dated. It's all the little things that are not being maintained. Rusted, grimy shower head, dated IPad radio port, non fictional balconies and stains on the furniture. If you find a good deal online for this place, book it, but if there's anything on the step around the same price range, look elsewhere.

reviews.title: What a ghetto pool area....
reviews.text: Was here at the end of August 2015. The pool area is terrible. If you want run down cabanas with missing seat cushions that look like they haven't been cleaned in a year, pool lounge chairs with disgusting stains and cigarette burns then stay here.....very very disappointing. I will not be back.

reviews.title: Nice amenities, poor management
reviews.text: The room was fabulous and the amenities were amazing; however, our trip took a turn for the worse when we went to bed and it smelled like a farm.  Turns out they were new feather pillows and the hotel hadn't taken the time to air them out before putting them on a bed.  The smell was so bad that my hair even retained the smell after a shower.  We soon found more issues when room service calls were not completed.  One request took 5 attempts and 2 days to complete.  (we just asked for a frying pan for the kitchen in our suite).  Another issue is that the wifi never worked in the room. But the absolute worst thing that happened was on the day we checked out, we were told that we could still use the spa after checkout (same day).  So we checked out early and headed to the spa; however, when we got there they told us that because we checked out we were not able to use the facilities.  We had specifically asked before we checked out and were very disappointed by the whole thing.  Overall, I would not recommend.

reviews.title: Seen Better Days
reviews.text: It's sad to see how this hotel is not being maintained like it used to. New owners took over the hotel and letting it get run down. Rooms are ok but furniture is showing wear and tear and the hotel is not what it once was. Pool is nice but chair cushions are stained and need to be replaced and cabanas look they need an overhaul. You can get good rates on rooms and it is a quiet hotel

reviews.title: Very disappointed!
reviews.text: Wow, Harrahs took this place over a few years ago and has let it go. This use to be my "go to place" but not anymore. I love the location, room/balcony views and pool area. But i have noticed over the past three years that no money is being invested in this place and the condition of the rooms i have stayed in are dilapidated. I think they are waiting for the next investor to come along and re-do everything.The pics being shown on Yelp appear to be 3-7 years old. My suite has dirty/stained couches and draperies, no utensils or serving wear in the kitchen, a 7-8 year old coffee pot, chipped and dirty walls, doors and paint, outdated furnishings and decorations. The hotel itself has dirty carpets and the pool lounges cushions are gross; stained, weathered and many cigarette hotels. I feel sorry for the staff, mainly the housekeepers, who probably hear the majority of the complaints and the desk staff, who have no control over the management who probably dont care. Sad for me, going to try a hotel on the strip next, will let everyone know what I find.And Simons restaurant is now a cafe that does not serve breakfast and has limited hours.

reviews.title: Sadly Steadily Declining
reviews.text: I have stayed here several times  I really enjoyed previous stays, but I have noticed that the decor and service has slipped a little with each visit.  This last visit however it was definitely noticeable.  The wifi, included in the resort fee, is always a challenge.  It is difficult to sign in and keeps expiring at odd times.  In the room i had the furniture was dated and worn,  Even a cigarette burn in the leather chair.  How you you get a cigarette burn in a non-smoking hotel?  The shower controls only allowed for one temperature of water.  Probably the most irritating thing was the lack of service from housekeeping.  On my second day there I left my room and was gone all day.  I had turned on the housekeeping light and yet when I returned that night my room had not been touched nor was any effort made to do so.  I will have to think long and hard before I return.

reviews.title: Past its prime?
reviews.text: I did not have a enjoyable experience when i visited the hotel.I have been to Vegas countless times and i have allways wanted to stay at this hotel.The checiking in process went smooth enough. But from the start i reacted to the LONG waiting time to get an elevator. The room we had was nice and had a decent view (if you look away from the parkingfacility two floors down). But the room itself was not cleaned properly. Leftover clothes from the previous visitors. The shower was just plain dirty and the floor in the living room had several nail clippings from the previous guests. I called downstairs and asked if they could offer me an upgrade. Instead of asking why i wanted to change rooms the guy answering plainly said "where fully booked" and gave me the impression that he wanted to hang up.We then ordered in room dining which arrives in a brown paper bag. That does not give the luxury feeling that the resort wants you to have. The order was wrong and we had to wait an additional 15mins for the rest of our food.I the decided that i would change hotels. I called downstairs and asked if i could cancel the rest of my stay. "call expedia" was the short response i got (i had booked via hotels.com). He hung up on me without saying goodbye in a proper way. I cancelled my reservation and left for another resort.When i got back home i sent an email woicing my concerns and my dissatisfaction. It has now been three weeks and no reply.A disapointng stay.

reviews.title: Upscale modern,great value (but a long walk from the Strip)
reviews.text: The good: we had a nice view of the Strip from our room.  Room was upscale modern, very spacious.  Weird little kitchen area.   Fancy bathroom fixtures.  Very clean.  Front desk service was warm and personal.   The meh: your parking options are valet (and a long wait to pick your car up), or a seriously long walk to the Palms casino parking garage.  It is also a long and not very pedestrian-friendly walk to the Strip.Great value for the money at the rate we got.

reviews.title: No longer a loyal customer
reviews.text: Around 2 years ago, when I first stayed at the Palms Place, it was great. I liked its location and modern design.I've been back several times after that and without fail, each experience has been worse than the last.There is always something that does not work. Some pieces of furniture (bedside lamp, desk lamp, even a coffee table) will just be missing sometimes. Several light fixtures will not work, some of the already few outlets don't work, forcing me to connect my devices in awkward locations.During my last stay, I noticed several things in the room either be missing or broken. (missing bedside lamp, desk lamp, and some of the few lamps that were there did not work. make-up mirror did not work.)I was fine with it. I knew that's how Palms Place is now, and I booked anyway. (though I do always hope.)But the bathtub did not work. No water at all. I called about it, they sent up a guy quick enough. He quickly diagnosed the problem as something that can't be fixed easily and offered me room change. Fine. Now how I wanted to spend the night, but I do want a working bathtub for the remaining three nights.I pack all my stuff back up. Later, another guy came up to give me keys to my new room.I grab all my stuff and went to my new room. The room had other peoples' stuff in it. The room was occupied! I was given KEYS TO A PREOCCUPIED ROOM. That is scary for me, and even scarier for those people.Unbelievable. I went back down to my old room, put my stuff down and went to the front desk.
